paras.t: Et ego in infirmitate, id est in infirmitatis similitudine, qua factus sum infirmis infirmus, proportionando fortitudinem perfectionis meæ capacitati eorum, et conformando me vobis, quantum fieri potuit; et timore cordis, non propter mala mihi imminentia (non enim timui eos qui corpus occidunt, nec timui Deum offendere mortaliter, sciens me confirmatum in bono), sed propter pericula imminentia vobis nondum perfectis: timui enim ne a diabolo, mundo et propriis concupiscentiis falleremini; et tremore multo corporis, procedente ex timore mentis (in tantum enim timui corde, ut passio timoris redundaret in membris, et faceret ea tremere); fui apud vos.
paras.en: [[2:3|And I|Et ego]] [[2:3|in weakness|in infirmitate]], that is, in the semblance of weakness, by which I [[1 Cor 9:22|became weak|factus sum infirmis infirmus]] to the weak, proportioning the strength of my perfection to their capacity, and conforming myself to you as far as could be; [[2:3|and in fear|et timore]] of heart, not because of evils hanging over me (for I did not fear [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body|eos qui corpus occidunt]], nor did I fear to offend God mortally, knowing myself confirmed in good [that is, confirmed in grace, so as not to fall into mortal sin]), but because of the dangers hanging over you, who were not yet perfect: for I feared lest you should be deceived by the devil, the world and your own concupiscences; [[2:3|and in much trembling|et tremore multo]] of body, proceeding from the fear of the mind (for I feared so much in heart that the passion of fear overflowed into my limbs and made them tremble); [[2:3|I was with you|fui apud vos]].

paras.t: Et sermo meus factus quibusdam seorsum, et prædicatio mea omnibus vobis palam proposita, non fuit in persuasibilibus humanæ sapientiæ verbis, id est non in argumentatione dialectica verborum decore ornata, seu persuasione humana, quasi per talia principaliter vellem vos ad credendum inducere, seu fidem probare; sed fuit in ostensione spiritus, id est in manifestatione operum Spiritus Sancti, et declaratione virtutis miraculorum. Hoc dicit, vel quia credentes per prædicationem ipsius receperunt Spiritum Sanctum in signo sensibili, sicut in primitiva Ecclesia sæpe fiebat; vel, quia Spiritus Sanctus per gratiam specialem atque miracula ostendit prædicationem Pauli esse salubrem, et fidem catholicam roboravit.
paras.en: [[2:4|And my speech|Et sermo meus]], addressed to some apart, [[2:4|and my preaching|et prædicatio mea]], set forth openly to you all, [[2:4|was not in the persuasive words of human wisdom|non fuit in persuasibilibus humanæ sapientiæ verbis]], that is, not in dialectical argument adorned with elegance of words, or in human persuasion, as though by such things I chiefly wished to lead you to believe, or to prove the faith; [[2:4|but in shewing of the Spirit|sed fuit in ostensione spiritus]], that is, in the manifestation of the works of the Holy Ghost, [[2:4|and|et]] in the declaration of the [[2:4|power|virtutis]] of miracles. He says this either because those who believed through his preaching received the Holy Ghost in a sensible sign, as often happened in the primitive Church[[Acts 2:4||]][[Acts 10:44||]] [the margin gives Acts ii, 1–4; x, 31; x, 44, etc.; x, 31 does not fit]; or because the Holy Ghost, by special grace and by miracles, showed the preaching of Paul to be wholesome, and strengthened the Catholic faith.

paras.t: Ideo subditur: ut fides vestra non sit in sapientia hominum, id est, non innitatur humanæ rationi, nec putetur ab hominibus excogitata et ficta. Errant ergo qui fidem naturalibus rationibus demonstrari posse affirmant. Sed in virtute Dei, id est, divina potestate stabiliatur per certa miracula, sicque æternæ veritati innitatur ut fundamento.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[2:5|That your faith might not stand on the wisdom of men|ut fides vestra non sit in sapientia hominum]], that is, that it might not rest on human reason, nor be thought to have been devised and invented by men. They err, then, who affirm that the faith can be demonstrated by natural reasons. [[2:5|but on the power of God|Sed in virtute Dei]], that is, that it might be established by the divine power through sure miracles, and so rest on the eternal truth as on a foundation.

paras.t: Sapientiam autem, id est cognitionem sublimem rerum divinarum, profunda mysteria fidei, et ea quæ Christi divinitatem concernunt: quam sapientiam inter vos loqui non possumus, propter imperfectionem et incapacitatem vestram; loquimur inter perfectos, id est inter sapientes, per modum collationis; vel, Inter perfectos seu capaces auditor[…] modum instructionis. Perfectorum […]que est solidus cibus. Sapientiam non hujus sæculi, id est non […]rem sapientiam humana ratione sub[…] neque principum hujus sæculi, […] nec sapientiam fallacem a dæmone […]quisitam, vel a philosophis seu t[…] principibus traditam, loquimur: q[…] […]cipes destruuntur, id est, cum om[…] sapientia pereunt et damnantur.
paras.en: [[2:6|Howbeit we speak wisdom|Sapientiam autem]], that is, the sublime knowledge of divine things, the deep mysteries of the faith, and the things that concern the Godhead of Christ: which wisdom we cannot speak among you, because of your imperfection and incapacity; we speak it [[2:6|among the perfect|inter perfectos]], that is, among the wise, by way of conference [*collatio*: a discussion held together, as among equals]; or, [[2:6|among the perfect|Inter perfectos]], or capable hearer[…] […] the manner of instruction. […] [[Heb 5:14|strong meat is for the perfect|est solidus cibus]]. [[2:6|yet not the wisdom of this world|Sapientiam non hujus sæculi]], that is, not […] wisdom […] by human reason […] [[2:6|neither of the princes of this world|neque principum hujus sæculi]] […], nor the deceitful wisdom […] from the demon, or handed down by the philosophers or t[…] princes, do we speak: […] princes [[2:6|that come to nought|destruuntur]], that is, perish and are damned with […] wisdom[[Bar 3:19||]].

paras.t: Sed loquimur, id est prædicam[…] sapientiam, id est Christum, qui e[…] tus et sapientia Patris, in mysti[…] est in sacro secreto seu sacrame[…] carnationis, docendo hanc sapienti[…] effabiliter incarnatam, juxta illud, V[…] caro factum est; vel, In mysterio, […] explanando mysteria ejus, quibus i[…] ri Testamento præsignata est. Vel, […] mur eam in mysterio, id est sub q[…] occulto velamine: nunc enim v[…] per speculum in ænigmate. Quæ […] dita est, id est ignota filiis hujus […] Vel hoc ideo dicitur, quia perfect[…] prehendi non potest. Quam præd[…] vit, id est, ordinavit ac præparavit […] Pater ante sæcula, id est ab æter[…] gloriam nostram, id est ad hoc, […] eam consequamur vitam gloriosam […]titudinemque æternam. Ideo enim […] vit eam incarnari, ut glorificem[…] ipsum. Unde in Proverbiis ait h[…] pientia: Ab æterno ordinata sum […] antiquis, antequam terra fieret. Di[…] eam Pater ut ipsa sit objectum h[…] dinis nostræ, et ita præparavit ea[…] bis, quibus et se ipsum præpara[…] eum feliciter possideamus.
paras.en: [[2:7|But we speak|Sed loquimur]], that is, we preach […] [[2:7|wisdom|sapientiam]], that is, Christ, who […] and the wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]], [[2:7|in a mystery|in mysti]][…] […], that is, in a sacred secret, or sacra[…] […]carnation, teaching that this wisdom […] […]effably incarnate, according to that saying: […] [[John 1:14|was made flesh|caro factum est]]; or, [[2:7|in a mystery|In mysterio]], […] explaining its mysteries, by which i[…] […] Testament it was foreshadowed. Or, […] it [[2:7|in a mystery|in mysterio]], that is, under […] hidden veil: for now […] [[1 Cor 13:12|through a glass in a dark manner|per speculum in ænigmate]]. [[2:7|which is hidden|Quæ]] […], that is, unknown to the children of this […] Or this is said because perfect[…] […] it cannot be […]prehended. [[2:7|which God ordained|Quam]] […], that is, which the Father ordained and prepared […] [[2:7|before the world|ante sæcula]], that is, from eter[…] […] [[2:7|unto our glory|gloriam nostram]], that is, to this end, […] that we may attain a glorious life […] and eternal […]titude. For to this end […] that it be made incarnate, that […] glorif[…] […] him. Hence in Proverbs […] wisdom says: [[Prov 8:23|I was set up from eternity|Ab æterno ordinata sum]] […] [[Prov 8:23|of old, before the earth was made|antiquis, antequam terra fieret]]. The Father […] it, that it might be the object of our […] […], and so prepared it […] […], for whom he also prepared himself, […] that we may happily possess him.

paras.t: Quæ sapientiam æternam et i[…] tam, nemo, id est nullus, principi[…] jus sæculi, id est dæmonum vel […] perfectum seu philosophorum […] cognitione certa ac stabili. Quomo[…] tem principes et dæmones cogn[…] Christum in mundo conversantem […] nedo non in expectatione epistolæ […] […] tractatum est: idcirco nunc transeo.
paras.en: [[2:8|Which|Quæ]], the eternal and i[…] wisdom, [[2:8|none|nemo]], that is, no one, [[2:8|of the princes|principi]][…] [[2:8|of this world|jus sæculi]], that is, of the demons or […] perfect, or of the philosophers […] with certain and stable knowledge. How […] the princes and the demons kne[…] Christ while he lived in the world […] not in the expectation of the epistle […] […] has been treated: therefore I pass over it now.

paras.t: Sed videtur, quod istud non possit exponi de principibus seu legisperitis Judæorum: de illis quippe scriptum est, Ex principibus multi crediderunt in eum. Et respondendum, quod licet multi eorum crediderint, tamen comparatione incredulorum paucissimi erant. Potest etiam dici, quod non permanserunt stabiles in credendo, maxime tempore passionis. Si enim cognovissent principes isti Christum cognitione certa, nunquam Dominum gloriæ, id est Christum, Deum verum, et Dominum majestatis, crucifixissent. Si enim dæmones cognovissent, certe nequaquam suggessissent ad mortem illius, a quo moriente noverunt se vincendos ac spoliandos. Similiter, si principes Judæorum cognovissent, non procurassent a Pilato mortem Christi. Per hoc autem quod Christus vocatur hic Dominus gloriæ, manifeste probatur quod sit verus Deus, quoniam nulla creatura pura habet dominium gloriæ, sed solam participationem subjectam.
paras.en: But it seems that this cannot be explained of the princes or doctors of the law of the Jews: for of them it is written, [[John 12:42|many of the chief men also believed in him|Ex principibus multi crediderunt in eum]]. And the answer must be that, although many of them believed, yet in comparison with the unbelievers they were very few. It can also be said that they did not remain steadfast in believing, above all at the time of the passion. [[2:8|For if they had known it|Si enim cognovissent]], that is, if these princes had known Christ with certain knowledge, [[2:8|they would never|nunquam]] [[2:8|have crucified|crucifixissent]] [[2:8|the Lord of glory|Dominum gloriæ]], that is, Christ, true God, and Lord of majesty. For if the demons had known, they would surely never have prompted the death of him by whose death they knew they would be vanquished and despoiled. Likewise, if the princes of the Jews had known, they would not have procured the death of Christ from Pilate. And by this, that Christ is here called the Lord of glory, it is plainly proved that he is true God, since no mere creature has lordship over glory, but only a subject share in it.

paras.t: Quod vero ista sapientia nobis ab æterno parata, sit abscondita, et principibus hujus mundi ignota, probat Apostolus auctoritate Scripturæ. Sed sicut scriptum est per Prophetam: Quod oculus corporalis, imo et spiritualis, non vidit, id est, perfecte non cognovit, nec auris, scilicet corporalis seu spiritualis, audivit ab homine puro, nec in cor hominis ascendit, id est, a corde humano cogitari seu concipi nequit, imo nec ab affectu hominis capi potest, quæ præparavit Deus his qui diligunt illum, id est præmium illud æternum amatoribus Dei paratum, videlicet sapientiam increatam, Divinitatis fruitionem, et cetera bona electis præparata: quæ utique nec oculus corporalis, nec auditus hominis, immediate capere possunt, nec aliquo modo sciuntur nisi per revelationem divinam.
paras.en: That this wisdom, prepared for us from eternity, is hidden and unknown to the princes of this world, the Apostle proves by the authority of Scripture: [[2:9|But, as it is written|Sed sicut scriptum est]] by the Prophet: [[2:9|That eye|Quod oculus]], bodily, nay, and spiritual, [[2:9|hath not seen|non vidit]], that is, hath not perfectly known, [[2:9|nor ear|nec auris]], namely bodily or spiritual, [[2:9|heard|audivit]], that is, the ear of a mere man, [[2:9|neither hath it entered into the heart of man|nec in cor hominis ascendit]], that is, it cannot be thought or conceived by the human heart, nay, nor can it be grasped by the affection of man, [[2:9|what things God hath prepared for them that love him|quæ præparavit Deus his qui diligunt illum]], that is, that eternal reward prepared for the lovers of God, namely the uncreated wisdom, the fruition of the Godhead, and the other good things prepared for the elect: which neither the bodily eye nor the hearing of man can grasp immediately, nor are they known in any way except by divine revelation.

paras.t: Ideo subditur: Nobis autem revelavit Deus per Spiritum suum, id est per Spiritum Sanctum, qui […] corda nostra omni sapientia copiose perfudit. Possit enim aliquis dicere Paulo: Si bona ista sunt invisibilia, inaudibilia et inexcogitabilia, quomodo tu nosti ea? Et respondet Apostolus, quod non per se ipsum, neque perfecte per speciem noscit jam ea, sed per illuminationem Spiritus Sancti, in fide seu per speculum in ænigmate.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[2:10|But to us God hath revealed them by his Spirit|Nobis autem revelavit Deus per Spiritum suum]], that is, by the Holy Ghost, who […] has copiously filled our hearts with all wisdom. For someone might say to Paul: If these good things are invisible, inaudible and beyond all thought, how dost thou know them? And the Apostle answers that he knows them now not of himself, nor perfectly by sight [*per speciem*: by clear vision, as the blessed see, in contrast to faith], but by the illumination of the Holy Ghost, in faith, or [[1 Cor 13:12|through a glass in a dark manner|per speculum in ænigmate]].

paras.t: Sciendum quoque, quod Apostolus hoc loco magis allegat sensum quam verba Isaiæ. Sic enim ibi scriptum est: Oculus non vidit, Deus, absque te, quæ præparasti exspectantibus te. Nec potest dici, quod Apostolus alleget scripturam hanc secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum. Illa namque non habet scripturam hanc, sicut Hieronymus sæpe testatur.
paras.en: It should also be known that in this place the Apostle cites the sense rather than the words of Isaias. For there it is written thus: [[Is 64:4|the eye hath not seen, O God, besides thee, what things thou hast prepared for them that wait for thee|Oculus non vidit, Deus, absque te, quæ præparasti exspectantibus te]]. Nor can it be said that the Apostle cites this scripture according to the translation of the Seventy interpreters; for that translation does not have this scripture, as Jerome often testifies.

paras.t: Quod autem Spiritus Sanctus potuit nobis ista revelare, patet per hoc: Spiritus enim omnia scrutatur, id est, Spiritus Sanctus universa cognoscit, non solum creata, sed etiam profunda Dei, id est divina secreta, seu incomprehensibilia quæ soli Deo sunt cognita, videlicet divinam essentiam, divinam sapientiam, et quidquid in Deo est. Et hoc probat Apostolus per simile.
paras.en: That the Holy Ghost could reveal these things to us is plain from this: [[2:10|For the Spirit searcheth all things|Spiritus enim omnia scrutatur]], that is, the Holy Ghost knows all things, not only created things, but [[2:10|yea, the deep things of God|etiam profunda Dei]], that is, the divine secrets, or the incomprehensible things known to God alone, namely the divine essence, the divine wisdom, and whatever is in God. And the Apostle proves this by a comparison.

paras.t: Quis enim scit hominum quæ sunt hominis, nisi spiritus hominis qui in ipso est? id est, sicut nemo scit affectus et cogitationes atque secreta alterius, nisi anima ejus, non alter, nec anima alterius; ita et quæ Dei sunt, id est divina secreta, et quæ in Deo sunt, nemo, id est nullus, cognovit, nisi Spiritus Dei, id est Spiritus Sanctus, et cui ipse revelat. Per hoc non excipitur Filius a cognitione divinorum, sed nec Spiritus Sanctus ab ista cognitione excipitur quum Filius ait: Nemo novit Filium nisi Pater, neque Patrem quis novit nisi Filius, et cui voluerit Filius revelare. Tanta quippe est divinarum Personarum connexio, ut una expressa, alia detur intelligi, nisi in his quæ relative dicuntur.
paras.en: [[2:11|For what man knoweth the things of a man, but the spirit of a man that is in him?|Quis enim scit hominum quæ sunt hominis, nisi spiritus hominis qui in ipso est?]] That is, just as no one knows the affections and thoughts and secrets of another but his own soul, not another man, nor another man's soul; [[2:11|So the things also that are of God|ita et quæ Dei sunt]], that is, the divine secrets and the things that are in God, [[2:11|no man|nemo]], that is, no one, [[2:11|knoweth, but the Spirit of God|cognovit, nisi Spiritus Dei]], that is, the Holy Ghost, and he to whom he reveals them. By this the Son is not excluded from the knowledge of divine things; just as the Holy Ghost is not excluded from that knowledge either when the Son says: [[Matt 11:27|no one knoweth the Son but the Father: neither doth any one know the Father, but the Son, and he to whom it shall please the Son to reveal him|Nemo novit Filium nisi Pater, neque Patrem quis novit nisi Filius, et cui voluerit Filius revelare]]. For so close is the bond of the divine Persons that when one is expressed another is given to be understood, except in those things that are said relatively [that is, what belongs to one Person by his relation to another, as fatherhood to the Father].

paras.t: Ex his verbis Apostoli probatur quod Spiritus Sanctus sit verus Deus, dupliciter: Primo, quoniam perfecte cognoscit divina seu Deum: quod utique nulli creato intellectui convenit; imo in infinitum deficit a plena comprehensione Dei. Secundo, quia Apostolus ponit simile de spiritu hominis, qui ideo noscit quæ hominis sunt, quoniam intimus et consubstantialis est homini. Ergo et Spiritus Dei cognoscens quæ Dei sunt, intimus et consubstantialis est Deo: quod creaturæ non convenit.
paras.en: From these words of the Apostle it is proved in two ways that the Holy Ghost is true God. First, because he knows divine things, or God, perfectly: which belongs to no created intellect; nay, every such intellect falls infinitely short of the full comprehension of God[[Rom 11:33||]][[Rom 11:34||]]. Secondly, because the Apostle gives the comparison of the spirit of a man, which knows the things of a man because it is inmost to the man and consubstantial with him. Therefore the Spirit of God also, knowing the things of God, is inmost to God and consubstantial with him: which does not belong to a creature.

paras.t: Nos autem non spiritum hujus mundi, id est non animum sæcularem, non affectum inflantem, non spiritum pythonicum conjecturaliter divinantem, accepimus, sed Spiritum qui ex Deo est, id est Spiritum Sanctum ex Patre et Filio tanquam ex uno fonte procedentem, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis, id est, beneficia divina cognoscamus, et grati simus, gloriemurque in Domino, non in nobis.
paras.en: [[2:12|Now, we|Nos autem]] [[2:12|have received|accepimus]] [[2:12|not the spirit of this world|non spiritum hujus mundi]], that is, not a worldly mind, not a puffed-up affection, not a pythonic spirit divining by conjecture [that is, a spirit of soothsaying, like the damsel's "pythonical spirit" in Acts 16:16], [[2:12|but the Spirit that is of God|sed Spiritum qui ex Deo est]], that is, the Holy Ghost, proceeding from the Father and the Son as from one source, [[2:12|that we may know the things that are given us from God|ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis]], that is, that we may know the divine benefits, and be grateful, and glory in the Lord, not in ourselves.

paras.t: Utile ergo est ut homo diligenter consideret gratiam et misericordiam Dei sibi concessam, imo universa beneficia Dei, naturalia et supernaturalia, communia et specialia, exhibita et promissa: quatenus ex hoc in Dei amore accendatur, Deo promptius famuletur, gratiasque agendo mereatur non solum conservari in bono, sed quotidie donis amplioribus adimpleri. Habenti enim dabitur, ei vero qui non habet, id est ingrato, et quod videtur habere, auferetur ab eo. Unde Virgo Deifera, hunc Spiritum habens, agnovit quæ a Deo donata fuerant sibi, quum dixit: Beatam me dicent omnes generationes, quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus. Et Psalmista: Benedic, anima mea, Domino, et noli oblivisci omnes retributiones ejus; itemque: Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi?
paras.en: It is profitable, then, that a man should diligently consider the grace and mercy of God granted to him, nay, all the benefits of God, natural and supernatural, common and special, already bestowed and promised: so that from this he may be kindled in the love of God, serve God more readily, and by giving thanks merit not only to be kept in good, but to be filled daily with ampler gifts. [[Matt 25:29|For to every one that hath shall be given|Habenti enim dabitur]]; [[Matt 25:29|but from him that hath not|ei vero qui non habet]], that is, from the ungrateful, [[Matt 25:29|that also which he seemeth to have shall be taken away|et quod videtur habere, auferetur ab eo]]. Hence the God-bearing Virgin [*Deifera*: she who bore God], having this Spirit, acknowledged the things that had been given her by God, when she said: [[Luke 1:48|all generations shall call me blessed|Beatam me dicent omnes generationes]], [[Luke 1:49|Because he that is mighty hath done great things to me: and holy is his name|quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus]]. And the Psalmist: [[Ps 102:2|Bless the Lord, O my soul, and never forget all he hath done for thee|Benedic, anima mea, Domino, et noli oblivisci omnes retributiones ejus]]; and again: [[Ps 115:3|What shall I render to the Lord, for all the things that he hath rendered to me?|Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi?]] [the margin gives Ps. cxv, 12, numbering this psalm's verses on from Ps 114; in the numbering used here it is Ps 115:3]

paras.t: Quæ beneficia nobis a Deo collata, loquimur, id est, aliis enuntiamus, non in doctis humanæ sapientiæ verbis, id est non stilo rhetorico atque pompatico, sed in doctrina Spiritus, id est secundum doctrinam nobis a Spiritu Sancto infusam, loquendo humili simplicique sermone, et vera scientia, spiritualibus auditoribus spiritualia documenta comparantes, id est, proportionaliter dantes seu proponentes, videlicet secundum capacitatem ipsorum. Inter tales enim sapientiam loquimur: quam inter imperfectos non loquimur, quoniam capere nequeunt. Unde subjungitur:
paras.en: [[2:13|Which things|Quæ]], the benefits conferred on us by God, [[2:13|we speak|loquimur]], that is, we declare to others, [[2:13|not in the learned words of human wisdom|non in doctis humanæ sapientiæ verbis]], that is, not in a rhetorical and pompous style, [[2:13|but in the doctrine of the Spirit|sed in doctrina Spiritus]], that is, according to the doctrine infused into us by the Holy Ghost, speaking in humble and simple speech, and with true knowledge, [[2:13|comparing spiritual things with spiritual|spiritualibus auditoribus spiritualia documenta comparantes]], spiritual teachings with spiritual hearers: that is, giving or setting them forth in proportion, namely according to their capacity. For among such we speak wisdom, which we do not speak among the imperfect, since they cannot grasp it. Hence it is added:

paras.t: Animalis autem homo, id est carnalis et vitiosus, cujus affectus et intellectus in sensibilibus detinentur, non percipit ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei, id est spiritualia bona. Sermo enim justitiæ, mysticus intellectus, cetera quoque divina ei non sapiunt, nec delectatur in eis, propter sui interioris gustus infectionem: sicut febricitans non gustat mellis dulcedinem, propter exterioris sui gustus corruptionem. Imo etiam quamvis sit homo in gratia, tamen si nondum profecit in bonis, sed adhuc partim inclinatur ad ista terrena, non sapit quæ Dei sunt. Nam et Petro dixit Salvator: Vade retro me, satana; non sapis quæ Dei sunt, sed quæ hominum. Stultitia enim est illi, id est, prædicta spiritualia et divina videntur homini animali stulta et vana: quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico dicitur, Exsecratio peccatori sapientia; et non potest intelligere per internum saporem ista divina, quamdiu permanet talis, quia spiritualiter examinatur, id est, per spiritualem inquisitionem seu considerationem cognoscitur esse animalis: ideo scitur non posse intelligere illa. Vel, Spiritualiter examinatur, id est, ideo non intelligit hæc, quia spiritualia non nisi spiritualiter discutiuntur.
paras.en: [[2:14|But the sensual man|Animalis autem homo]] [*animalis*: living by the life of the senses, as a mere animal], that is, the carnal and vicious man, whose affection and understanding are held fast in things of sense, [[2:14|perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God|non percipit ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei]], that is, spiritual goods. For the word of justice, the mystical understanding, and the other divine things too have no savour for him [*non sapiunt*: the Latin *sapere* is both "to taste" and "to be wise"], nor does he delight in them, because of the infection of his inward taste: just as one sick of a fever does not taste the sweetness of honey, because of the corruption of his outward taste. Nay, even though a man be in grace, yet if he has not yet advanced in good things, but is still partly inclined to these earthly things, he does not savour the things that are of God. For the Saviour said even to Peter: [[Mark 8:33|Go behind me, Satan|Vade retro me, satana]]; [[Mark 8:33|thou savourest not the things that are of God but that are of men|non sapis quæ Dei sunt, sed quæ hominum]]. [[2:14|For it is foolishness to him|Stultitia enim est illi]], that is, the spiritual and divine things just mentioned seem foolish and vain to the sensual man: as it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 1:26|to sinners wisdom is an abomination|Exsecratio peccatori sapientia]]; [[2:14|and he cannot understand|et non potest intelligere]] these divine things by inward savour, so long as he remains such, [[2:14|because it is spiritually examined|quia spiritualiter examinatur]], that is, by spiritual inquiry or consideration he is known to be sensual: therefore he is known to be unable to understand them. Or, [[2:14|spiritually examined|Spiritualiter examinatur]], that is, he does not understand these things because spiritual things are not weighed except spiritually.

paras.t: Spiritualis autem homo, in quo est Spiritus Dei, judicat, id est, bene discernit, omnia ad salutem pertinentia, vel de singulis talibus verum judicium proferendo, inter bonum et malum, verum et falsum, veraciter distinguendo. Habet enim sanum intellectum et purum affectum: ideo ejus judicium nec errore decipitur, nec passione corrumpitur. Et ipse a nemine judicatur: id est, alius nullus carnalis potest eum reprehendere, vel de ipso recte judicare: non enim intelligit opera ejus.
paras.en: [[2:15|But the spiritual man|Spiritualis autem homo]], in whom is the Spirit of God, [[2:15|judgeth|judicat]], that is, discerns well, [[2:15|all things|omnia]] pertaining to salvation, or, giving a true judgment on each such thing, distinguishing truly between good and evil, true and false. For he has a sound understanding and a pure affection: therefore his judgment is neither deceived by error nor corrupted by passion. [[2:15|and he himself is judged of no man|Et ipse a nemine judicatur]]: that is, no other man who is carnal can reprove him, or judge rightly of him: for he does not understand his works.

paras.t: Nihilo minus videmus quotidie spirituales homines a carnalibus judicari et reprobari; sed hoc est judicium usurpatorium et falsum. Interdum etiam carnales de spiritualibus judicant, approbando vitam eorum; sed est judicium imperfectum, ex levitate procedens.
paras.en: Nevertheless we see every day spiritual men judged and condemned by carnal men; but this is a usurped and false judgment. Sometimes too the carnal judge of the spiritual by approving their life; but it is an imperfect judgment, proceeding from levity.

paras.t: Sed advertendum, quod sicut ex verbis principis theologorum, capitulo 2 de Divinis nominibus, elicitur, dupliciter judicat homo de aliqua re: Primo, per solam cognitionem informem et nudam, quemadmodum habens moralem scientiam, judicat de virtutibus quas non habet: et istud est imperfectum judicium. Sic enim homo carnalis, tamen ingeniosus et eruditus, de rebus spiritualibus judicat, sermocinatur et dictat. Secundo, judicat homo de rebus per connaturalitatem seu conformitatem sui affectus ad eas, ut castus de his quæ castitatem respiciunt. Unde de virtutibus hoc modo judicare non potest nisi virtuosus. Et ita de spiritualibus bonis et rebus divinis ad fidem pertinentibus, judicat homo per sapientiam, quæ est donum Spiritus Sancti, et consistit in sapido quodam gustu spiritualium de quibus judicium profert, nec habetur sine gratia gratum faciente. Propter quod scriptum est: In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia. Ex quibus elucescit, quod non nisi spiritualis homo percipit, gustat, vereque judicat ea quæ Dei sunt, per donum sapientiæ: per quod etiam de aliis inferioribus rebus judicat secundum rationes divinas.
paras.en: But it must be noted that, as is drawn from the words of the prince of theologians in the second chapter of *On the Divine Names* [that is, Dionysius the Areopagite; the margin gives "Art. xii de Div. Nom.", apparently Denis's own commentary on that work], a man judges of a thing in two ways. First, by bare and unformed knowledge alone, as one who has moral science judges of virtues that he does not have: and this is an imperfect judgment. For in this way a carnal man, if he is clever and learned, judges, discourses and writes about spiritual things. Secondly, a man judges of things by connaturality, or by the conformity of his affection to them, as the chaste man judges of what concerns chastity. Hence none but the virtuous can judge of the virtues in this way. And so a man judges of spiritual goods and of divine things pertaining to the faith by wisdom, which is a gift of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]], and consists in a certain savoury taste of the spiritual things on which it gives judgment [*sapientia*, wisdom, and *sapidus*, savoury, come from the same root, *sapere*, to taste], and it is not had without sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*: the grace that makes a man pleasing to God]. For which reason it is written: [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia]]. From this it is clear that none but the spiritual man perceives, tastes and truly judges the things that are of God, by the gift of wisdom: by which he also judges of other, lower things according to divine reasons.

paras.t: Quod autem carnalis homo non intelligat quæ Dei sunt, probat Apostolus auctoritate Scripturæ: Quis enim cognovit sensum Domini, id est judicium seu censuram mentis divinæ de rebus, aut quis instruxit eum? Nullus utique. Hoc scriptum est in Isaia, et allegatum est ab Apostolo ad Romanos, ubi et plenius expositum est. Tantum autem vult Apostolus dicere, quod de divinis et spiritualibus rebus nullus veraciter judicat, nec eas intelligit, nisi qui habet sensum Domini. Animalis vero homo non habet sensum Domini, sed spiritualis. Ideo subditur: Nos autem sensum Christi habemus, id est intellectum a Christo illuminatum, ejusque sensui conformatum: ideo cognoscimus, approbamus, et sapimus ea quæ Dei sunt, sicut et Christus. Habemus enim sensum Domini, sicut eruditi discipuli habere dicuntur sensum sui magistri.
paras.en: That the carnal man does not understand the things of God, the Apostle proves by the authority of Scripture: [[2:16|For who hath known the mind of the Lord|Quis enim cognovit sensum Domini]], that is, the judgment or verdict of the divine mind concerning things, [[2:16|that he may instruct him|aut quis instruxit eum?]] [Denis reads *aut quis instruxit eum?*, "or who hath instructed him?", where the Vulgate has *qui instruat eum*] No one, surely. This is written in Isaias, and cited by the Apostle in Romans, where it is also explained more fully [Is 40:13 and Rom 11:34]. But the Apostle means only to say that no one truly judges of divine and spiritual things, or understands them, except one who has the mind of the Lord. Now the sensual man does not have the mind of the Lord, but the spiritual man does. Therefore it is added: [[2:16|But we have the mind of Christ|Nos autem sensum Christi habemus]], that is, an understanding enlightened by Christ and conformed to his mind [*sensus*: "mind", also "sense" or "understanding"]: therefore we know, approve and savour the things that are of God, as Christ also does. For we have the mind of the Lord, as learned disciples are said to have the mind of their master.

3.title: Elucidatio capituli tertii: Et ego, fratres, non potui vobis loqui
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: And I, brethren, could not speak to you

paras.t: Adhuc autem Apostolus clarius prosequitur imperfectionem Corinthiorum, et causam contentionis eorum aufert ; et ait : Et ego, fratres, non potui vobis loqui quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnalibus : id est, alta mysteria fidei et sublimia de divinitate Christi, perfecta quoque internæ perfectionis exercitia, non potui vobis proponere, sed parva et rudia atque humilia de Christi humanitate vobis proposui, non judicans me aliquid scire inter vos, nisi Jesum, et hunc crucifixum. Tanquam parvulis, id est imperfectis, in Christo, lac, id est facilem doctrinam et teneram instructionem, vobis potum dedi, id est, tali doctrina spiritualiter vos potavi, et animas vestras rigavi, non escam, id est, non solidum cibum, non profundam sapientiam, non sublimem vitæ perfectionem vobis tradere potui. Nondum enim poteratis spiritualiter capere talia ; sed nec nunc quidem potestis : adhuc enim carnales estis, id est carnalibus vitiis subjacentes. Quum enim sit inter vos zelus, id est invidia latens, et contentio, id est lis verborum inde procedens, nonne carnales estis (pro eodem sumit Apostolus carnalem et animalem), et secundum hominem ambulatis, id est, secundum humanam fragilitatem, imperfectionem et ignorantiam vivitis et sentitis? Quum enim quis, id est aliquis vestrum, dicat, Ego quidem sum Pauli, alius autem, Ego Apollo, id est, unus dicit se baptizatum a Paulo, alius ab Apolline, et idcirco unus se alteri præfert, nonne homines estis? id est, vitia hominibus consueta sectamini, et non estis divini, sed homines nudi, humanum sensum sequentes, non Spiritus Sancti instinctum.
paras.en: The Apostle goes on still more plainly about the imperfection of the Corinthians, and takes away the cause of their contention; and he says: [[3:1|And I, brethren, could not speak to you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal|Et ego, fratres, non potui vobis loqui quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnalibus]]: that is, I could not set before you the high mysteries of the faith and sublime things about the divinity of Christ, nor the perfect exercises of inward perfection, but I set before you small, simple and lowly things about the humanity of Christ, [[1 Cor 2:2|For I judged not myself to know anything among you, but Jesus Christ: and him crucified|non judicans me aliquid scire inter vos, nisi Jesum, et hunc crucifixum]]. [[3:1|As unto little ones|Tanquam parvulis]], that is, the imperfect, [[3:1|in Christ|in Christo]], [[3:2|I gave you milk to drink|lac vobis potum dedi]]: milk, that is, easy teaching and tender instruction; I gave you to drink, that is, I gave you such teaching to drink spiritually and watered your souls; [[3:2|not meat|non escam]], that is, I could not give you solid food[[Heb 5:14||]], deep wisdom, sublime perfection of life. [[3:2|for you were not able as yet|Nondum enim poteratis]] to take such things in spiritually; [[3:2|But neither indeed are you now able: for you are yet carnal|sed nec nunc quidem potestis : adhuc enim carnales estis]], that is, subject to carnal vices. [[3:3|For, whereas there is among you envying|Quum enim sit inter vos zelus]], that is, hidden envy, [[3:3|and contention|et contentio]], that is, the quarrel of words that comes from it, [[3:3|are you not carnal|nonne carnales estis]] (the Apostle takes "carnal" and "animal" for the same), [[3:3|and walk you not according to man|et secundum hominem ambulatis]], that is, live and think according to human frailty, imperfection and ignorance? [[3:4|For while one saith: I indeed am of Paul: and another: I am of Apollo|Quum enim quis, id est aliquis vestrum, dicat, Ego quidem sum Pauli, alius autem, Ego Apollo]]: that is, one says he was baptized by Paul, another by Apollo, and so one sets himself above the other: [[3:4|are you not men|nonne homines estis]]? that is, you follow the vices usual among men, and are not divine but mere men, following human sense, not the prompting of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Ex prædictis constat, quod prædicator seu doctor moderari debet sensum et stilum doctrinæ suæ, secundum audientium capacitatem. — Sciendum quoque, quod nomine lactis in Scriptura interdum signatur carnalis voluptas, ut ibi : Quem docebit Dominus scientiam? et quem intelligere faciet auditum? Et respondet : Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere. Interdum per lac significatur innocentia seu puritas vitæ, propter naturalem lactis nitorem et utilitatem, juxta illud : Quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, lac concupiscite, ut in eo crescatis in salutem. Quandoque vero per lac, imperfecta doctrina exprimitur, sicut hoc loco ; et item ad Hebræos : Omnis qui lactis est particeps, expers est sermonis justitiæ. — Præterea, in Scriptura per hominem aliquando designatur quædam perfectio, et maxime pietas seu discretio. Unde quod discretum et pium est, dicimus esse humanum; quod vero irrationabile et crudele, dicimus inhumanum. Aliquando autem per hominem datur intelligi vitiositas quædam ad quam homines proni sunt. In quantum enim consideratur in homine pars intellectiva, designatur per ipsum perfectio. In quantum autem notatur in eo sensualitas, quam major pars hominum sequitur, significatur per eum vitiositas ista. Et ita nunc sumitur, quum ait Apostolus : Nonne carnales estis, et secundum hominem ambulatis? et, Nonne homines estis?
paras.en: From what has been said it is plain that a preacher or teacher should temper the sense and style of his teaching to the capacity of his hearers. It must also be known that by the name of milk Scripture sometimes signifies carnal pleasure, as here: [[Is 28:9|Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the hearing|Quem docebit Dominus scientiam? et quem intelligere faciet auditum?]]? And he answers: [[Is 28:9|them that are weaned from the milk, that are drawn away from the breasts|Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere]]. Sometimes milk signifies innocence or purity of life, because of the natural whiteness and usefulness of milk, according to the words: [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes|Quasi modo geniti infantes]] endowed with reason, desire milk, [[1 Pet 2:2|that thereby you may grow unto salvation|ut in eo crescatis in salutem]]. And sometimes imperfect teaching is expressed by milk, as in this place; and likewise to the Hebrews: [[Heb 5:13|every one that is a partaker of milk is unskilful in the word of justice|Omnis qui lactis est particeps, expers est sermonis justitiæ]]. Further, in Scripture "man" sometimes designates a certain perfection, and above all kindness or discretion. So we call what is discreet and kind "humane", and what is unreasonable and cruel "inhuman". But sometimes "man" is used to mean a certain viciousness to which men are prone[[Gen 8:21||]]. For in so far as the intellective part is considered in man, perfection is designated by the word. In so far as sensuality is noted in him, which the greater part of men follow, that viciousness is signified by it. And so it is taken now, when the Apostle says: [[3:3|are you not carnal and walk you not according to man|Nonne carnales estis, et secundum hominem ambulatis]]? and, [[3:4|are you not men|Nonne homines estis]]?

paras.t: Consequenter tollit Apostolus Corinthiorum errorem, dicentium aliquid gratiæ inesse Baptismo virtute ministri. Quid igitur est Apollo, episcopus vel baptista vester? Quid vero Paulus? id est, quid de nobis sentire debetis? Et respondet : Ministri sunt ejus cui credidistis, id est Christi, cujus fidem recepistis. Et unicuique eorum ac aliorum convenit esse Christi ministrum, sicut Dominus dedit, id est secundum quod Deus præstitit gradum officii et gratiæ donum. Ego plantavi, id est, primo fidei fundamenta annuntiavi, et prædicando converti. Apollo rigavit, id est, vos in fonte Baptismatis lavit, et doctrinam vobis a me traditam, sua prædicatione perfudit. Sed nec ego, nec ipse gratiam contulit. Deus autem incrementum dedit, id est, fructum, salutem et gratiam dedit, illuminando, purgando, ac perficiendo interius. Propter quod scriptum est : Pater meus agricola est. Non est autem sic intelligendum, quin etiam Deus sit principalis plantator atque rigator. Ait nempe Salvator : Omnis plantatio quam non plantavit Pater meus cœlestis, eradicabitur; et rursus, Ego te plantavi vineam electam. Sed hoc vult Apostolus dicere, quod sua instrumentalis plantatio, et instrumentalis rigatio Apollinis et cæterorum, erat dispositio ad recipiendum salutem a Deo. Itaque, neque Paulus aut alius ei similis qui plantat, secundum modum prædictum, neque Apollo vel similis qui rigat, ut dictum est, est aliquid ex se, vel comparatione ejus qui operatur interius: sed, qui incrementum dat, Deus, id est, is qui salutem et gratiam donat, reputandus est, et ab illo debet se quisque nominare, non a Paulo aut Apolline.
paras.en: Next the Apostle takes away the error of the Corinthians, who said that some grace was in Baptism by the power of the minister. [[3:4|What then is Apollo|Quid igitur est Apollo]], your bishop or baptizer? [[3:4|and what is Paul|Quid vero Paulus]]? that is, what ought you to think of us? And he answers: [[3:5|The ministers of him whom you have believed|Ministri sunt ejus cui credidistis]], that is, of Christ, whose faith you have received. [[3:5|and to every one|Et unicuique]] of them and of others it belongs to be Christ's minister, [[3:5|as the Lord hath given|sicut Dominus dedit]], that is, according as God has granted the degree of office and the gift of grace. [[3:6|I have planted|Ego plantavi]], that is, I first proclaimed the foundations of the faith and converted you by preaching[[Acts 18:11||]]. [[3:6|Apollo watered|Apollo rigavit]], that is, washed you in the font of Baptism, and steeped the teaching I had handed on to you in his preaching. But neither I nor he conferred grace. [[3:6|but God gave the increase|Deus autem incrementum dedit]], that is, gave the fruit, salvation and grace, by enlightening, cleansing and perfecting within. For this reason it is written: [[John 15:1|my Father is the husbandman|Pater meus agricola est]]. Yet this is not to be understood as if God were not also the principal planter and waterer. For the Saviour says: [[Matt 15:13|Every plant which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up|Omnis plantatio quam non plantavit Pater meus cœlestis, eradicabitur]]; and again, [[Jer 2:21|I planted thee a chosen vineyard|Ego te plantavi vineam electam]]. But the Apostle means that his instrumental planting, and the instrumental watering of Apollo and the others, was a disposing for receiving salvation from God. [[3:7|Therefore, neither he that planteth is any thing, nor he that watereth|Itaque, neque … qui plantat … neque … qui rigat … est aliquid]]: so neither Paul nor anyone like him who plants, in the way described, nor Apollo or anyone like him who waters, as has been said, is anything of himself, or in comparison with Him who works within: [[3:7|but God that giveth the increase|sed, qui incrementum dat, Deus]], that is, He who gives salvation and grace is to be reckoned with, and each should name himself after Him, not after Paul or Apollo.

paras.t: Qui plantat autem et qui rigat, extrinsecus operando, unum sunt, id est ejusdem conditionis et deputationis. Uterque enim est servus, nullus vero eorum est operator interior. Quamvis autem hi unum sunt, non tamen æqualiter præmiabuntur. Subditur enim : Unusquisque autem ministrorum Dei, propriam, id est sibi congruam, mercedem in patria accipiet a Deo secundum suum laborem exteriorem vel interiorem, ad Dei gloriam ordinatum, id est secundum exigentiam meriti sui laboris. Quomodo autem hoc intelligi debeat, multa possent induci. Sed breviter tangendo, sciendum quod merces seu præmium essentiale debetur et respondet fervori caritatis divinæ. Quanto autem quis Deum plus diligit, et a vitiis purior, atque in bonis magis habituatus est, tanto delectabilius facit opus Dei atque ferventius, et per consequens minus laboriose, præsertim loquendo de corporali labore, et prout labor pœnam ac fatigationem includit. Quanto autem delectabilius et ferventius operatur, tanto amplius promeretur. Potest ergo contingere, imo contingit quotidie, ut homo perfectus qui minus laboriose facit opus Dei, plus mereatur, quam homo imperfectus, tamen gratiam habens, qui cum gravi labore eadem facit quæ perfectus. Dicendum ergo, quod exteriori ac corporali labori respondet præmium accidentale, caritatis autem fervori, præmium essentiale. Quilibet ergo recipiet præmium accidentale secundum suum laborem corporalem: sed quanto hic labor ex ampliori caritate procedit, tanto plus recipiet de præmio essentiali, quod est visio Dei, quæ est tota merces et vita æterna.
paras.en: [[3:8|Now he that planteth and he that watereth, are one|Qui plantat autem et qui rigat, extrinsecus operando, unum sunt]]: working from outside, they are one, that is, of the same condition and appointment. For each is a servant, and neither of them is the inward worker. But although they are one, they will not be rewarded equally. For it is added: [[3:8|And every man shall receive his own reward, according to his own labour|Unusquisque autem … propriam … mercedem … accipiet … secundum suum laborem]]: every one of God's ministers will receive from God in the fatherland his own reward, that is, the one fitting for him, according to his labour, outward or inward, directed to the glory of God, that is, according to what the merit of his labour requires. Much could be brought in on how this is to be understood. But to touch on it briefly, it must be known that the essential reward is owed to, and answers to, the fervour of divine charity. Now the more a man loves God, the purer he is from vices and the more practised in good, the more delightfully and fervently he does the work of God, and so the less laboriously, especially when speaking of bodily labour, and of labour as it includes pain and weariness. And the more delightfully and fervently he works, the more he merits. So it can happen, and indeed happens daily, that a perfect man who does the work of God less laboriously merits more than an imperfect man, though in grace, who does the same things as the perfect man with heavy labour. It must be said, then, that the accidental reward answers to outward and bodily labour, and the essential reward to the fervour of charity [the essential reward is the vision of God itself; accidental rewards are joys added to it]. Each, then, will receive accidental reward according to his bodily labour; but the more this labour comes from greater charity, the more he will receive of the essential reward, which is the vision of God, which is the whole reward and eternal life.

paras.t: Quod autem quilibet secundum suum laborem accipiet, patet : Dei enim sumus adjutores, id est cooperatores, instrumentaliter operando, materiamque forinsecus præparando. Ut autem Dionysius quod omnium divinorum divinissimum est, Dei cooperatorem exsistere in reductione rationalis naturæ ad suum principium. Dei agricultura, id est ager a Deo colendus, estis, per hoc quod Deus de cordibus vestris vitiorum et passionum spinas exstirpat, virtutum semina inserit, gratiæ fecunditatem largitur. Et ita dicitur homo agricultura Dei, per similitudinem campi quem rusticus colit. Sicut enim Ecclesia appellatur vinea Domini, sic dicitur agricultura ipsius. Dei ædificatio, id est domus seu ædificium mysticum, a Deo per gratiam ædificatum, estis. Congregatio quippe fidelium, dicitur domus et templum seu tabernaculum Dei : primo, quoniam Deus fideles per caritatem consolidat atque connectit; secundo, quia per gratiam mentes eorum inhabitat.
paras.en: That each will receive according to his labour is plain: [[3:9|For we are God's coadjutors|Dei enim sumus adjutores]], that is, fellow workers, working as instruments and preparing the material from outside. And as Dionysius says [the verb is lost in the transcription], the most divine of all divine things is to be God's fellow worker in leading rational nature back to its principle. [[3:9|You are God's husbandry|Dei agricultura estis]], that is, a field to be tilled by God, in that God roots out of your hearts the thorns of vices and passions, plants the seeds of the virtues, and bestows the fruitfulness of grace. And so man is called God's husbandry, by likeness to a field which a countryman tills. For as the Church is called the vineyard of the Lord[[Is 5:1||]][[Matt 20:1||]], so it is called His husbandry. [[3:9|you are God's building|Dei ædificatio estis]], that is, a house or mystical building built by God through grace. For the congregation of the faithful is called the house and temple or tabernacle of God: first, because God makes the faithful firm and joins them together by charity; second, because He dwells in their minds by grace.

paras.t: Secundum gratiam Dei, quæ data est mihi, id est secundum apostolatum, et sapientiam mihi a Spiritu Sancto infusam, ut sapiens, id est in divinis eruditus atque discretus, architectus, id est spiritualis hujus ædificii principalis constructor, per comparationem ad alios qui vobis prædicaverunt : quamvis non sim inter Apostolos architectus, quum mea reputatione sim minimus Apostolorum; et hoc ipsum quod me ipsum architectum appello, non jactanter dico, quia non mihi, sed gratiæ Dei illud attribuo; fundamentum, id est fundamentalem doctrinam, initialem prædicationem, fidem seu Christum, posui in cordibus vestris instrumentaliter et dispositive, quoniam primo vobis prædicavi, vosque converti ad fidem; [alius autem superædificat.] Unusquisque autem vestrum videat, id est diligenter perpendat, quomodo superædificet, id est, qualem structuram operum huic fundamento fidei superponat, ne opera ejus discordent a fide, ne Deum quem ore confitetur, factis neget. Vel sic, et melius, ut sequentia verba insinuant : Unusquisque prædicatorum docentium vos, videat quomodo superædificet, id est, qualia documenta vobis proponat, ne sua doctrina fundamento a me posito contradicat.
paras.en: [[3:10|According to the grace of God that is given to me|Secundum gratiam Dei, quæ data est mihi]], that is, according to the apostleship and the wisdom poured into me by the Holy Ghost, [[3:10|as a wise architect|ut sapiens architectus]]: wise, that is, learned and discreet in divine things; architect, that is, the chief builder of this spiritual building, in comparison with the others who have preached to you: though I am not an architect among the Apostles, since in my own reckoning I am [[1 Cor 15:9|the least of the apostles|minimus Apostolorum]]; and in calling myself an architect I do not speak boastfully, because I ascribe it not to myself but to the grace of God; [[3:10|I have laid the foundation|fundamentum posui]]: the foundation, that is, the fundamental teaching, the first preaching, the faith, or Christ, I have laid in your hearts instrumentally and by way of disposing, since I first preached to you and converted you to the faith; [[3:10|and another buildeth thereon|alius autem superædificat]] [the transcription has these words in brackets]. [[3:10|But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon|Unusquisque autem … videat … quomodo superædificet]]: let each of you take heed, that is, weigh carefully, how he builds upon it, that is, what structure of works he sets upon this foundation of faith, lest his works disagree with the faith, lest he deny by deeds the God whom he confesses with his mouth[[Tit 1:16||]]. Or thus, and better, as the following words suggest: let each of the preachers who teach you take heed how he builds upon it, that is, what teachings he sets before you, lest his teaching contradict the foundation laid by me.

paras.t: Fundamentum enim aliud nemo potest ponere, id est veraciter prædicare, aut salubriter collocare, præter id quod positum est, id est, evangelizatum est a nobis et constitutum a Patre, quod est Christus Jesus, qui est solus fundamentum universale, principale principium universæ Ecclesiæ, quoniam ex se stabilitatem habet, et stabilit alios. De quo Petrus ait in Actibus : Hic est omnium Dominus, et non est in aliquo alio salus. Apostoli vero dicuntur fundamenta secundaria et particularia in Christo fundamento. Ipsi enim post Christum fundaverunt Ecclesiam. Propter quod in Apocalypsi scribitur, quod murus civitatis habet fundamenta duodecim. Et Psalmista pluraliter ait : Fundamenta ejus in montibus sanctis. — Porro Christus secundum divinam naturam, et Pater ac Spiritus Sanctus, sunt unum fundamentum electorum simpliciter primum, et fundans, non fundatum. Christus autem ut homo Verbo unitus, vel potius ut humanitatem Verbo unitam habens, est fundamentum immediatum et proximum post Trinitatem, et tamen in Deo fundatum, et toti Ecclesiæ conferens stabilimentum. Quemadmodum enim caput Christi Deus, sic et fundamentum Christi Deus.
paras.en: [[3:11|For other foundation no man can lay|Fundamentum enim aliud nemo potest ponere]], that is, truly preach or savingly set down, [[3:11|but that which is laid|præter id quod positum est]], that is, preached by us and established by the Father, [[3:11|which is Christ Jesus|quod est Christus Jesus]], who alone is the universal foundation, the chief principle of the whole Church, since He has firmness of Himself and makes others firm. Of whom Peter says in the Acts: [[Acts 10:36|He is Lord of all|Hic est omnium Dominus]], and [[Acts 4:12|Neither is there salvation in any other|non est in aliquo alio salus]]. The Apostles are called secondary and particular foundations in Christ the foundation. For they founded the Church after Christ. For this reason it is written in the Apocalypse that [[Apoc 21:14|the wall of the city had twelve foundations|murus civitatis habet fundamenta duodecim]]. And the Psalmist says in the plural: [[Ps 86:1|The foundations thereof are the holy mountains|Fundamenta ejus in montibus sanctis]]. Further, Christ according to the divine nature, with the Father and the Holy Ghost, is the one foundation of the elect, first absolutely, founding and not founded. But Christ as man united to the Word, or rather as having humanity united to the Word, is the immediate and nearest foundation after the Trinity, and yet founded in God, and giving firmness to the whole Church. For as [[1 Cor 11:3|the head of Christ is God|caput Christi Deus]], so too the foundation of Christ is God.

paras.t: Si quis autem superædificat, docendo vel operando, supra fundamentum hoc, quod est Christus seu fides, aurum, id est amorem vel contemplationem divinorum, argentum, id est dilectionem proximi, seu speculationem intellectualium atque cœlestium creaturarum, per quas Deus evidentius subtiliusque cognoscitur, lapides pretiosos, id est opera virtuosa seu verba efficacia, ligna, fœnum, stipulam, id est vanam doctrinam, magis vel minus nocivam, non tamen hæreticam, nec mortaliter vitiosam. Vel per lignum, fœnum, stipulam, intelliguntur peccata venialia triplicem gradum habentia : ut per ligna designentur peccata venialia magis tenacia et mortalibus viciniora, quæ ardebunt diutius, nisi modo purgentur, quemadmodum lignum diutius ardet quam fœnum aut stipula ; per fœnum vero signantur peccata venialia medio modo se habentia ; per stipulam, peccata levissima, quæ citius purgantur quam prædicta, sicut et stipula citius consumitur quam fœnum aut lignum. Denique venialia ista dicuntur ædificari supra fidei fundamentum, id est juxta illud. Non enim procedunt ex fide, nec innituntur ei, sed sunt simul cum ea. Non enim caritatem exstinguunt. Simili modo dicimus aliquam civitatem sitam supra mare, id est juxta mare : secundum quem sensum ait Psalmista, Qui fundavit terram super aquas, id est juxta eas.
paras.en: [[3:12|Now, if any man build upon this foundation|Si quis autem superædificat super fundamentum hoc]], by teaching or doing, upon this foundation, which is Christ, or the faith, [[3:12|gold|aurum]], that is, the love or contemplation of divine things, [[3:12|silver|argentum]], that is, love of neighbour, or the contemplation of intellectual and heavenly creatures, through which God is known more plainly and more subtly[[Wis 13:5||]], [[3:12|precious stones|lapides pretiosos]], that is, virtuous works or effective words, [[3:12|wood, hay, stubble|ligna, fœnum, stipulam]], that is, vain teaching, more or less harmful, but not heretical nor mortally sinful. Or by wood, hay and stubble are understood venial sins having three degrees: so that wood designates venial sins that cling more and are nearer to mortal sins, which will burn longer unless they are cleansed now, as wood burns longer than hay or stubble; hay signifies venial sins of a middle kind; stubble, the lightest sins, which are cleansed more quickly than the others, as stubble is consumed more quickly than hay or wood. Lastly, these venial sins are said to be built upon the foundation of faith, that is, beside it. For they do not proceed from faith nor rest on it, but are together with it. For they do not extinguish charity. In the same way we say that a city lies upon the sea, that is, beside the sea: in which sense the Psalmist says, [[Ps 135:6|Who established the earth above the waters|Qui fundavit terram super aquas]][[Ps 23:2||]], that is, beside them.

paras.t: Uniuscujusque opus manifestum erit, id est, in publicum deducetur et innotescet, non solum Deo et propriæ conscientiæ, sed etiam aliis, quando Dominus illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium. Unde ait Salvator : Nihil opertum quod non revelabitur. Dies enim Domini, id est dies judicii, vel potius Dominus in die judicii (dies namque et tempus dicuntur facere ea quæ fiunt in die et tempore), declarabit opera singulorum qualia sint : quia in igne conflagrationis revelabitur, id est, manifestabitur dies Domini, vel Dominus, qui venturus est judicare per ignem, cujus majestatem ignis ipse ostendet ; vel, Revelabitur opus cujuslibet, sicut subjungitur. Et uniuscujusque opus quale sit, ignis probabit, id est ostendet. Quod potest intelligi : vel de igne purgatorii, quantum ad eos qui interim moriuntur ; vel de igne conflagrationis præcedente judicium, quo exuretur facies mundi, de quo in Psalmo, Ignis ante ipsum præcedet ; vel de igne æterno, sequente judicium. Ignis autem conflagrationis mundabit et emundabit eos qui superædificaverunt lignum, fœnum, stipulam. Qui vero superædificaverunt aurum, argentum, lapides pretiosos, a quolibet igne hoc erunt securi. Ideo sequitur : Si cujus, id est alicujus, opus manserit, id est, intactum et inconsumptum perseveraverit ab igne, tanquam non habens culpam admixtam : quod superædificatum est, id est opus tale in fide fundatum, mercedem accipiet plenam et indilatam. Nihil enim de opere suo amittet, et quod amavit inveniet. Si cujus opus arserit, id est, ignis pœnam pertulerit propter veniale admixtum ; detrimentum patietur, id est, minus de gloria obtinebit, quanto opus suum imperfectius ac cremabilius fuerit. Ipse autem homo sola venialia habens, salvus erit, satisfactione completa ; sic tamen quasi per ignem, id est ignis sustinendo ardorem, secundum culpæ suæ exigentiam.
paras.en: [[3:13|Every man's work shall be manifest|Uniuscujusque opus manifestum erit]], that is, will be brought out in public and become known, not only to God and to one's own conscience but to others too, when the Lord [[1 Cor 4:5|will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts|illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium]]. So the Saviour says: [[Matt 10:26|nothing is covered that shall not be revealed|Nihil opertum quod non revelabitur]]. [[3:13|For the day of the Lord|Dies enim Domini]], that is, the day of judgment, or rather the Lord on the day of judgment (for the day and the time are said to do what is done in the day and the time), [[3:13|shall declare it|declarabit]], what sort the works of each are: [[3:13|because it shall be revealed in fire|quia in igne conflagrationis revelabitur]], in the fire of the conflagration [Denis's text adds *conflagrationis*], that is, the day of the Lord will be made manifest, or the Lord, who is to come to judge by fire, whose majesty the fire itself will show; or, each man's work will be revealed, as is added. [[3:13|And the fire shall try every man's work, of what sort it is|Et uniuscujusque opus quale sit, ignis probabit]], that is, will show. This can be understood either of the fire of purgatory, as for those who die in the meantime; or of the fire of the conflagration going before the judgment, by which the face of the world will be burned, of which the Psalm says, [[Ps 96:3|A fire shall go before him|Ignis ante ipsum præcedet]]; or of the eternal fire that follows the judgment. The fire of the conflagration will cleanse and purge those who built wood, hay and stubble upon it. But those who built gold, silver and precious stones will be safe from all this fire. So it follows: [[3:14|If any man's work abide|Si cujus opus manserit]], that is, continue untouched and unconsumed by the fire, as having no guilt mixed in, [[3:14|which he hath built thereupon|quod superædificatum est]], that is, such a work founded in faith, [[3:14|he shall receive a reward|mercedem accipiet]], full and without delay. For he will lose nothing of his work, and will find what he loved. [[3:15|If any mans work burn|Si cujus opus arserit]], that is, has borne the punishment of fire for the venial sin mixed in, [[3:15|he shall suffer loss|detrimentum patietur]], that is, will obtain less of glory, the more imperfect and burnable his work was. [[3:15|but he himself shall be saved|ipse autem salvus erit]]: the man himself, having only venial sins, will be saved when satisfaction is complete; [[3:15|yet so as by fire|sic tamen quasi per ignem]], that is, by enduring the burning of the fire, according to what his guilt requires.

paras.t: Denique, sicut exposita sunt hæc pro tempore judicii universalis, ita intelligi possunt de die particularis judicii : ut dies Domini dicatur dies mortis, quo Deus hominem visitat, tollens eum de vita præsenti. Illa itaque dies Domini, seu Dominus in die illa, declarat quale sit opus hominis, quem statim quum mortuus fuerit, judicat : quia in igne purgatorii revelabitur seu declaratur quale sit opus hominis. Et uniuscujusque opus quale sit, scilicet purum vel impurum, ignis purgatorii probabit : non quod omnes illum ignem sustinebunt, quia nec de omnibus simpliciter est jam sermo, sed de his omnibus qui manent in fundamento, id est in Christo per gratiam, et superædificant opera perfectionis, quæ non ardent, vel opera imperfecta, quæ ardent. Si cujus opus manserit immune ac liberum ab igne purgatorii, ut sunt opera significata per aurum, argentum et lapides pretiosos ; quod superædificatum est, id est opus hoc in Christo seu in fide fundatum, mercedem accipiet et gloriam sempiternam sine mora, ita quod evolabit. Si cujus opus arserit in purgatorio ; detrimentum patietur, pœnam luendo, gloriamque minorem habendo. Ipse autem salvus erit, quum […] opera ejus digne cremata et expurgata : sic tamen quasi per ignem purgatorii, per quem transibit ad gloriam, quoniam non discessit a fundamento, nec aliquid prætulit Deo, sed ultimo fini magis inhæsit quam alicui bono creato, quamvis a terrenis affectibus non fuerit satis mundatus.
paras.en: Lastly, as these things have been explained of the time of the general judgment, so they can be understood of the day of the particular judgment: so that the day of the Lord is called the day of death, on which God visits a man, taking him from the present life. That day of the Lord, then, or the Lord on that day, declares what sort a man's work is, whom He judges as soon as he has died: because in the fire of purgatory it will be revealed, or declared, what sort a man's work is. And the fire of purgatory will try every man's work, of what sort it is, namely pure or impure: not that all will undergo that fire, for the words do not now concern all simply, but all those who remain on the foundation, that is, in Christ by grace, and build upon it works of perfection, which do not burn, or imperfect works, which burn. If any man's work abide, immune and free from the fire of purgatory, as are the works signified by gold, silver and precious stones, which he hath built thereupon, that is, this work founded in Christ, or in faith, he shall receive a reward and everlasting glory without delay, so that he will fly away to it. If any man's work burn in purgatory, he shall suffer loss, by paying the penalty and having less glory. But he himself shall be saved when his works […] [a word is lost in the transcription] have been duly burned and purged: yet so as by the fire of purgatory, through which he will pass to glory, since he did not depart from the foundation, nor prefer anything to God, but clung to the last end more than to any created good, though he had not been cleansed enough from earthly affections.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Apostolus, cur aliquis mereatur omnino perire, æternaliterque damnari. Nescitis (imo scire debetis) quia templum Dei estis vos, in quo Dominus habitat per caritatem et gratiam (qui enim manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo), et Spiritus Dei, videlicet Spiritus Sanctus, habitat in vobis ? De quo Spiritu dicit Salvator : Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum. Omnes autem fideles re et nomine, sunt unum templum Dei, id est una Ecclesia, propter mysticam unitatem, seu unam fidem, atque individuam caritatem ; et unusquisque eorum est templum Dei. Dicitur autem homo templum Dei, non solum propter animam, in qua Deus per gratiam commoratur (nam anima justi sedes est sapientiæ), sed etiam propter corpus rationi et Deo subjectum, in quo gratia mentis, et per consequens inhabitatio Dei redundat. Dicit enim alio loco Apostolus : Nescitis quia membra vestra templum sunt Spiritus Sancti ? Et iterum : Glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows why someone deserves to perish altogether and be damned for ever. [[3:16|Know you not|Nescitis]] (indeed you ought to know) [[3:16|that you are the temple of God|quia templum Dei estis]], in which the Lord dwells by charity and grace (for [[1 John 4:16|he that abideth in charity abideth in God, and God in him|qui enim manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo]]), [[3:16|and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you|et Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis?]], namely the Holy Ghost? Of this Spirit the Saviour says: [[John 14:16|I will ask the Father: and he shall give you another Paraclete, that he may abide with you for ever|Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum]]. All who are faithful in fact and in name are one temple of God, that is, one Church, because of the mystical unity, or the one faith and undivided charity; and each of them is a temple of God. Man is called a temple of God not only because of the soul, in which God dwells by grace (for the soul of the just is the seat of wisdom[[Wis 7:27||]]), but also because of the body, subject to reason and to God, into which the grace of the mind, and so the indwelling of God, overflows. For the Apostle says in another place: [[1 Cor 6:19|know you not that your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost|Nescitis quia membra vestra templum sunt Spiritus Sancti]]? And again: [[1 Cor 6:20|Glorify and bear God in your body|Glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro]].

paras.t: Si quis autem templum Dei violaverit, id est, credentes perverterit, falsa docendo aut impie operando, disperdet, id est, diversimode perdet, illum Deus, damnando illum anima et corpore in æternum. Sed et si quis materiale templum violaverit, erit sacrilegus. Templum enim Dei vivum et spirituale, sanctum est formaliter, quod estis vos, qui in Baptismo sanctificati estis, et per opera bona exercitati.
paras.en: [[3:17|But if any man violate the temple of God|Si quis autem templum Dei violaverit]], that is, perverts believers by teaching falsehood or acting wickedly, [[3:17|him shall God destroy|disperdet illum Deus]] [*disperdet*: Denis reads *dis-* as "in various ways"], condemning him in soul and body for ever. And if anyone violates the material temple, he will be guilty of sacrilege. [[3:17|For the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum enim Dei … sanctum est … quod estis vos]]: the living and spiritual temple of God is holy formally, and that you are, who were sanctified in Baptism and trained by good works.

paras.t: Nemo vos seducat, laudando, blandiendo, simulando, ornate loquendo, aut simili modo. Si quis videtur inter vos sapiens esse in hoc sæculo, id est sæcularem sapientiam habere, se sapientem putare, et ab aliis sapiens reputari, stultus fiat mundo : id est, talem sapientiam a se repellat, se ipsum stultum reputet, saltem in se, quia ex se ipso non habet nisi ignorantiæ tenebras ; nec cupiat in mundo sapiens reputari, sed amet nesciri ; ut sit sapiens Deo, id est, ut veram sapientiam mereatur a Deo acquirere. Sapientia enim hujus mundi, id est carnalis prudentia : de qua dictum est ad Romanos, Prudentia carnis, mors est; stultitia est apud Deum, id est, a Deo stulta judicatur. Imo et naturalis seu philosophica sapientia quæ fide et dono sapientiæ non ornatur, stulta est coram Deo, id est infructuosa et tumida. Quod auctoritate Scripturæ probat Apostolus. Scriptum est enim in libro Job : Comprehendam, id est, concludam et capiam, sapientes mundi in astutia, id est in apparente sapientia eorum. Nostra translatio habet sic : Qui apprehendit sapientes in astutia eorum, et consilium pravorum dissipat. Cui consonat quod per Isaiam de Domino dicitur : Convertens sapientes retrorsum, et scientiam eorum stultam faciens. Et iterum scriptum est : Dominus novit cogitationes sapientium sæculi hujus, quoniam vanæ sunt. Nostra littera talis est : Dominus scit cogitationes hominum, quoniam vanæ sunt.
paras.en: [[3:18|Let no man deceive himself|Nemo vos seducat]] [Denis reads "Let no man deceive you"], by praise, flattery, pretence, fine speaking or the like. [[3:18|If any man among you seem to be wise in this world|Si quis videtur inter vos sapiens esse in hoc sæculo]], that is, to have worldly wisdom, to think himself wise and to be thought wise by others, [[3:18|let him become a fool|stultus fiat]] to the world: that is, let him drive such wisdom from himself, count himself a fool, at least in himself, because of himself he has nothing but the darkness of ignorance; and let him not desire to be thought wise in the world, but love to be unknown; [[3:18|that he may be wise|ut sit sapiens]] to God, that is, that he may deserve to gain true wisdom from God. [[3:19|For the wisdom of this world|Sapientia enim hujus mundi]], that is, carnal prudence, of which it was said to the Romans, [[Rom 8:6|the wisdom of the flesh is death|Prudentia carnis, mors est]]; [[3:19|is foolishness with God|stultitia est apud Deum]], that is, is judged foolish by God. Indeed even natural or philosophical wisdom which is not adorned by faith and the gift of wisdom is foolish before God, that is, fruitless and puffed up. This the Apostle proves by the authority of Scripture. [[3:19|For it is written|Scriptum est enim]] in the book of Job: [[3:19|I will catch|Comprehendam]], that is, shut in and seize, [[3:19|the wise in their own craftiness|sapientes … in astutia … eorum]], the wise of the world, in their craftiness, that is, in their seeming wisdom. Our translation has it thus: [[Job 5:13|Who catcheth the wise in their craftiness, and disappointeth the counsel of the wicked|Qui apprehendit sapientes in astutia eorum, et consilium pravorum dissipat]]. With which agrees what is said of the Lord through Isaias: [[Is 44:25|That turn the wise backward, and that make their knowledge foolish|Convertens sapientes retrorsum, et scientiam eorum stultam faciens]]. [[3:20|And again|Et iterum]] it is written: [[3:20|The Lord knoweth the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain|Dominus novit cogitationes sapientium sæculi hujus, quoniam vanæ sunt]]: of the wise of this world. Our text reads: [[Ps 93:11|The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men, that they are vain|Dominus scit cogitationes hominum, quoniam vanæ sunt]].

paras.t: Itaque nemo glorietur in hominibus, jactando se baptizatum seu doctum ab illo, vel illo ; sed in solo Domino glorietur. Omnia enim vestra sunt, id est vestræ servituti et utilitati parata et deputata, sive Paulus, sive Apollo, sive Cephas, id est Petrus archiapostolus ; sive mundus iste sensibilis, scilicet corpora cœlestia, elementa et mixta. De corporibus enim cœlestibus Moyses ait in Deuteronomio : Solem, lunam et omnia astra cœli creavit Dominus Deus tuus in ministerium cunctis gentibus. Et Psalmista : Omnia, inquit, subjecisti sub pedibus ejus. Et in Genesi Dominus loquitur : Faciamus hominem, etc., et præsit bestiis terræ, et piscibus maris, et avibus cœli, universæque creaturæ. Sed et angeli administratorii spiritus sunt. Sive vita, id est operatio nostra, ut vobis proficiat; sive mors corporalis, ut pro vobis, si opus fuerit, sustineatur; sive præsentia beneficia Dei quæ habetis in re, sive futura promissa quæ habetis in spe. Omnia enim hæc vestra sunt aliquo modo, ut dictum est. Vos autem estis servi atque discipuli Christi, et estis ejus, jure creationis, gubernationis ac liberationis. Christus autem Dei. Christus secundum divinam naturam, est Dei Patris, tanquam unicus et naturalis Filius ejus. Secundum humanitatem vero, est Dei tanquam minister ipsius, factus obediens usque ad mortem. De quo Deus ait per Isaiam: Ecce intelligit servus meus, et exaltabitur. Hinc etiam Filius dicit ad Patrem: Omnia mea, tua sunt; et, Ego non quæro gloriam meam.
paras.en: [[3:21|Let no man therefore glory in men|Itaque nemo glorietur in hominibus]], boasting that he was baptized or taught by this man or that; but [[2 Cor 10:17|let him glory in the Lord|in solo Domino glorietur]] alone. [[3:22|For all things are yours|Omnia enim vestra sunt]], that is, made ready and appointed for your service and benefit, [[3:22|whether it be Paul or Apollo or Cephas|sive Paulus, sive Apollo, sive Cephas]], that is, Peter, the chief of the Apostles; [[3:22|or the world|sive mundus]], this world of sense, namely the heavenly bodies, the elements and the things compounded of them. For of the heavenly bodies Moses says in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 4:19|the sun and the moon, and all the stars of heaven|Solem, lunam et omnia astra cœli]] [[Deut 4:19|which the Lord thy God created for the service of all the nations|creavit Dominus Deus tuus in ministerium cunctis gentibus]]. And the Psalmist: [[Ps 8:8|Thou hast subjected all things under his feet|Omnia, inquit, subjecisti sub pedibus ejus]]. And in Genesis the Lord says: [[Gen 1:26|Let us make man|Faciamus hominem]], etc., and let him rule over the beasts of the earth, the fishes of the sea, the birds of the air and every creature. And the angels too are [[Heb 1:14|ministering spirits|administratorii spiritus]]. [[3:22|or life|Sive vita]], that is, our working, that it may profit you; [[3:22|or death|sive mors]], bodily death, to be borne for you if need be; [[3:22|or things present|sive præsentia]], the benefits of God which you have in fact, [[3:22|or things to come|sive futura]], the promises which you have in hope. For all these are yours in some way, as has been said. [[3:23|And you are Christ's|vos autem Christi]]: you are the servants and disciples of Christ, and you are His, by right of creation, government and deliverance. [[3:23|And Christ is God's|Christus autem Dei]]. Christ according to the divine nature is God the Father's, as His only and natural Son. According to His humanity He is God's as His servant, [[Phil 2:8|becoming obedient unto death|factus obediens usque ad mortem]]. Of whom God says through Isaias: [[Is 52:13|Behold my servant shall understand, he shall be exalted|Ecce intelligit servus meus, et exaltabitur]]. Hence too the Son says to the Father: [[John 17:10|all my things are thine|Omnia mea, tua sunt]]; and, [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]].

4.title: Expositio capituli quarti: Sic nos existimet homo ut ministros Christi
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: Let a man so account of us as of the ministers of Christ

paras.t: Præterea docet Apostolus, quid debeant subditi de superioribus suis sentire, ne eos plus quam decet magnificent, nec eos contemnant, si forte in aliquibus minus excellentes videntur. Sic nos Apostolos et prædicatores ac Christi vicarios existimet homo quicumque fidelis, ut ministros Christi, non ut principales, aut gratiæ collatores, et ut dispensatores, id est exhibitores seu distributores, mysteriorum Dei, id est divinorum sacramentorum; vel, Mysteriorum Dei, id est ecclesiasticorum officiorum. Hic jam quæritur, id est, a vobis Corinthiis interrogatur atque discutitur, inter dispensatores, ut fidelis quis inveniatur, id est, quis dispensatorum istorum sit verus dispensator, cui possit dispensatio secure committi. Corinthii enim inter dispensatores hos discernebant, unum approbantes, alium reprobantes. Sed quia homines sancti tale judicium non formidant nec reputant, subditur:
paras.en: Further, the Apostle teaches what subjects ought to think of their superiors, so that they neither extol them more than is fitting nor despise them if perhaps they seem less excellent in some things. [[4:1|Let a man so account of us|Sic nos existimet homo]]: let every faithful man so account of us Apostles and preachers and vicars of Christ, [[4:1|as of the ministers of Christ|ut ministros Christi]], not as principal causes or bestowers of grace, [[4:1|and the dispensers|et ut dispensatores]], that is, the presenters or distributors, [[4:1|of the mysteries of God|mysteriorum Dei]], that is, of the divine sacraments; or, of the mysteries of God, that is, of the offices of the Church.
