[[4:2|Here now it is required|Hic jam quæritur]], that is, it is asked and discussed by you Corinthians, [[4:2|among the dispensers that a man be found faithful|inter dispensatores, ut fidelis quis inveniatur]], that is, which of these dispensers is a true dispenser, to whom the dispensing can safely be entrusted. For the Corinthians made distinctions among these dispensers, approving one and rejecting another. But because holy men neither fear nor regard such judgment, it is added:

paras.t: Mihi autem pro minimo est, id est, nihili pondero, ut a vobis adhuc carnalibus judicer judicio reprobationis, tanquam dispensator indignus, aut ab hominibus die […], id est ab homine in hoc tempore peregrinante; sed neque me ipsum judico judicio absoluto ac definitivo, damnando videlicet me ipsum. Debet tamen homo judicare se ipsum judicio discussionis et reprobationis opinativæ, æstimando se peccatorem vilem ac miserum. Nihil enim mihi conscius sum, id est, de nullo peccato remorsum conscientiæ habeo: de præteritis enim satisfeci, et scio quia indulta sunt mihi. Nec obstat quod alibi dicit, Venit Christus peccatores salvos facere, quorum ego primus sum. Hoc enim dixit habendo respectum ad tempus præteritum, quo persequebatur Ecclesiam. Qui autem judicat me, id est ad quem pertinet absolute judicare de secretis cordis mei, Dominus est, qui solus novit corda humana: nam et Pater omne judicium dedit Filio.
paras.en: [[4:3|But to me it is a very small thing|Mihi autem pro minimo est]], that is, I weigh it as nothing, [[4:3|to be judged by you|ut a vobis adhuc carnalibus judicer]], who are still carnal, with a judgment of condemnation, as an unworthy dispenser, [[4:3|or by man's day|aut ab hominibus die]] […] [a word is lost in the transcription], that is, by man on pilgrimage in this time; [[4:3|But neither do I judge my own self|sed neque me ipsum judico]] with an absolute and final judgment, namely by condemning myself. Yet a man ought to judge himself with a judgment of examination and of a reproof based on opinion, counting himself a vile and wretched sinner. [[4:4|For I am not conscious to myself of anything|Nihil enim mihi conscius sum]], that is, I have no remorse of conscience for any sin: for I have made satisfaction for the past, and I know that it has been forgiven me. Nor does it stand in the way that he says elsewhere, [[1 Tim 1:15|Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the chief|Venit Christus peccatores salvos facere, quorum ego primus sum]]. For he said this with regard to the past time, when he persecuted the Church. [[4:4|but he that judgeth me is the Lord|qui autem judicat me, Dominus est]], that is, He to whom it belongs to judge absolutely the secrets of my heart, who alone knows human hearts: for [[John 5:22|hath given all judgment to the Son|Pater omne judicium dedit Filio]] [Denis: "the Father hath given …"].

paras.t: Itaque nolite ante tempus extremi judicii judicare judicio definitivo de secretis ac dubiis, maxime aliorum, quoadusque veniat Dominus ad judicium; qui et illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, id est, peccata occulta faciet manifesta, ponendo ea in lumine cognitionis, sicut ait: Nihil occultum quod non revelabitur, […] stabit consilia cordium, an bona et justa fuerint, an non, prout per Isaiam protestatur. Ego autem opera eorum et cogitationes eorum venio ut congregem. Et tunc laus, id est sententia salvativa et meritorum protestatio, erit unicuique bene agenti a Deo, id est Christo judice. Quasi dicat : Tunc nullus laudabitur nisi quem Deus laudaverit ; et omnem laude dignum Deus laudabit.
paras.en: [[4:5|Therefore, judge not before the time|Itaque nolite ante tempus extremi judicii judicare]] of the last judgment, with a final judgment, of secret and doubtful things, especially those of others, [[4:5|until the Lord come|quoadusque veniat Dominus]] to judgment; [[4:5|who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness|qui et illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum]], that is, will make hidden sins manifest, setting them in the light of knowledge, as He says: [[Luke 8:17|there is not any thing secret that shall not be made manifest|Nihil occultum quod non revelabitur]], […] [[4:5|and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts|stabit consilia cordium]] [the beginning of *manifestabit* is lost in the transcription], whether they were good and just or not, as He declares through Isaias: [[Is 66:18|But I know their works, and their thoughts: I come that I may gather them|Ego autem opera eorum et cogitationes eorum venio ut congregem]]. [[4:5|And then shall every man have praise from God|Et tunc laus … erit unicuique … a Deo]]: praise, that is, the sentence of salvation and the declaring of merits, will be to every one who does well from God, that is, from Christ the judge. As if he said: then no one will be praised except him whom God praises; and God will praise everyone worthy of praise.

paras.t: Hæc autem, fratres, transfiguravi in me et Apollo : id est, ista quæ scripsi de vestra gloriatione inani, qua quilibet gloriatur in eo qui sibi eloquentior videtur et doctior, vel cui magis afficitur, gratia exempli seu figuraliter dixi de me atque Apollo : quum tamen non gloriaremini in nobis, sed magis in pseudoapostolis et mundi hujus philosophiæ magistris : quos nolui nominatim exprimere, ne major dissensio fieret ; sed loco illorum expressi me et Apollo, quatenus eisdem rationibus quibus probavi non esse gloriandum in Apollo et me, intelligatis non esse gloriandum in his in quibus gloriamini. Quod utique feci propter vos, id est ad vestri instructionem, [ut in nobis discatis,] videlicet, ne supra, id est ultra, quam scriptum est in Jeremia, ubi jubemur in Deo, non in hominibus gloriari, unus vestrum adversus alterum infletur tumore superbiæ pro alio, id est zelo baptistæ vel doctoris ad quem inclinatur. Si enim Apostolus illos pseudo nominasset, Corinthii superbissent contra se invicem, unoquoque eorum zelante pro suo doctore sive baptista.
paras.en: [[4:6|But these things, brethren, I have in a figure transferred to myself and to Apollo|Hæc autem, fratres, transfiguravi in me et Apollo]]: that is, what I have written about your vain glorying, by which each one glories in the man who seems to him more eloquent and learned, or to whom he is more attached, I have said by way of example, or figuratively, of myself and Apollo: though you did not glory in us, but rather in false apostles and masters of the philosophy of this world. These I did not wish to name, lest greater dissension arise; but in their place I put myself and Apollo, so that by the same reasons by which I proved that one must not glory in Apollo and me, you might understand that one must not glory in those in whom you glory. This I did [[4:6|for your sakes|propter vos]], that is, for your instruction, [[4:6|that in us you may learn|ut in nobis discatis]], namely, [[4:6|that one be not puffed up against the other for another, above that which is written|ne supra … quam scriptum est … unus … adversus alterum infletur … pro alio]]: above, that is, beyond, what is written in Jeremias, where we are commanded to glory in God, not in men[[Jer 9:23||]][[Jer 9:24||]]; puffed up with the swelling of pride, for another, that is, out of zeal for the baptizer or teacher to whom he leans. For if the Apostle had named those false apostles, the Corinthians would have grown proud against one another, each of them zealous for his own teacher or baptizer.

paras.t: Non autem debes, o homo, contra alium intumescere. Quis enim te discernit ? id est, quis te ab alio facit differre ? Quis te ab alio distinguit ac separat dignitate ac merito, ut contra eum infleris, et ei te præferas ? Et quoniam posset quis allegare suam perfectionem, dicendo quod virtuosior esset ac melior seu doctior alio, huic vanitati respondet Apostolus : Quid autem boni in donis naturæ vel gratiæ habes quod non accepisti a Deo mediate vel immediate, a quo est omne datum optimum et omne donum perfectum ? Si autem accepisti hoc modo, quid gloriaris in te vel creaturis, quasi non acceperis ista bona a Deo ? Itaque Deo gratias age, et in ipso lætare ; et quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus, ut Deo humilitatem jubenti tanto promptius pareas, quanto plura bona ab eo receperis. Unde ait Gregorius : Tanto esse humilior atque ad serviendum Deo promptior quisque debet ex munere, quanto obligatiorem se conspicit in reddenda ratione. Quanto enim quis majora a Deo suscipit dona, tanto amplius obligatur Deo in omnibus obedire ex caritate sincera.
paras.en: You must not swell up against another, O man. [[4:7|For who distinguisheth thee|Quis enim te discernit]]? that is, who makes you differ from another? Who distinguishes and separates you from another in dignity and merit, so that you are puffed up against him and set yourself above him? And since someone might allege his own perfection, saying that he is more virtuous and better or more learned than another, the Apostle answers this vanity: [[4:7|Or what hast thou that thou hast not received|quid autem habes quod non accepisti?]]: what good in the gifts of nature or grace do you have that you have not received from God, mediately or immediately, from whom is [[Jas 1:17|Every best gift and every perfect gift|omne datum optimum et omne donum perfectum]]? [[4:7|and if thou hast received, why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received it|Si autem accepisti … quid gloriaris … quasi non acceperis]]: if you have received in this way, why do you glory in yourself or in creatures, as if you had not received these goods from God? So give thanks to God and rejoice in Him; and [[Ecclus 3:20|The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things|quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus]], so that you may obey God, who commands humility, the more readily the more goods you have received from Him. So Gregory says: Each one ought to be the humbler and the readier to serve God because of a gift, the more bound he sees himself to be in rendering an account. For the greater the gifts a man receives from God, the more he is bound to obey God in all things out of sincere charity[[Luke 12:48||]].

paras.t: Insuper, amplius ironice loquens, Corinthiorum præsumptionem redarguit, dicens : Jam saturati estis saturitate spirituali : de qua dicitur, Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur. Itaque, Saturati estis cibo animæ, scilicet pane vitæ et aqua sapientiæ. Jam divites facti estis, id est divinis charismatibus adimpleti. Sine nobis regnatis, id est, auxilio nostro non indigetis, regendo vos ipsos. Quod autem hoc non asserendo, sed increpando et condolendo dicatur, pandunt verba sequentia : et utinam regnetis veraciter, juste regendo vos invicem, et vitiis prævalendo, ut et nos vobiscum regnaremus, id est, consortes essemus atque participes meriti vestri atque tantæ perfectionis. Et hoc merito dico :
paras.en: Besides, speaking more ironically, he rebukes the presumption of the Corinthians, saying: [[4:8|You are now full|Jam saturati estis]] with spiritual fullness, of which it is said, [[Matt 5:6|Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice: for they shall have their fill|Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur]]. So: you are full of the food of the soul, namely [[Ecclus 15:3|the bread of life|pane vitæ]] and the water of wisdom. [[4:8|you are now become rich|Jam divites facti estis]], that is, filled with divine gifts. [[4:8|you reign without us|Sine nobis regnatis]], that is, you do not need our help, ruling yourselves. That this is said not as an assertion but in rebuke and sorrow the following words show: [[4:8|and I would to God you did reign|et utinam regnetis]] truly, ruling one another justly and prevailing over vices, [[4:8|that we also might reign with you|ut et nos vobiscum regnaremus]], that is, that we might be companions and sharers of your merit and of so great a perfection. And I say this with reason:

paras.t: Puto enim (ironice autem loquitur), quod Deus nos Apostolos universos novissimos, id est imos et vilissimos, ostendit, quum tamen secundum veritatem simus a Deo constituti principes mundi. Ostendit autem nos tanquam morti destinatos, id est ad moriendum missos, quasi ad nihil utiles simus, nisi ut occidamur ; quia spectaculum, id est objectum præcipuæ et cujusdam admirativæ inspectionis, facti sumus mundo, id est hominibus impiis et mundanis, et angelis bonis ac malis, et hominibus rationabiliter ac pie viventibus. Quemadmodum enim ad spectaculum aliquod magna hominum confluit multitudo, sic ad inspiciendum personas et persecutiones Apostolorum, homines concurrerunt : impii, ut irriderent : dæmones, ut fortitudinem mentis auferrent ; angeli sancti, ut intus confortarent ; homines pii, ut condolerent. — Potest tamen legi assertive sine ironia, ut sit sensus : Puto enim, id est agnosco, quod Deus nos Apostolos novissimos, id est infimos et abjectos, ostendit, id est, apparere fecit, dando nobis præcepta spernendi mundum et cuncta quæ mundi sunt, prædicandi quoque crucem Christi et mundi contemptum.
paras.en: [[4:9|For I think that God hath set forth us apostles, the last|Puto enim … quod Deus nos Apostolos … novissimos … ostendit]] (he speaks ironically): that God has shown all of us Apostles as the last, that is, the lowest and most worthless, though in truth we have been made by God princes of the world[[Ps 44:17||]]. He has shown us [[4:9|as it were men appointed to death|tanquam morti destinatos]], that is, sent to die, as if we were good for nothing but to be killed; [[4:9|We are made a spectacle|quia spectaculum facti sumus]], that is, the object of special and a kind of wondering gaze, [[4:9|to the world|mundo]], that is, to wicked and worldly men, [[4:9|and to angels|et angelis]], good and bad, [[4:9|and to men|et hominibus]] who live reasonably and devoutly. For just as a great crowd of men flocks to some spectacle, so men ran together to look upon the persons and persecutions of the Apostles: the wicked to mock, the demons to take away their strength of mind, the holy angels to strengthen them within, devout men to share their grief. Yet it can also be read as an assertion, without irony, so that the sense is: For I think, that is, I recognize, that God has shown us Apostles as the last, that is, the lowest and outcast; has shown us, that is, has made us appear so, by giving us precepts to despise the world and all that is of the world, and to preach the cross of Christ and contempt of the world.

paras.t: Nos stulti propter Christum, id est, amore Christi sic agimus, quod a mundo stulti et insensati putamur ; vos autem prudentes estis in Christo, secundum æstimationem vestram superbam. Nos infirmi reputamur, et propriam infirmitatem agnoscimus ; vos autem fortes, id est, virtuosi estis, ut opinamini, qui putatis vos non indigere nostro auxilio. Vos nobiles, nos autem ignobiles. Totum ironice dicitur, ut confundantur et corrigantur carnales. Apostoli quippe carne et spiritu nobiliores erant Corinthiis, quoniam semen Abrahæ erant, et primitias Spiritus Sancti receperunt. Usque in hanc horam, id est assidue, et esurimus, et sitimus, et nudi sumus, id est, inopiam cibi, potus ac vestium patimur. Unde alibi dicit Apostolus : In fame et siti, in frigore et nuditate. Tunc impletum est verbum Christi quod dixit : Veniet tempus quum auferetur ab eis sponsus, et tunc jejunabunt. Et colaphis cædimur, tanquam blasphemi. Et instabiles sumus, fugiendo de loco ad locum : juxta illud, Quum persecuti vos fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam. Et laboramus operantes manibus nostris pro victu atque vestitu. Maledicimur a perversis, et benedicimus, id est, bona eis dicimus, prædicando ipsis verbum salutis. Persecutionem patimur propter justitiam, et sustinemus libenter amore Christi. Ibant enim Apostoli gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati. Blasphemamur, id est, crimen blasphemiæ nobis imponitur, et obsecramus Deum pro blasphemantibus. Tanquam purgamenta hujus mundi facti sumus, id est, reputamur a perfidis quasi immunditiæ quædam, inficientes hunc mundum nostra doctrina. Idcirco quum occidimur, putant mundum purgari ab hominibus pestilentibus : sicque efficimur mundi purgamenta. Factique sumus omnium peripsema usque adhuc, id est velut superfluitas quædam generis humani, ita ut apti non simus hominibus sociari, sed tolli. Peripsema autem vocatur purgamentum ferri vel pomi seu alterius rei, illud videlicet quod aufertur a materia rei ut purgetur, sicut est limatura æris aut ligni.
paras.en: [[4:10|We are fools for Christs sake|Nos stulti propter Christum]], that is, for love of Christ we act so that the world thinks us foolish and senseless; [[4:10|but you are wise in Christ|vos autem prudentes estis in Christo]], according to your proud reckoning. [[4:10|we are weak|Nos infirmi]], we are thought weak, and we acknowledge our own weakness; [[4:10|but you are strong|vos autem fortes]], that is, you are virtuous, as you suppose, who think you do not need our help. [[4:10|you are honourable, but we without honour|Vos nobiles, nos autem ignobiles]]. All is said ironically, that the carnal may be put to shame and corrected. For the Apostles were nobler than the Corinthians in flesh and spirit, since they were the seed of Abraham and received [[Rom 8:23|the firstfruits of the Spirit|primitias Spiritus Sancti]]. [[4:11|Even unto this hour|Usque in hanc horam]], that is, constantly, [[4:11|we both hunger and thirst and are naked|et esurimus, et sitimus, et nudi sumus]], that is, we suffer want of food, drink and clothing. So the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Cor 11:27|in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness|In fame et siti, in frigore et nuditate]]. Then was fulfilled the word of Christ which He spoke: [[Matt 9:15|the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then they shall fast|Veniet tempus quum auferetur ab eis sponsus, et tunc jejunabunt]]. [[4:11|and are buffeted|Et colaphis cædimur]], as blasphemers. [[4:11|and have no fixed abode|Et instabiles sumus]], fleeing from place to place, according to the words: [[Matt 10:23|when they shall persecute you in this city, flee into another|Quum persecuti vos fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam]]. [[4:12|And we labour, working with our own hands|Et laboramus operantes manibus nostris]] for food and clothing. [[4:12|We are reviled: and we bless|Maledicimur a perversis, et benedicimus]]: reviled by the perverse, and we bless, that is, speak good to them, preaching to them the word of salvation. [[4:12|We are persecuted: and we suffer it|Persecutionem patimur propter justitiam, et sustinemus]]: we suffer persecution for justice' sake, and bear it gladly for love of Christ. For [[Acts 5:41|they indeed went from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus|Ibant enim Apostoli gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati]]. [[4:13|We are blasphemed|Blasphemamur]], that is, the crime of blasphemy is laid upon us, [[4:13|and we entreat|et obsecramus]] God for those who blaspheme. [[4:13|We are made as the refuse of this world|Tanquam purgamenta hujus mundi facti sumus]], that is, the faithless regard us as a kind of filth, infecting this world with our teaching. So when we are killed, they think the world is cleansed of pestilent men: and so we are made the refuse of the world. [[4:13|the offscouring of all, even until now|Factique sumus omnium peripsema usque adhuc]], that is, as it were the leavings of the human race, so that we are not fit to be in the company of men, but to be removed. Peripsema is the name for the scrapings of iron or of fruit or some other thing, namely what is taken off the material of a thing to clean it, like filings of bronze or wood.

paras.t: Non ut confundam vos, hæc scribo finaliter. Est autem confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gratiam et gloriam, ut dicitur in Ecclesiastico. De prima confusione loquitur modo Apostolus. Non enim intendebat eos finaliter confundere, sed corrigere, sicut subjungit : sed ut filios meos spirituales carissimos, id est valde dilectos, etsi non propter bonitatem et merita vestra, tamen propter bonitatem divinam, moneo, id est, ad meliora exhortor. Merito autem vocavi vos filios : Nam si decem millia pædagogorum, id est quantamcumque multitudinem erudientium vos, in Christo Jesu, id est in fide et Evangelio Salvatoris, habeatis (dicitur autem pædagogus instructor pueri) ; sed non multos patres spirituales habetis ad hoc, id est genitores qui vos in Christo genuerunt, convertendo vos primo ab esse carnali et infideli, ad esse spirituale atque divinum. Talis autem pater ego fui : Nam in Christo Jesu, id est in esse christiformi seu statu christiano, per Evangelium, id est per evangelicæ sapientiæ prædicationem, ego vos genui instrumentaliter, scilicet ante alios, proponendo vobis Evangelium Christi, et ad fidei susceptionem animas vestras disponendo. Verumtamen unus est Pater noster in cœlo, quem solum debemus Patrem vocare, id est omnis paternitatis efficientiam et gratiam ei præsertim adscribere.
paras.en: [[4:14|I write not these things to confound you|Non ut confundam vos, hæc scribo]] as my end. There is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings grace and glory, as is said in Ecclesiasticus[[Ecclus 4:25||]]. The Apostle speaks now of the first shame. For he did not intend to shame them as an end, but to correct them, as he adds: [[4:14|but I admonish you as my dearest children|sed ut filios meos … carissimos … moneo]]: as my dearest spiritual children, that is, much loved, if not because of your goodness and merits, yet because of the divine goodness, I admonish you, that is, exhort you to better things. And I was right to call you children: [[4:15|For if you have ten thousand instructors in Christ|Nam si decem millia pædagogorum … in Christo Jesu … habeatis]]: ten thousand instructors, that is, however great a number of men teaching you, in Christ Jesus, that is, in the faith and Gospel of the Saviour (a *pædagogus* is the one who teaches a boy); [[4:15|yet not many fathers|sed non multos patres spirituales habetis]], spiritual fathers for this, that is, begetters who begot you in Christ, by first converting you from a carnal and unbelieving being to a spiritual and divine being. Such a father I was: [[4:15|For in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you|Nam in Christo Jesu … per Evangelium … ego vos genui]]: in Christ Jesus, that is, in a Christlike being, or the Christian state; by the gospel, that is, by the preaching of the wisdom of the Gospel; I have begotten you as an instrument, namely before others, by setting the Gospel of Christ before you and disposing your souls to receive the faith. Yet [[Matt 23:9|one is your father, who is in heaven|unus est Pater noster in cœlo]], whom alone we ought to call Father, that is, to whom above all we ought to ascribe the working and grace of all fatherhood[[Eph 3:15||]].

paras.t: Rogo ergo vos, fratres, imitatores mei estote, tanquam boni discipuli obedientesque filii, quatenus sicut ego Christi vestigia sequor, ita vos viam meam, id est virtutes, sequamini. Ideo misi ad vos Timotheum, latorem hujus epistolæ, qui est filius meus carissimus et fidelis in Domino : qui vos commonefaciat, id est, admonendo vos instruat, vias meas, id est præcepta et documenta, quæ sunt in Christo Jesu, id est secundum voluntatem et doctrinam ipsius : in nullo enim a Christo discordo ; sicut ubique in omni Ecclesia doceo.
paras.en: [[4:16|Wherefore, I beseech you, be ye followers of me|Rogo ergo vos, fratres, imitatores mei estote]], brethren, as good disciples and obedient sons, so that [[4:16|as I also am of Christ|sicut ego Christi]]: as I follow in Christ's footsteps, so you may follow my way, that is, my virtues. [[4:17|For this cause have I sent to you Timothy|Ideo misi ad vos Timotheum]], the bearer of this letter, [[4:17|who is my dearest son and faithful in the Lord. Who will put you in mind|qui est filius meus carissimus et fidelis in Domino : qui vos commonefaciat]], that is, will instruct you by admonishing you, [[4:17|of my ways, which are in Christ Jesus|vias meas, quæ sunt in Christo Jesu]]: my ways, that is, precepts and teachings, which are in Christ Jesus, that is, according to His will and teaching: for in nothing do I disagree with Christ; [[4:17|as I teach every where in every church|sicut ubique in omni Ecclesia doceo]].

paras.t: Tanquam non venturus sim ad vos, sic inflati sunt quidam ex vobis tumore superbiæ, gloriantes in eloquentia et doctrina philosophorum : et tam imperterrite sic inflantur, quasi non essem venturus ad vos. Solent autem discipuli a malis retrahi timore adventus magistri. Veniam autem ad vos cito, si Dominus voluerit : cujus voluntas supponenda est semper, juxta illud : Dicatis, Si Dominus voluerit, et, Si vixerimus, faciemus hoc vel illud ; et cognoscam, id est attendam et examinabo, non sermonem rhetoricum eorum qui inflati sunt, sed virtutem, id est, vitam virtuosam an habeant, seu opera miraculorum. Non enim in sermone, id est […] est regnum Dei, id est meritum attingendi ac pertingendi regnum cœlorum, sed in virtute bonæ conversationis consistit. Ait enim Salvator : Non omnis qui dicit mihi, Domine, Domine, intrabit in regnum cœlorum, sed qui facit voluntatem Patris mei ; et rursus, Qui audit verba hæc, et non facit ea, comparabitur viro stulto. Verba enim sine opere, sunt folia sine fructu. Arbor autem quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur et in ignem mittetur.
paras.en: [[4:18|As if I would not come to you, so some are puffed up|Tanquam non venturus sim ad vos, sic inflati sunt quidam]]: some of you are puffed up with the swelling of pride, glorying in the eloquence and teaching of the philosophers; and they are puffed up so fearlessly, as if I were not going to come to you. For disciples are usually held back from evil by fear of their master's coming. [[4:19|But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord will|Veniam autem ad vos cito, si Dominus voluerit]]: whose will must always be presupposed, according to the words: [[Jas 4:15|For that you should say: If the Lord will|Dicatis, Si Dominus voluerit]], and, [[Jas 4:15|If we shall live, we will do this or that|Si vixerimus, faciemus hoc vel illud]] [the margin gives Jac. iv, 13; the words are those of v. 15]; [[4:19|and will know|et cognoscam]], that is, will attend to and examine, [[4:19|not the speech of them that are puffed up, but the power|non sermonem rhetoricum eorum qui inflati sunt, sed virtutem]]: not their rhetorical speech, but their power, that is, whether they have a virtuous life, or works of miracles. [[4:20|For the kingdom of God is not in speech|Non enim in sermone, id est […] est regnum Dei]], that is, […] [a few words are lost in the transcription]; the kingdom of God, that is, the merit of reaching and attaining the kingdom of heaven, does not consist in that, [[4:20|but in power|sed in virtute]] of good conduct. For the Saviour says: [[Matt 7:21|Not every one that saith to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven: but he that doth the will of my Father|Non omnis qui dicit mihi, Domine, Domine, intrabit in regnum cœlorum, sed qui facit voluntatem Patris mei]]; and again, [[Matt 7:26|every one that heareth these my words and doth them not, shall be like a foolish man|Qui audit verba hæc, et non facit ea, comparabitur viro stulto]]. For words without deeds are leaves without fruit. And [[Matt 7:19|Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, shall be cut down, and shall be cast into the fire|Arbor autem quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur et in ignem mittetur]].

paras.t: Quid vultis ? id est, quod ex his duobus eligitis, scilicet, in virga, id est rigore justitiæ et occulto caritatis affectu, videlicet animo disciplinandi, veniam ad vos, an in caritate aperta et spiritu mansuetudinis, id est animo mansueto et indulgenti ? Quamvis hoc secundum sit præoptandum, potius tamen optandum esset primum, quam carere boni patris adventu, quamvis rigoroso. Meliora nempe sunt vulnera diligentis, quam oscula adulantis, ut ait Scriptura.
paras.en: [[4:21|What will you|Quid vultis]]? that is, which of these two do you choose: [[4:21|Shall I come to you with a rod|in virga veniam ad vos]], that is, with the rigour of justice and a hidden affection of charity, namely with a mind to discipline, [[4:21|Or in charity and in the spirit of meekness|an in caritate aperta et spiritu mansuetudinis]], open charity, that is, with a meek and indulgent mind? Although the second is to be preferred, still the first would be more to be wished than to be without the coming of a good father, even a stern one. For, as Scripture says, [[Prov 27:6|Better are the wounds of a friend, than the deceitful kisses of an enemy|Meliora nempe sunt vulnera diligentis, quam oscula adulantis]] [Denis has *adulantis*, "of a flatterer"; a correction in the margin of the edition gives *odientis*, "of an enemy", the Vulgate's word].

paras.t: In præinductis omnibus consideratur discretio sancti Apostoli, qui verbis duris et increpatoriis verba caritativa atque suavia miscet, infundens vinum justitiæ et oleum pietatis, ut sanet animas vulneratas. Virtutes quoque suas tam diligenter describit, non ob propriam laudem, sed ut imitemur semitas ejus.
paras.en: In all that has been brought in, the discretion of the holy Apostle is to be considered, who mixes charitable and sweet words with hard and rebuking ones, pouring in the wine of justice and the oil of kindness, to heal wounded souls. He also describes his own virtues so carefully, not for his own praise, but that we may imitate his paths.

5.title: Expositio capituli quinti: Omnino auditur inter vos fornicatio
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: It is absolutely heard that there is fornication among you
5.note: The end of this article (vv. 12–13) is damaged in the transcription: the beginnings of the lines are lost and have been filled from the sense, in square brackets in the Latin.

paras.t: Accedit demum Apostolus ad particularem increpationem Corinthiorum, et ait : Omnino auditur inter vos fornicatio, id est, omnibus modis scitur, narratur, atque percipitur a me et ab aliis, quod inter vos sit fornicatio (quæ est illicitus concubitus), et talis, id est tam infamis et nefaria fornicatio, qualis nec inter gentes incredulas auditur seu esse percipitur, ita ut uxorem patris sui defuncti aliquis vestrum habeat conjugem. Lyra videtur hæc sic intelligere, quod mulier illa fuerit etiam mater istius ; sed verius creditur quod erat ejus noverca. Talis autem fornicatio, est incestus pœna mortis prohibitus. Unde in Levitico : Qui dormierit cum noverca sua, morte moriatur. Unde et Ruben dicitur in Genesi : Non crescas, quia ascendisti cubile patris tui. Et vos inflati estis tumore elationis, id est, ex superbia neglexistis tantum scelus corrigere, scilicet propter mutuas vestras contentiones, quibus occupati, omittitis opera caritatis ; et non magis luctum, id est compassionem et fletum, habuistis, deplorando tam horrendum piaculum proximi, ut tollatur de medio vestrum, id est, separetur a vobis per excommunicationem, qui hoc opus fecit, cujus omnes participes estis quodammodo, sustinendo talem inter vos.
paras.en: At last the Apostle comes to a particular rebuke of the Corinthians, and says: [[5:1|It is absolutely heard that there is fornication among you|Omnino auditur inter vos fornicatio]], that is, it is known, told and perceived in every way, by me and by others, that there is fornication among you (which is unlawful intercourse), [[5:1|and such fornication as the like is not among the heathens|et talis fornicatio, qualis nec inter gentes]]: such, that is, so infamous and wicked a fornication, as is not heard of or found even among the unbelieving Gentiles, [[5:1|that one should have his father's wife|ita ut uxorem patris sui … aliquis … habeat]]: that one of you should have the wife of his dead father as his wife. Lyra seems to understand this to mean that the woman was also his mother; but it is more truly believed that she was his stepmother. Such fornication is incest, forbidden under pain of death. So in Leviticus: [[Lev 20:11|If a man lie with his stepmother, and discover the nakedness of his father, let them both be put to death|Qui dormierit cum noverca sua, morte moriatur]]. So too it is said to Ruben in Genesis: [[Gen 49:4|grow thou not; because thou wentest up to thy father's bed|Non crescas, quia ascendisti cubile patris tui]]. [[5:2|And you are puffed up|Et vos inflati estis]] with the swelling of pride, that is, out of pride you have neglected to correct so great a crime, namely because of your mutual contentions, busy with which you leave aside the works of charity; [[5:2|and have not rather mourned|et non magis luctum habuistis]], that is, felt compassion and wept, lamenting so horrible a crime of your neighbour, [[5:2|that he might be taken away from among you|ut tollatur de medio vestrum]], that is, be separated from you by excommunication, [[5:2|that hath done this thing|qui hoc opus fecit]], in which all of you share in a way by tolerating such a man among you.

paras.t: Ego quidem Paulus absens a vobis jam corpore, præsens autem spiritu, id est consideratione et animi sollicitudine : sicut et Eliseus præsens erat, quum Giezi accepit munera Naaman Syri ; jam judicavi tanquam præsens spiritu (vel sic : Ac si corporaliter præsens essem) eum qui sic operatus est, id est fornicarium illum. Sic autem judicavi eum, in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, congregatis vobis et meo spiritu, id est, quum collecti fueritis publice in nomine Christi, et in meo spiritu, id est in vera concordia, habendo videlicet spiritum seu caritatis affectum ad invicem, sicut et ego ad vos habeo, cum virtute Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est potestate et auctoritate Christi, qui cooperabitur vobis, tradere hujusmodi Satanæ, id est, ut tradatur talis fornicator diabolo per sententiam excommunicationis : et hoc, in interitum carnis, id est ad hoc ut dæmon eum corporaliter affligat. In primitiva namque Ecclesia, ad fidei confirmationem, solebat excommunicationem sequi corporalis vexatio dæmonis, quousque peccator pœniteret ; et si non pœnitebat, vexabatur quousque animam exhalaret. Hanc potestatem præsertim habebant Apostoli, ut sicut ab obsessis poterant dæmones ejicere, ita enormiter delinquentes poterant dæmoni tradere, corporaliter tribulando. Sed quia hanc corporis pœnam ordinaverunt ad animæ salutem, subditur : ut spiritus salvus sit, id est, anima ejus salva fiat, in die adventus Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est in die judicii universalis, seu particularis vel in die mortis : quod redit in idem. Nam qualis quis moritur, talis Deo in die judicii præsentabitur.
paras.en: [[5:3|I indeed, absent in body but present in spirit|Ego quidem … absens … corpore, præsens autem spiritu]]: I Paul, now absent from you in body, but present in spirit, that is, in thought and care of mind: as Eliseus too was present when Giezi took the gifts of Naaman the Syrian[[4 Kings 5:26||]]; [[5:3|have already judged, as though I were present|jam judicavi tanquam præsens]] in spirit (or thus: as if I were present in body) [[5:3|him that hath so done|eum qui sic operatus est]], that is, that fornicator. And I have judged him so, [[5:4|In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, you being gathered together and my spirit|in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, congregatis vobis et meo spiritu]], that is, when you have been publicly gathered in the name of Christ, and in my spirit, that is, in true concord, namely having the spirit or affection of charity towards one another, as I have towards you, [[5:4|with the power of our Lord Jesus|cum virtute Domini nostri Jesu]], that is, with the power and authority of Christ, who will work with you, [[5:5|To deliver such a one to Satan|tradere hujusmodi Satanæ]], that is, that such a fornicator be delivered to the devil by the sentence of excommunication: and this [[5:5|for the destruction of the flesh|in interitum carnis]], that is, that the demon may afflict him in body. For in the early Church, to confirm the faith, a bodily vexation by the demon used to follow excommunication until the sinner repented; and if he did not repent, he was vexed until he breathed out his soul. This power the Apostles especially had: that just as they could cast demons out of the possessed[[Matt 10:8||]], so they could deliver grave offenders to the demon, afflicting them in body. But since they ordered this bodily punishment to the salvation of the soul, it is added: [[5:5|that the spirit may be saved|ut spiritus salvus sit]], that is, that his soul may be saved, [[5:5|in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ|in die adventus Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], the day of the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, that is, the day of the general judgment, or of the particular judgment, that is, the day of death: which comes to the same thing. For as each one dies, so he will be presented to God on the day of judgment.

paras.t: Ex prædictis concludit Apostolus : Non est bona gloriatio vestra, o Corinthii, qua vel de baptistis et ministris gloriando contenditis, mutuoque præfertis, et ex hoc fraternam correctionem negligitis. Vel, gloriatio qua vos justos jactatis, bona non est, eo quod tantum peccatum inter vos toleretis. Qui enim non corrigit, quum potest et debet, communicat delinquenti, et particeps est peccati. Consequenter ostendit, quam periculosum sit congregationi sustinere perversum. Nescitis quia modicum fermentum, id est parva pars infectiva, totam massam corrumpit, id est, universam materiam inficit ? Sic unum peccatum, seu unus pestilens et perversus, videlicet consensus hujus peccati, et fornicator hujusmodi, totam massam, id est vestram congregationem, contaminat, inficit et seducit, nisi auferatur tale fermentum. Expurgate ergo vetus fermentum, id est, consensum peccati istius et auctorem peccati hujus amovete a vestra communione, ut sitis nova conspersio, id est gratia Baptismatis et virtutum operibus innovati, sicut estis azymi, id est a peccati fermento alieni effecti in fonte Baptismi. Azyma dicitur ab ἀ, quod est sine, et ζύμη, quod est fermentum, quasi sine fermento. Conspersio autem et azyma idem sunt, utpote farina per aquam glutinata sine fermento, sicque significant puritatem a corruptione peccati. Denique in fermento duo pensantur, videlicet : sapor virtualis, quo efficit panem saporosum ; et ita per fermentum signatur doctrina evangelica, ibi quum dicitur : Simile est regnum cælorum fermento, quod acceptum mulier abscondit in farinæ satis tribus, donec fermentatum est totum. Secundo consideratur in fermento corruptio adipis ; et ita significat culpam, quæ alios inficiendo corrumpit : et ita nunc sumitur.
paras.en: From what has been said the Apostle concludes: [[5:6|Your glorying is not good|Non est bona gloriatio vestra]], O Corinthians, by which you contend in glorying about your baptizers and ministers and set them above one another, and for this neglect fraternal correction. Or, the glorying by which you boast that you are just is not good, since you tolerate so great a sin among you. For one who does not correct when he can and ought, shares with the offender and is a partaker of the sin. Next he shows how dangerous it is for a community to tolerate a perverse man. [[5:6|Know you not that a little leaven|Nescitis quia modicum fermentum]], that is, a small infecting part, [[5:6|corrupteth the whole lump|totam massam corrumpit]], that is, infects the whole material? So one sin, or one pestilent and perverse man, namely consent to this sin and such a fornicator, contaminates, infects and leads astray the whole lump, that is, your community, unless such leaven is removed. [[5:7|Purge out the old leaven|Expurgate ergo vetus fermentum]], that is, remove consent to this sin and the author of this sin from your communion, [[5:7|that you may be a new paste|ut sitis nova conspersio]], that is, renewed by the grace of Baptism and the works of the virtues, [[5:7|as you are unleavened|sicut estis azymi]], that is, made strangers to the leaven of sin in the font of Baptism. *Azyma* comes from *a*, which means "without", and *zyme*, which is leaven: as it were "without leaven". *Conspersio* [paste] and *azyma* are the same, namely flour bound with water without leaven, and so they signify purity from the corruption of sin. Lastly, two things are considered in leaven: its strong savour, by which it makes bread tasty, and so leaven signifies the teaching of the Gospel, where it is said: [[Matt 13:33|The kingdom of heaven is like to leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened|Simile est regnum cælorum fermento, quod acceptum mulier abscondit in farinæ satis tribus, donec fermentatum est totum]]. Secondly, the corruption of leaven is considered [the transcription reads *adipis*]; and so it signifies guilt, which corrupts others by infecting them: and it is taken so here.

paras.t: Sitis itaque nova conspersio : Etenim pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus, id est, agnus paschalis pro nostra salute oblatus est Christus : qui loquitur, Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam. De quo ait Joannes : Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. Itemque alibi : Dignus est Agnus qui occisus est. Ipse enim verus est agnus qui abstulit peccata mundi, qui mortem nostram sui ipsius oblatione seu morte destruxit. Ipse quoque est pascha nostrum, id est transitus noster, præbendo nobis exemplum transeundi de hac peregrinatione ad patriam. Propter quod ait : Ego sum via, veritas et vita. Pascha enim transitus dicitur. Hujus Agni figura fuit agnus ille paschalis seu legalis, de quo in Exodo legitur. Unde quod ibi habebatur, Os ejus non confringetis, ab Evangelista allegatur de Christo. Similiter, sicut per effusionem sanguinis agni illius liberabantur filii Israel ab angelo devastante, seu plaga Ægypti, sic nos per effusionem sanguinis Christi liberamur a potestate diaboli et a ruina peccati. Insuper, sicut carnes agni illius manducabantur cum azymis panibus, sic fideles vivere et Christi corpus comedere debent sine fermento peccati. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: So be a new paste: [[5:7|For Christ our pasch is sacrificed|Etenim pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus]], that is, Christ has been offered as the paschal lamb for our salvation: who says, [[Jer 11:19|I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim|Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam]]. Of whom John says: [[John 1:29|Behold the Lamb of God. Behold him who taketh away the sin of the world|Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi]]. And likewise elsewhere: [[Apoc 5:12|The Lamb that was slain is worthy|Dignus est Agnus qui occisus est]]. For He is the true lamb who took away the sins of the world, who destroyed our death by the offering of Himself, that is, by His death. He is also our pasch, that is, our passage, giving us the example of passing over from this pilgrimage to the fatherland. For this reason He says: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas et vita]]. For pasch means passage[[Ex 12:11||]]. The figure of this Lamb was that paschal or legal lamb of which we read in Exodus. So what was said there, [[Ex 12:46|neither shall you break a bone thereof|Os ejus non confringetis]], is cited by the Evangelist of Christ[[John 19:36||]]. Likewise, just as by the shedding of that lamb's blood the children of Israel were set free from the destroying angel, or the plague of Egypt[[Ex 12:22||]][[Ex 12:23||]], so by the shedding of Christ's blood we are set free from the power of the devil and the ruin of sin. Moreover, as the flesh of that lamb was eaten with unleavened bread[[Ex 12:8||]], so the faithful should live and eat the body of Christ without the leaven of sin. So it is added:

paras.t: Itaque epulemur, id est, in Domino deliciemur ac nutriamur, Christi sacramentis vescamur, et ei incorporemur, non in fermento veteri, id est non in iniquitatibus nostris antiquis ac solitis, neque in fermento malitiæ, id est peccato ex deliberatione animi facto (juxta illud : Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso), et nequitiæ, id est non in fraudulenta aliisque nociva conversatione, prout Petrus monet : Deponentes omnem malitiam et dolum et simulationes et invidias ; sed in azymis, id est operibus, sinceritatis, id est internæ puritatis, ut habeamus cor mundum, et veritatis, id est justitiæ, etiam quantum ad proximos ; vel, In azymis veritatis, id est actibus sanctæ contemplationis et illuminatæ cognitionis.
paras.en: [[5:8|Therefore, let us feast|Itaque epulemur]], that is, let us delight and be nourished in the Lord, feed on the sacraments of Christ and be incorporated into Him, [[5:8|not with the old leaven|non in fermento veteri]], that is, not in our old and customary iniquities, [[5:8|nor with the leaven of malice|neque in fermento malitiæ]], that is, sin done with deliberation of mind (according to the words: [[Ps 35:2|The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin|Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso]]), [[5:8|and wickedness|et nequitiæ]], that is, not in a deceitful conduct harmful to others, as Peter warns: [[1 Pet 2:1|laying away all malice and all guile and dissimulations and envies|Deponentes omnem malitiam et dolum et simulationes et invidias]]; [[5:8|but with the unleavened bread|sed in azymis]], that is, the works, [[5:8|of sincerity|sinceritatis]], that is, of inward purity, so that we may have a clean heart, [[5:8|and truth|et veritatis]], that is, of justice, also towards our neighbours; or, in the unleavened bread of truth, that is, in the acts of holy contemplation and enlightened knowledge.

paras.t: Scripsi vobis in epistola. Sciendum quod Apostolus, ante missionem præsentis epistolæ, misit Corinthiis epistolam quamdam, quæ non habetur : in qua jussit ut non miscerentur fornicariis, quod Corinthii non bene intellexerunt, putantes Apostolum loqui de spirituali fornicatione, quæ est idololatria. Ideo nunc exponit verba illic scripta, et ait : Scripsi vobis in epistola (illa quam non habemus), ne commisceamini fornicariis familiaritate, communione, aut cohabitatione : et non utique fornicariis hujus mundi, id est, hoc scripsi, ut non misceamini fornicariis hujus mundi, id est publice criminosis : de quibus subjungitur, aut avaris, aut rapacibus, id est violentis ablatoribus rei alienæ, aut idolis servientibus, id est idololatris, qui tamen Christiani esse volunt. Alioqui debueratis de hoc mundo exisse, id est, si aliter intellexissem quam sic, oporteret vos mundum omnino exire, si velletis mihi acquiescere. Nam si de gentilibus locutus fuissem, non possetis verba mea implere, nisi mundum exeundo, quum ubique demorentur gentiles. Nunc autem scripsi vobis in ista epistola clarius, non commisceri prædictis criminosis Christianis. De infidelibus namque non loquor : quibus etiam quomodo verbum salutis annuntiaretur, si vitarentur? Ideo additur : Si is qui frater, id est, si Christianus, nominatur inter vos fornicator, id est, notorius fornicator fuerit et convictus, aut avarus, aliena tenendo, aut idolis serviens, aut maledicus, id est detractor vel blasphemus, aut ebriosus, aut rapax, vel simili crimine vitiatus, cum hujusmodi nec cibum sumere, sed eum in omnibus evitare, ut erubescendo pœniteat. Unde alibi dicit Apostolus : Subtrahatis vos ab omni fratre ambulante inordinate. Non ergo prohibet cum infidelibus atque gentilibus sumere cibum, præsertim quum alias asserat : Si quis vocat vos infidelium ad cenam, et vultis ire, omne quod vobis apponitur manducate.
paras.en: [[5:9|I wrote to you in an epistle|Scripsi vobis in epistola]]. It must be known that the Apostle, before sending the present epistle, sent the Corinthians a certain epistle which we do not have, in which he commanded that they should not mix with fornicators. The Corinthians did not understand this well, thinking that the Apostle spoke of spiritual fornication, which is idolatry. So he now explains the words written there, and says: I wrote to you in an epistle (that one which we do not have), [[5:9|not to keep company with fornicators|ne commisceamini fornicariis]], by familiarity, communion or living together: [[5:10|I mean not with the fornicators of this world|et non utique fornicariis hujus mundi]], that is, I wrote this, that you should not mix with the fornicators of this world, that is, with public criminals: of whom it is added, [[5:10|or with the covetous or the extortioners|aut avaris, aut rapacibus]], that is, those who violently take away what belongs to others, [[5:10|or the servers of idols|aut idolis servientibus]], that is, idolaters, who yet want to be Christians [Denis takes "the fornicators of this world" as Christians who are public sinners]. [[5:10|otherwise you must needs go out of this world|Alioqui debueratis de hoc mundo exisse]], that is, if I had meant it otherwise, you would have to leave the world altogether if you wished to obey me. For if I had spoken of the Gentiles, you could not fulfil my words except by leaving the world, since the Gentiles live everywhere. [[5:11|But now I have written to you, not to keep company|Nunc autem scripsi vobis non commisceri]]: I have written to you more clearly in this epistle, not to keep company with the criminal Christians mentioned. For I do not speak of unbelievers: how would the word of salvation be preached to them if they were shunned? So it is added: [[5:11|if any man that is named a brother be a fornicator|Si is qui frater, id est, si Christianus, nominatur inter vos fornicator]]: a brother, that is, a Christian, a fornicator, that is, if he is a notorious and convicted fornicator, [[5:11|or covetous|aut avarus]], keeping what belongs to others, [[5:11|or a server of idols or a railer|aut idolis serviens, aut maledicus]], that is, a detractor or blasphemer, [[5:11|or a drunkard or an extortioner|aut ebriosus, aut rapax]], or stained by a like crime: [[5:11|with such a one, not so much as to eat|cum hujusmodi nec cibum sumere]], but to shun him in all things, so that he may be ashamed and repent. So the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Thess 3:6|that you withdraw yourselves from every brother walking disorderly|Subtrahatis vos ab omni fratre ambulante inordinate]]. He does not forbid, then, eating with unbelievers and Gentiles, especially since he asserts elsewhere: [[1 Cor 10:27|If any of them that believe not, invite you, and you be willing to go: eat of any thing that is set before you|Si quis vocat vos infidelium ad cenam, et vultis ire, omne quod vobis apponitur manducate]].

paras.t: Deinceps ostendit Apostolus, quod de infidelibus non habet dare præceptum. Quid enim mihi de his qui foris sunt, id est, quid spectat ad me de infidelibus, qui extra Ecclesiam sunt nomine, numero et re, judicare, id est dare sententiam ut vitentur? Imo potius debet se fidelis illis pie applicare, ut convertantur. Nonne de his qui intus sunt, id est fidelibus, qui intra Ecclesiam sunt nomine vel merito, vos judicatis, et non de his qui foris sunt? quasi dicat : Si vos non judicatis de his qui foris sunt, ita nec ego. Non […] [au]ctoritatem habeo super eos. Nam [eos qui] foris sunt, id est infideles, Deus [judicabit] judicio damnationis, non discus[sionis] […] [se]u disceptationis. Sic enim judicati sunt, juxta illud : Qui non cre[dit, jam] judicatus est, quia non credit in [nomine] unigeniti Filii Dei. […] [Auferte] malum, id est prædictum for[nicatorem] … qui habet uxorem patris sui, [ex vobis] ipsis, id est ex vestra societate. … [Qui] tetigerit picem, inquinabitur. Et [in Deut]eronomio Dominus : Auferes, in[quit, m]alum de medio tui, ut ceteri ti[morem] habeant. Debemus etiam auferre [cogitatio]nes malas et omne peccatum de [cordibus] nostris, prout per Prophetam [Dominus] jubet : Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows that he has no command to give about unbelievers. [[5:12|For what have I to do to judge them that are without|Quid enim mihi de iis qui foris sunt, judicare?]]: that is, what concern is it of mine to judge, that is, to pass sentence that they be shunned, about unbelievers, who are outside the Church in name, number and fact? Rather the faithful man should apply himself to them in kindness, that they may be converted. [[5:12|Do not you judge them that are within|nonne de iis qui intus sunt, vos judicatis?]], that is, the faithful, who are within the Church in name or merit, and not those who are without? As if he said: if you do not judge those who are without, neither do I. [The beginnings of the following lines are lost in the transcription; the gaps are filled here from the sense, as far as they can be.] I have no authority over them. [[5:13|For them that are without, God will judge|Nam … foris sunt … Deus]]: those who are without, that is, unbelievers, God will judge with the judgment of condemnation, not of examination or discussion. For so they have been judged, according to the words: [[John 3:18|he that doth not believe is already judged: because he believeth not in the name of the only begotten Son of God|judicatus est, quia non credit in]]. […] [[5:13|Put away the evil one|malum]], that is, the fornicator already mentioned, … who has his father's wife, [[5:13|from among yourselves|ipsis]], that is, from your company. … [[Ecclus 13:1|He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled|tetigerit picem, inquinabitur]][[Lev 20:11||]] [the margin here gives Levit. xx, 11]. And the Lord in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 19:19|thou shalt take away the evil out of the midst of thee|auferes malum de medio tui]], [[Deut 19:20|That others hearing may fear|ut ceteri timorem habeant]] [the margin gives Deut. xiii, 19, 20; the words are those of Deut 19:19–20]. We ought also to put away evil thoughts and every sin from our hearts, as the Lord commands through the Prophet: [[Is 1:16|take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]].

6.title: Elucidatio capituli sexti: Audet aliquis vestrum habens negotium, etc.?
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: Dare any of you, having a matter against another
6.note: Several lines are lost in the transcription at vv. 12–13 and at the end of the article (v. 20). Please check against the scan.

paras.t: Revocatis Corinthiis ab errore circa matrimonium, jam revocantur ab errore circa judicium, in quo multis modis erraverunt, ut patebit. Audet aliquis vestrum fidelis, ausu temerario, non metuens in hoc Dei offensam, habens negotium, id est causam judicialem, adversus alterum fidelem, judicari apud iniquos, id est pro habendo judicio accedere judices infideles, qui semper adversantur fidelibus, et non apud sanctos, id est, judices fideles non interpellatis? Quod erat multipliciter malum. Dabatur enim per hoc infidelibus occasio opprimendi pauperes Christianos, et aspernandi Ecclesiam, quasi non habentem personas ad judicandum active idoneas. Dabatur quoque infirmis fidelibus occasio reputandi infideles (quum tamen dicat Scriptura : Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus), et occasio redeundi ad idololatriam.
paras.en: Having called the Corinthians back from their error about marriage [so the transcription; the previous chapter concerned incest], he now calls them back from their error about judgment, in which they erred in many ways, as will appear. [[6:1|Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to be judged before the unjust|Audet aliquis vestrum … habens negotium … adversus alterum … judicari apud iniquos]]: does any of you, one of the faithful, dare with rash daring, not fearing to offend God in this, having a matter, that is, a lawsuit, against another of the faithful, go to be judged before the unjust, that is, approach unbelieving judges to have a judgment, who are always hostile to the faithful, [[6:1|and not before the saints|et non apud sanctos]], that is, do you not call on faithful judges? This was bad in many ways. For it gave unbelievers an occasion to oppress poor Christians and to despise the Church, as though it had no persons fit to act as judges. It also gave the weak among the faithful an occasion to esteem unbelievers (though Scripture says: [[Ps 14:4|In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing|Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus]]), and an occasion to return to idolatry.

paras.t: Consequenter ostenditur, quod fideles digniores sunt judicare quam perfidi. An nescitis quoniam, id est quod, sancti, videlicet perfecti, ut Apostoli et apostolici viri, de hoc mundo, id est homines habitantes in hoc mundo inferiori, judicabunt, per assessionem et approbationem? Assidebunt enim Christo, ejusque sententiam omnes electi approbabunt. Unde ait Salvator : Vos qui secuti estis me, sedebitis super sedes duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel. Et Sapiens : Judicabunt justi nationes, et dominabuntur populis. Et si, id est quia, in vobis, id est per sanctos qui inter vos sunt, judicabitur mundus. Est autem mundus perditionis, id est collectio hominum reproborum. De quo mundo ait Christus Apostolis : De mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos [de mun]do : et alibi : Non pro mundo ro[go]. [Est] etiam mundus salvationis. De quo dicitur : Sic Deus dilexit mundum, id est collectionem hominum electorum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret. Sancti ergo judicabunt mundum perditionis judicio reprobationis, sicut et Christus. Mundum vero salvationis judicabunt judicio beatæ præmiationis. Si ergo judicabitis mundum hoc modo, indigni estis qui de minimis judicetis? id est, indigni non estis judicare de parvis et sæcularibus causis : quod patet per locum a majori. Etiam Nescitis (id est, scire vos convenit) quoniam angelos judicabimus? Hoc communiter de angelis apostatis intelligi solet, de quibus scriptum est in Apocalypsi, Draco pugnabat et angeli ejus : quos Sancti cum Christo damnabunt. Sed quoniam dictum est quod omnes electi judicabunt per approbationem sententiæ Judicis, possumus dicere quod homines electi judicabunt etiam angelos sanctos. Pro cujus pleniori intelligentia advertendum, quod meritum et demeritum præmii essentialis, seu pœnæ principalis, non convenit his qui sunt in termino, sed qui in via. Angeli autem boni et mali a principio mundi in termino positi sunt, per inavertibilem conversionem ad Dominum, et inconvertibilem aversionem a Deo, sicut Damascenus declarat. Ergo a principio mundi judicati sunt, quantum ad remunerationem principalem, quæ est vel adeptio vel carentia visionis divinæ essentiæ. Verumtamen, sicut angeli boni in præmio accidentali proficiunt, per hoc quod homines eorum ministerio salvantur, sic angeli mali pœnam accidentalem sibi accumulant, inducendo homines ad peccata. Propterea angeli boni et mali in die judicii judicabuntur, quantum ad præmium meriti accidentalis, illud plene et ultimate percipiendo. Et judicabunt homines electi angelos sanctos judicio approbationis. Quanto magis sæcularia? id est, multo amplius digni sumus judicare causas terrenas et res temporales.
paras.en: Next it is shown that the faithful are worthier to judge than the faithless. [[6:2|Know you not that the saints shall judge this world|An nescitis quoniam … sancti … de hoc mundo … judicabunt]]: that is, that the saints, namely the perfect, like the Apostles and apostolic men, will judge this world, that is, the men who live in this lower world, by sitting with the Judge and approving? For they will sit with Christ, and all the elect will approve His sentence. So the Saviour says: [[Matt 19:28|you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel|Vos qui secuti estis me, sedebitis super sedes duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel]]. And the Wise Man: [[Wis 3:8|They shall judge nations, and rule over people|Judicabunt justi nationes, et dominabuntur populis]]. [[6:2|And if the world shall be judged by you|Et si … in vobis … judicabitur mundus]]: if, that is, since, the world will be judged by you, that is, by the saints who are among you. There is a world of perdition, that is, the gathering of reprobate men. Of this world Christ says to the Apostles: [[John 15:19|you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world|De mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo]]; and elsewhere: [[John 17:9|I pray not for the world|Non pro mundo rogo]] [the ends of these lines are damaged in the transcription]. There is also a world of salvation. Of which it is said: [[John 3:16|God so loved the world|Sic Deus dilexit mundum]], that is, the gathering of the elect, [[John 3:16|as to give his only begotten Son|ut Filium suum unigenitum daret]]. The saints, then, will judge the world of perdition with a judgment of condemnation, as Christ will. But they will judge the world of salvation with a judgment of blessed reward. If, then, you will judge the world in this way, [[6:2|are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters|indigni estis qui de minimis judicetis]]? that is, you are not unworthy to judge small and worldly cases: which is plain by the argument from the greater. [[6:3|Know you not that we shall judge angels|Nescitis quoniam angelos judicabimus?]] (that is, it is fitting that you should know)? This is usually understood of the apostate angels, of whom it is written in the Apocalypse, [[Apoc 12:7|the dragon fought, and his angels|Draco pugnabat et angeli ejus]]: whom the Saints with Christ will condemn. But since it has been said that all the elect will judge by approving the Judge's sentence, we can say that elect men will judge the holy angels too. For a fuller understanding of this it must be noted that merit and demerit of the essential reward, or of the principal punishment, do not belong to those who are at the term [that is, at their final state], but to those on the way. Now the good and bad angels were placed at the term from the beginning of the world, by an unchangeable turning to the Lord and an unchangeable turning away from God, as Damascene declares. So they were judged from the beginning of the world as to the principal reward, which is either the attaining or the lack of the vision of the divine essence. Yet just as the good angels advance in accidental reward through men being saved by their ministry, so the bad angels heap up accidental punishment for themselves by leading men into sin. So the good and bad angels will be judged on the day of judgment as to the reward of accidental merit, receiving it fully and finally. And elect men will judge the holy angels with a judgment of approval. [[6:3|How much more things of this world|Quanto magis sæcularia]]? that is, we are much more worthy to judge earthly cases and temporal things.

paras.t: Sæcularia ergo judicia, id est negotia mundana, si habueritis ; contemptibiles qui sunt in Ecclesia, illos constituite ad judicandum. Propter diligentem considerationem sequentium, cogimur ista dupliciter explanare. Primo, ironice, id est cum ironia seu irrisione, non utique passionata, sed caritativa ac justa, qua ad correctionem irrisi ordinantur. Ut sit sensus : Contemptibiles qui sunt in Ecclesia, id est viros improbos et ceteris viliores, constituite ad judicandum, id est, tales facitis judices. Propter quod fratres coacti sunt interpellare judices infideles. Simili sensu dicitur illud Prophetæ : Immolate laudem de fermento. Ad verecundiam vestram dico, id est, ad vestram confusionem enarro vos ita fecisse. Sic non est (id est, ex vestro facto sequi videtur quod non est) inter vos sapiens quisquam, id est circumspectus quisquam et expertus, qui possit judicare inter fratrem suum, id est inter proximum et proximum fide germanum? Sed frater cum fratre, id est unus fidelium contra alium, in judicio contendit ; et hoc, apud infideles, scilicet judices? — Secundo, exponitur sine ironia, hoc modo : Sæcularia judicia si habueritis ; contemptibiles qui sunt in Ecclesia, id est minus devotos, internos ac deiformes, constituite ad judicandum, id est, hortor ut tales ordinetis judices. Sæpe enim contingit, ut minus contemplativi et spirituales, sint magis activi et in temporalibus aptiores. Ad verecundiam vestram dico, quod non fecistis hoc modo. Dicit autem B. Gregorius : Terrenas causas examinent, qui rerum exteriorum sapientiam perceperunt ; qui vero spiritualibus donis ditati sunt, terrenis non debent negotiis implicari. Augustinus quoque : Christum (ait) testem invoco, quia mallem quotidie aliquid manibus operari, quam tumultuosissimas causarum prolixitates pati.
paras.en: [[6:4|If therefore you have judgments of things pertaining to this world|Sæcularia igitur judicia si habueritis]], that is, worldly business, [[6:4|set them to judge who are the most despised in the church|contemptibiles qui sunt in Ecclesia, illos constituite ad judicandum]]. Because of careful consideration of what follows, we are obliged to explain this in two ways. First, ironically, that is, with irony or mockery, not passionate but charitable and just, by which those mocked are led to correction. So that the sense is: the most despised in the Church, that is, wicked men, viler than the rest, you set to judge, that is, you make such men judges. For this reason the brethren have been forced to call on unbelieving judges. In a like sense the Prophet says: [[Amos 4:5|offer a sacrifice of praise with leaven|Immolate laudem de fermento]]. [[6:5|I speak to your shame|Ad verecundiam vestram dico]], that is, I tell to your confusion that you have done so. [[6:5|Is it so that there is not among you any one wise man|Sic non est inter vos sapiens quisquam]] (that is, it seems to follow from what you have done that there is not), that is, anyone circumspect and experienced, [[6:5|that is able to judge between his brethren|qui possit judicare inter fratrem suum]], that is, between neighbour and neighbour, a brother in faith? [[6:6|But brother goeth to law with brother: and that before unbelievers|Sed frater cum fratre judicio contendit: et hoc apud infideles?]]: that is, one of the faithful against another, and that before unbelieving judges? Secondly, it is explained without irony, in this way: if you have worldly judgments, set to judge the most despised in the Church, that is, those less devout, inward and godlike: that is, I urge you to appoint such men as judges. For it often happens that those less contemplative and spiritual are more active and better fitted for temporal things. I speak to your shame, that you have not done so. Blessed Gregory says: Let those examine earthly cases who have received wisdom about outward things; but those enriched with spiritual gifts should not be entangled in earthly business[[2 Tim 2:4||]]. Augustine too: I call Christ to witness, he says, that I would rather do some work with my hands every day than suffer the most tumultuous lengths of lawsuits.

paras.t: Jam quidem omnino delictum est in vobis, quod judicia habetis inter vos, id est, hoc ipsum vestro peccato agitur, atque peccatum est, quod inter vos negotia judicio determinanda habetis, inter quos quies et pax esse deberent. Unde concludit Augustinus : Peccatum est, judicium habere contra fratrem. Pro cujus sano intellectu habendo, addit paraphrastes : Perfectis licet repetere sua simpliciter, id est sine causa, sine lite, sine judicio; sed non convenit eis inde movere causam ante judicem. Infirmis vero licet repetere sua, causam movendo coram judice, et judicium habendo contra fratrem, sed non contentiose vel fraudulenter, nec apud judices infideles. Sed nec hoc videtur satis resolutum. Ecclesia enim non errat habendo judicia. Religiosis etiam licet sua repetere coram judice; fideles quoque qui in terris sunt infidelium, quum fideles judices habere non valent, ad infideles judices recurrere possunt. Alii igitur dicunt quod liceat, non autem expediat, sæcularia habere judicia; et quod religiosi ac perfecti possunt repetere sua tanquam communia, non ut propria; item, quod fideles inter infideles habitantes, possunt coram judice infideli causam suam movere, si fideles judices non possint habere. Quare non magis injuriam accipitis? id est, cur non potius violentiam manifestam suffertis, quam habeatis judicia litigiosa? Quare non magis fraudem, id est occultam bonorum vestrorum ablationem, seu quamlibet machinationem dolosam, patimini? Simile est quod ait Salvator : Si quis voluerit judicio tecum contendere, et tunicam tuam tollere, dimitte ei et pallium. Rursusque ait : Qui abstulerit tua, noli repetere. Hoc Dominus consulit ad vitandum inquietudinem mentis. Sed vos injuriam facitis aliis, et fraudatis, id est, dolum eis infertis; et hoc, fratribus, id est fidelibus, quibus hoc minus facere congruit : et in hoc pessime facitis.
paras.en: [[6:7|Already indeed there is plainly a fault among you, that you have law suits one with another|Jam quidem omnino delictum est in vobis, quod judicia habetis inter vos]], that is, this very thing comes about by your sin, and is a sin, that you have business among you to be settled by judgment, among whom there should be quiet and peace. So Augustine concludes: It is a sin to have a lawsuit against a brother. For a sound understanding of this the paraphrast [the author of a paraphrase or gloss on the epistle] adds: The perfect may reclaim their goods simply, that is, without a suit, without litigation, without judgment; but it does not befit them to bring a case about it before a judge. The weak may reclaim their goods by bringing a case before a judge and having a lawsuit against a brother, but not contentiously or fraudulently, nor before unbelieving judges. But this does not seem resolved enough either. For the Church does not err in having lawsuits. Religious too may reclaim their goods before a judge; and the faithful who live in the lands of unbelievers, when they cannot have faithful judges, may have recourse to unbelieving judges. Others say, then, that it is lawful but not expedient to have worldly lawsuits; and that religious and the perfect may reclaim their goods as common, not as their own; also, that the faithful living among unbelievers may bring their case before an unbelieving judge if they cannot have faithful judges. [[6:7|Why do you not rather take wrong|Quare non magis injuriam accipitis]]? that is, why do you not rather suffer open violence than have contentious lawsuits? [[6:7|Why do you not rather suffer yourselves to be defrauded|quare non magis fraudem patimini?]]: fraud, that is, the hidden taking away of your goods, or any deceitful scheme? Like this is what the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:40|if a man will contend with thee in judgment, and take away thy coat, let go thy cloak also unto him|Si quis voluerit judicio tecum contendere, et tunicam tuam tollere, dimitte ei et pallium]]. And again He says: [[Luke 6:30|of him that taketh away thy goods, ask them not again|Qui abstulerit tua, noli repetere]]. The Lord counsels this so as to avoid disquiet of mind. [[6:8|But you do wrong and defraud|Sed vos injuriam facitis aliis, et fraudatis]]: you do wrong to others and defraud them, that is, use deceit against them; [[6:8|and that to your brethren|et hoc, fratribus]], that is, to the faithful, to whom it is even less fitting to do this: and in this you do very wickedly.

paras.t: Etenim, An nescitis (quod utique scire vos arbitror) quia iniqui, id est injusti, regnum Dei non possidebunt, id est, terram viventium, seu vitam æternam, non hereditabunt? Justi enim fulgebunt ut sol in regno Patris eorum. Et in Apocalypsi dicitur de injustis : Non intrabit in illam aliquid coinquinatum. Nolite errare, recipiendo falsum pro vero, vel malum pro bono. Neque fornicarii, neque idolis servientes, neque adulteri, neque molles, id est in se ipsos insanientes, provocando vel exercendo libidinem, neque masculorum concubitores, neque fures, neque avari, neque ebriosi, neque maledici, id est detractores, neque rapaces, regnum Dei possidebunt. Et hæc aliquando fuistis, id est, his vitiis subjacuistis ante veram conversionem ad fidem Christi; sed abluti estis a maculis peccatorum in Baptismo; sed sanctificati estis, splendorem gratiæ atque virtutum pulchritudinem recipiendo; sed justificati estis, bene operando, in nomine, id est virtute et invocatione, vel ad honorem nominis, Domini nostri Jesu Christi et in Spiritu Dei nostri, id est operatione Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: For [[6:9|Know you not that the unjust shall not possess the kingdom of God|An nescitis … quia iniqui … regnum Dei non possidebunt]] (which surely I think you know): the unjust, that is, the unrighteous, will not possess the kingdom of God, that is, will not inherit the land of the living, or eternal life? For [[Matt 13:43|the just shine as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father|Justi enim fulgebunt ut sol in regno Patris eorum]]. And in the Apocalypse it is said of the unjust: [[Apoc 21:27|There shall not enter into it any thing defiled|Non intrabit in illam aliquid coinquinatum]]. [[6:9|Do not err|Nolite errare]], by taking the false for the true, or evil for good. [[6:9|Neither fornicators nor idolaters nor adulterers|Neque fornicarii, neque idolis servientes, neque adulteri]], [[6:10|Nor the effeminate|neque molles]], that is, those who rage against themselves, arousing or practising lust, [[6:10|nor liers with mankind nor thieves nor covetous nor drunkards nor railers|neque masculorum concubitores, neque fures, neque avari, neque ebriosi, neque maledici]], that is, detractors, [[6:10|nor extortioners shall possess the kingdom of God|neque rapaces, regnum Dei possidebunt]]. [[6:11|And such some of you were|Et hæc aliquando fuistis]], that is, you were subject to these vices before your true conversion to the faith of Christ; [[6:11|But you are washed|sed abluti estis]] from the stains of sins in Baptism; [[6:11|but you are sanctified|sed sanctificati estis]], receiving the splendour of grace and the beauty of the virtues; [[6:11|but you are justified|sed justificati estis]], by doing well, [[6:11|in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and the Spirit of our God|in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, et in Spiritu Dei nostri]]: in the name, that is, by the power and invocation, or for the honour, of the name; in the Spirit, that is, by the working of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Quoniam vero præinducta verba de non repetendo sua, obscura sunt, exponit modo Apostolus quomodo intelligi debeant. Omnia mihi licent, id est, permittitur mihi omnia mea juste repetere tanquam licitum, sed non omnia expediunt : id est, non semper expedit omnia repetere in foro judiciali : primo, propter conservationem honoris, juxta illud Proverbiorum, Honor est homini qui separat se a contentionibus; secundo, quoniam est majoris boni impeditivum; tertio, propter minimam sollicitudinem atque angustiam animæ : quarto, propter periculum perjurandi, juxta illud Ecclesiastici, Ne contendas cum homine loquace, ne forte constituat tibi litem. Omnia mihi licent : secundum sensum prætactum, quum non sit lege naturali vel scripta prohibitum; […] est, libertatem animæ meæ nolo amittere, subdendo me terrenarum rerum amori ac judicis potestati : quod facerem, si judicio litigarem. Utique meum id defendere mallem, quam perdere rem temporalem. Quod etiam mea repetere licet, patet : Nam, […] debetur […] pro eo […] […] temporalis vitæ sustentatione, et venter indiget escis. Ideo licet temporalia bona repetere, ut habeamus victum et quibus tegamur. Non tamen debemus importune et nimis anxie pro istis contendere, quoniam temporaliter transeunt et venter et esca. Propter quod sequitur: Deus autem et hunc ventrem et hanc escam destruet, quia utrumque naturaliter corruptibile est. Et quamvis venter maneat substantialiter post resurrectionem communem, non tamen secundum statum et pristinum actum. Ideo pro necessitatibus ventris minor esse debet sollicitudo.
paras.en: Since the words brought in above about not reclaiming one's goods are obscure, the Apostle now explains how they should be understood. [[6:12|All things are lawful to me|Omnia mihi licent]], that is, I am permitted to reclaim all my goods justly, as a lawful thing, [[6:12|but all things are not expedient|sed non omnia expediunt]]: that is, it is not always expedient to reclaim everything in a court of law: first, to keep one's honour, according to the words of Proverbs, [[Prov 20:3|It is an honour for a man to separate himself from quarrels|Honor est homini qui separat se a contentionibus]]; second, because it hinders a greater good; third, because of the [not] small care and anguish of soul [the transcription reads *minimam*, "least"; the sense needs "no small"]; fourth, because of the danger of perjury, according to the words of Ecclesiasticus, Do not contend with a talkative man, lest perhaps he set a lawsuit against you[[Ecclus 8:4||]] [the margin reference is unreadable in the transcription; the thought is that of Ecclus 8:4]. [[6:12|All things are lawful to me|Omnia mihi licent]], in the sense already touched on, since it is not forbidden by natural or written law; […] … [the lemma, "but I will not be brought under the power of any", and some lines are lost in the transcription], that is, I do not want to lose the freedom of my soul by subjecting myself to the love of earthly things and to the power of a judge: which I should do if I went to law. I would certainly rather defend what is mine than lose a temporal thing. That it is lawful even to reclaim one's goods is plain: For […] [several lines are lost here, with the beginning of v. 13, "Meat for the belly"] … for the support of temporal life, [[6:13|and the belly for the meats|et venter indiget escis]]: the belly needs food. So it is lawful to reclaim temporal goods, that we may have [[1 Tim 6:8|food and wherewith to be covered|victum et quibus tegamur]]. Yet we must not contend for these importunately and too anxiously, since both belly and food pass away in time. For this reason it follows: [[6:13|but God shall destroy both it and them|Deus autem et hunc ventrem et hanc escam destruet]], because both are by nature corruptible. And although the belly remains in substance after the general resurrection, it does not remain in its state and former act. So there should be less care for the needs of the belly.

paras.t: Præterea redit Apostolus ad id unde cœperat loqui, videlicet ad reprobanda luxuriæ vitia. Corpus autem uniuscujusque fidelis, non fornicationi, sed Domino Deo subjiciatur et obsequatur, et Dominus corpori principetur, et præmium tribuat. Deus vero Pater seu Trinitas, et Dominum Jesum suscitavit tertia die a mortuis; et nos suscitabit in die judicii per virtutem suam omnipotentem, cui non est impossibile omne verbum.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle returns to the point he had begun from, namely to reproving the vices of lust. [[6:13|But the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord: and the Lord for the body|Corpus autem … non fornicationi, sed Domino … et Dominus corpori]]: let the body of every one of the faithful be subject and obedient not to fornication but to the Lord God, and let the Lord rule the body and give it its reward. [[6:14|Now God hath raised up the Lord|Deus vero … et Dominum … suscitavit]]: God the Father, or the Trinity, raised the Lord Jesus from the dead on the third day; [[6:14|and will raise us up also by his power|et nos suscitabit per virtutem suam]] on the day of judgment, by His almighty power, [[Luke 1:37|no word shall be impossible with God|cui non est impossibile omne verbum]].
