paras.t: Ratio autem cur corpus non fornicationi, sed Domino reddendum est, traditur. Nescitis quoniam corpora vestra membra sunt Christi? Ipse enim est caput nostrum, cui in Baptismo incorporamur; et ipsa Ecclesia est mysticum corpus Christi. Ideo quilibet vere christianus, est mysticum membrum ejus. Tollens ergo, id est assumens, seu divino cultui auferens, membra Christi, id est corpus meum et alterius quem ad voluptatem meo exemplo induco, faciam de eis membra meretricis, concumbendo cum ea, sicque una caro fiendo cum carne illius? Absit, ut rem adeo impiam agam. An nescitis quoniam qui adhæret meretrici carnali amore et copula corporali, unum corpus cum ea efficitur, per seminis communionem seu affectuum transformationem? Erunt enim, inquit Dominus in Genesi, duo, id est vir et mulier, in carne una, id est, pro eadem carne reputabuntur propter mutuam unionem, quamvis numeraliter atque realiter aliter differant. Hoc ad litteram de legitime conjunctis prædictum est. Apostolus tamen allegat hic de illicitis copulis fornicantium, quoniam ratio identitatis partim eadem est. Nam concubitus licitus et fornicatio conveniunt in esse naturæ, non autem in esse morali. Qui autem adhæret Domino adhæsione amorosa et obedientiali, unus spiritus est, id est, divino Spiritui per caritatem unitur, in Deum transformatur, eique indissolubiliter colligatur. Unde aiebat Salvator, loquens ad Patrem: Notum feci eis nomen tuum, ut dilectio tua in eis sit, et ego in eis. Amor namque est virtus unitiva diversos conjungens, quamvis essentialiter differant.
paras.en: The reason why the body is to be given not to fornication but to the Lord is given. [[6:15|Know you not that your bodies are the members of Christ|Nescitis quoniam corpora vestra membra sunt Christi]]? For He is our head, into whom we are incorporated in Baptism; and the Church itself is the mystical body of Christ. So every true Christian is a mystical member of His. [[6:15|Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them the members of an harlot|Tollens ergo … membra Christi … faciam … membra meretricis]]: take, that is, take up, or take away from divine worship, the members of Christ, that is, my body and that of another whom I lead into pleasure by my example, and make them the members of a harlot by lying with her, and so becoming one flesh with her flesh? [[6:15|God forbid|Absit]], that I should do so wicked a thing. [[6:16|Or know you not that he who is joined to a harlot is made one body|An nescitis quoniam qui adhæret meretrici … unum corpus … efficitur]]: joined by carnal love and bodily union, he is made one body with her, by the sharing of seed, or the transforming of affections? [[6:16|For they shall be, saith he, two in one flesh|Erunt enim, inquit … duo … in carne una]]: says the Lord in Genesis[[Gen 2:24||]][[Matt 19:5||]], two, that is, man and woman, in one flesh, that is, they will be reckoned as the same flesh because of their mutual union, though they differ in number and in reality. This was said literally of those lawfully joined. Yet the Apostle cites it here of the unlawful unions of fornicators, because the reason for the sameness is partly the same. For lawful intercourse and fornication agree in their natural being, not in their moral being. [[6:17|But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit|Qui autem adhæret Domino, unus spiritus est]]: joined by loving and obedient cleaving, he is one spirit, that is, is united to the divine Spirit by charity, transformed into God and bound to Him inseparably. So the Saviour said, speaking to the Father: [[John 17:26|I have made known thy name to them and will make it known: that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them|Notum feci eis nomen tuum, ut dilectio tua in eis sit, et ego in eis]]. For love is a uniting power that joins different things, though they differ in essence.

paras.t: Fugite fornicationem, id est omnem illicitum concubitum. Quædam peccata in se quamdam pœnam et amaritudinem habent, ut ira, invidia: et ista melius superantur luctando et resistendo. Nam quanto diligentius et particularius considerantur, tanto plus displicent, sicque facilius repelluntur. Alia autem peccata quamdam delectationem includunt, ut gula, luxuria: quæ melius vincuntur fugiendo quam colluctando. Quo enim particularius diligentiusque pensantur et revolvuntur, eo appetitus magis provocatur. Vitanda ergo sunt fomenta, occasiones et causæ luxuriæ. Ratio quoque fugiendi fornicationem subjungitur. Omne enim peccatum, præter fornicationem, quodcumque fecerit homo, cogitando, loquendo vel operando, extra corpus est, id est, non ita nocet corpori, ipsum debilitando, contaminando, ac diversis periculis exponendo, ut fornicatio. Qui autem fornicatur, in corpus suum peccat, ipsum (ut dictum est) lædendo, polluendo et destruendo, præsertim si multum exerceat actum hujusmodi.
paras.en: [[6:18|Fly fornication|Fugite fornicationem]], that is, all unlawful intercourse. Some sins have in themselves a certain pain and bitterness, like anger and envy: and these are better overcome by struggling and resisting. For the more carefully and particularly they are considered, the more they displease, and so the more easily they are driven off. But other sins include a certain pleasure, like gluttony and lust: and these are better overcome by flight than by wrestling. For the more particularly and carefully they are weighed and turned over in the mind, the more the appetite is stirred. So the kindlings, occasions and causes of lust are to be avoided. The reason for fleeing fornication is also added. [[6:18|Every sin that a man doth is without the body|Omne enim peccatum … quodcumque fecerit homo … extra corpus est]]: every sin except fornication, whatever a man does in thought, word or deed, is outside the body, that is, does not so harm the body, weakening it, defiling it and exposing it to various dangers, as fornication does. [[6:18|but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body|Qui autem fornicatur, in corpus suum peccat]], harming, defiling and destroying it (as has been said), especially if he practises such an act much.

paras.t: An nescitis quoniam membra vestra, non solum corpora propter aliqua membra, sed omnia membra vestra, id est corpus totum, templum est Spiritus Sancti, id est consecratum inhabitationi Spiritus Sancti in Baptismo, ubi expulso diabolo, abrenuntiastis pompis ejus, et Deo dicati estis, qui in vobis est per grat[iam], primo atque directe in anima, secu[ndario] autem in corpore? quem Spiritum [San]ctum habetis a Deo Patre, qui misi[t et] dedit fidelibus Spiritum Sanctum, im[o et] a Filio : sed et Spiritus Sanctus da[t se] ipsum. Propter quod ait Christus : Q[uum] venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam [vo]bis a Patre. Et non estis vestri, id [est] proprii juris ac potestatis. Sed totum [quod] habetis et estis, tenemini Deo, ut ad [ejus] honorem et gloriam omnia ordinen[tis]. Nam et de omnibus rationem redder[e debemus], tanquam de bonis mutuatis. Deo qu[oque] debemus nos ipsos, non solum rat[ione] creationis ac gubernationis, sed etiam [ra]tione salvationis. Ideo sequitur : Empti enim estis, id est a potestat[e et] jure diaboli liberati, qui venundati [fui]stis in iniquitatibus vestris, pretio [ma]gno, videlicet morte et sanguine Chr[isti] […]
paras.en: [[6:19|Or know you not that your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost|An nescitis quoniam membra vestra, templum sunt Spiritus Sancti]]: your members, not only the bodies for the sake of some members, but all your members, that is, the whole body, are the temple of the Holy Ghost, that is, consecrated to the dwelling of the Holy Ghost in Baptism, where, the devil having been driven out, you renounced his pomps and were dedicated to God; [[6:19|who is in you|qui in vobis est]] by grace, first and directly in the soul, secondarily in the body? [[6:19|whom you have from God|quem habetis a Deo]]: whom, the Holy Ghost, you have from God the Father, who sent and gave the Holy Ghost to the faithful, and indeed from the Son: and the Holy Ghost too gives Himself. For this reason Christ says: [[John 15:26|when the Paraclete cometh, whom I will send you from the Father|Quum venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis a Patre]] [the ends of these lines are lost in the transcription and have been filled from the sense]. [[6:19|and you are not your own|Et non estis vestri]], that is, of your own right and power. But all that you have and are, you owe to God, so that you may order all things to His honour and glory. For we must also render an account of all things[[Rom 14:12||]], as of goods lent us. We owe ourselves to God too, not only by reason of creation and government, but also by reason of salvation. So it follows: [[6:20|For you are bought|Empti enim estis]], that is, set free from the power and right of the devil, you who were sold for your iniquities[[Is 50:1||]], [[6:20|with a great price|pretio magno]], namely the death and blood of Christ […] [the rest of the article, with the end of v. 20, is lost in the transcription].

7.title: Declaratio capituli septimi: De quibus autem scripsistis mihi
7.title_en: Explanation of the seventh chapter: Now concerning the things whereof you wrote to me
7.note: Text is lost in the transcription at vv. 1–4 and at v. 33. Please check against the scan.

paras.t: De quibus autem scripsistis mihi. Apostolus hoc loco de matrimo[nio] […] Pseudo enim apostoli ut puriores ce[teris] viderentur, magisque eis crederetur, [præ]dicaverunt nuptias esse vitandas. Quo[d au]dito, scripserunt Corinthii Apostolo, c[…] tenendum esset de hoc. Quibus res[pon]det: De quibus autem scripsistis m[ihi], videlicet de nuptiis observandis vel f[ugi]endis, respondeo: Bonum simpliciter […] est perfectum, est bonum non solum […]jugato mulierem non tangere, id est [pe]nitus continere, et in castimonia Dom[ino] ministrare. In carne enim sine carne [vi]vere, non humana, sed angelica vita [est]. De talibus ait Salvator: Sunt eunuchi [qui] se castraverunt propter regnum coelor[um]. De quibus ait Dominus per Isaiam […]
paras.en: [[7:1|Now concerning the things whereof you wrote to me|De quibus autem scripsistis mihi]]. In this place the Apostle […] of matrimony. For the false apostles, so as to seem purer than the rest and to be the more believed, preached that marriage was to be avoided. Hearing this, the Corinthians wrote to the Apostle […] what was to be held on this. He answers them: [[7:1|Now concerning the things whereof you wrote to me|De quibus autem scripsistis mihi]], that is, about whether marriage is to be kept or shunned, I answer: [[7:1|It is good|Bonum]] simply speaking […] is perfect, it is good not only for […] married man [[7:1|not to touch a woman|mulierem non tangere]], that is, to contain altogether, and to minister to the Lord in chastity. For to live in the flesh without the flesh is not a human life but an angelic one. Of such the Saviour says: [[Matt 19:12|there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven|Sunt eunuchi qui se castraverunt propter regnum coelorum]]. Of whom the Lord says by Isaias[[Is 56:4||]] […] [the ends of the lines of this paragraph are lost in the transcription; the words that can be completed with certainty are given, the rest is marked as lost. What follows, the rest of v. 1 and the comment on vv. 2–3, is lost too. The margin's numbers for Isaias were not read; the passage meant is surely Is 56:4–5, the Lord's promise to the eunuchs of a place in His house and a name better than sons and daughters]

paras.t: […]nalem. Cujus ratio subditur: Mulier potestatem plenam et liberam sui corporis non habet, sed vir, quia non potest viro debitum denegare, potestque vir illud exigere. Similiter autem et vir sui corporis potestatem non habet, sed mulier. In lege enim debiti hujus pares sunt, quamvis in aliis mulieres subditæ esse debeant suis maritis.
paras.en: […] [the beginning of this sentence, which ended the gloss on v. 3, is lost; only the last letters of a word, "-nalem", survive]. The reason for this is added: [[7:4|The wife hath not power|Mulier potestatem]], full and free power, [[7:4|of her own body: but the husband|sui corporis non habet, sed vir]], because she cannot refuse the husband the debt, and the husband can demand it. [[7:4|And in like manner the husband also hath not power of his own body: but the wife|Similiter autem et vir sui corporis potestatem non habet, sed mulier]]. For under the law of this debt they are equal, though in other things wives ought to be subject to their husbands.

paras.t: Nolite fraudare, id est corporis usum subtrahere, invicem, nisi forte ex consensu communi, et hoc, ad tempus certum: tempus enim amplexandi, et tempus longe fieri ab amplexibus; ut vacetis, id est, devote insistatis, orationi: quæ est ascensus mentis in Deum: propter quod indiget spirituali elevatione, quæ per actum carnalem maxime impeditur. Etiam post actum talem, sensus manent ad tempus minus idonei ad spiritualia opera. Et iterum, tempore orationis completo, revertimini in id ipsum, id est ad pristinam debiti hujus persolutionem, ne tentet vos Satanas, id est, ne diuturnior elongatio a concubitu, fiat vobis occasio tentationis a dæmone, et incidatis adulterii crimen, propter incontinentiam vestram, id est, eo quod proni sitis ad vitia carnis.
paras.en: [[7:5|Defraud not|Nolite fraudare]], that is, withdraw not the use of the body from, [[7:5|one another|invicem]], [[7:5|except, perhaps, by consent|nisi forte ex consensu]] common to both, and that [[7:5|for a time|ad tempus]] fixed: for there is [[Eccles 3:5|a time to embrace, and a time to be far from embraces|tempus enim amplexandi, et tempus longe fieri ab amplexibus]]; [[7:5|that you may give yourselves|ut vacetis]], that is, devoutly apply yourselves, [[7:5|to prayer|orationi]]: which is the ascent of the mind to God, and so needs a spiritual uplifting, which is hindered most of all by the carnal act. Even after such an act the senses remain for a time less fit for spiritual works. [[7:5|and|Et]] [[7:5|again|iterum]], the time of prayer being completed, [[7:5|return together|revertimini in id ipsum]], that is, to your former paying of this debt, [[7:5|lest Satan tempt you|ne tentet vos Satanas]], that is, lest too long a separation from lying together become for you an occasion of temptation by the devil, and you fall into the crime of adultery, [[7:5|for your incontinency|propter incontinentiam vestram]], that is, because you are prone to the vices of the flesh.

paras.t: Hoc autem, videlicet ut revertamini in id ipsum propter incontinentiam vestram, ne in graviora mala cadatis, dico secundum indulgentiam, id est secundum permissionem seu concessionem. Matrimonium enim ordinatur etiam in remedium culpæ. Hæc videtur intentio Augustini hoc loco. Non secundum imperium, id est, non imperando hæc dico. Non enim necessarium est ad salutem ita reverti: imo melius esset, ex consensu abstinere. Incontinentiæ autem malum est, ut vir uxorem cognoscat ultra necessitatem procreandi liberos, reddendique debitum, nisi faciat hoc ne conjunx in adulterium ruat seu peccet: quia hoc fit ad satisfaciendum concupiscentiæ: quod est veniale, quando concupiscentia sistit intra limites matrimoniales, videlicet quod aliam nolet cognoscere. Si vero limites istos excedat, erit peccatum mortale, quando videlicet tanto impetu fertur, quod etiam, quamvis non esset sua, cognosceret eam. Denique tria sunt bona matrimonii quibus excusatur, videlicet fides quam mutuo conjuges servant, proles religiose educanda, et sacramentum, ne conjugium separetur. Quum igitur actus matrimonialis sit causa prolis generandæ, divinoque cultui mancipandæ, est actus religionis, nec aliquam habet culpam; sed est meritorius, si fiat ex caritate. Similiter si fiat causa reddendi debitum: tunc enim est actus justitiæ.
paras.en: [[7:6|But I speak this|Hoc autem]], namely that you return together for your incontinency, lest you fall into worse evils, [[7:6|by indulgence|dico secundum indulgentiam]], that is, by permission or concession. For matrimony is ordained also as a remedy for sin. This seems to be Augustine's meaning in this place. [[7:6|not by commandment|Non secundum imperium]], that is, I do not say this by way of command. For it is not necessary to salvation to return together so; indeed it would be better to abstain by consent. Now it is the evil of incontinence for a husband to know his wife beyond the need of begetting children and of rendering the debt, unless he does it lest his spouse fall into adultery or sin: for this is done to satisfy concupiscence, which is venial when the concupiscence stays within the bounds of marriage, that is, when he would not wish to know another woman. But if it goes beyond these bounds, it will be a mortal sin: namely when he is carried with such force that he would know her even if she were not his own. Lastly, there are three goods of matrimony by which it is excused [that is, by which the marriage act is cleared of fault]: namely the faith which the spouses keep to each other, offspring to be brought up religiously, and the sacrament, so that the marriage is not broken. Since therefore the marriage act, done for the sake of begetting offspring and devoting it to the worship of God, is an act of religion, it has no fault at all; rather it is meritorious, if it is done out of charity. Likewise if it is done for the sake of rendering the debt: for then it is an act of justice.

paras.t: Volo autem omnes homines esse sicut me ipsum: id est, quantum in me est, mallem omnes simpliciter continere: Omnes, inquam, indeterminate, non singulos; vel, Omnes, si convenienter fieri posset, sicut et ego contineo, qui etiam virgo sum. Sed unusquisque electorum fidelium proprium donum, id est gratiam sibi singulariter datam, habet ex Deo. Unde de quolibet Sancto cantatur: Non est inventus similis illi. Alius quidem sic, alius vero sic, id est, unus habet gratiam secundum hunc perfectionis gradum, alius secundum alium gradum. Idcirco non possunt omnes ad æqualem perfectionem induci: sed uni consulendum est ut in castitate permaneat; alii, ut fidem conjugalem observet: quorum utrumque Dei est donum. Hinc etiam quum Christus de virginitate dissereret, dixit: Non omnes capiunt verbum hoc; et, Qui potest capere, capiat.
paras.en: [[7:7|For I would that all men were even as myself|Volo autem omnes homines esse sicut me ipsum]]: that is, as far as in me lies, I would rather that all contained absolutely: all, I say, taken indefinitely, not each one; or, all, if it could fittingly be done, as I too contain, who am also a virgin. [[7:7|But every one|Sed unusquisque]] of the elect faithful [[7:7|hath his proper gift|proprium donum]], that is, a grace given to him singularly, [[7:7|from God|habet ex Deo]]. Hence it is sung of every Saint: [[Ecclus 44:20|there was not found the like to him|Non est inventus similis illi]] [said of Abraham in Ecclesiasticus, and sung in the Church's Office of Confessors]. [[7:7|one after this manner, and another after that|Alius quidem sic, alius vero sic]], that is, one has grace according to this degree of perfection, another according to another degree. Therefore not all can be brought to equal perfection: but one is to be counselled to remain in chastity, another to keep conjugal faith; and each of the two is a gift of God. Hence too, when Christ was discoursing of virginity, He said: [[Matt 19:11|All men take not this word|Non omnes capiunt verbum hoc]]; and, [[Matt 19:12|He that can take, let him take it|Qui potest capere, capiat]].

paras.t: Dico autem non nuptis, id est virginibus et nondum ligatis, et viduis: Bonum est illis, id est utile et magis meritorium, si sic permanent sicut et ego, id est, omnino contineant. Quod si se non continent, id est, concupiscentiam non refrenant, nubant, matrimonium contrahendo. Melius est enim nubere, quam uri, id est igne libidinis æstuare, angi et vinci. Et est comparatio impropria, velut si dicatur: Melior est angelus quam diabolus. Nubere enim, in se bonum est et sine culpa; uri vero, simpliciter malum.
paras.en: [[7:8|But I say to the unmarried|Dico autem non nuptis]], that is, to virgins and those not yet bound, [[7:8|and to the widows|et viduis]]: [[7:8|It is good for them|Bonum est illis]], that is, profitable and more meritorious, [[7:8|if they so continue, even as I|si sic permanent sicut et ego]], that is, if they contain altogether. [[7:9|But if they do not contain themselves|Quod si se non continent]], that is, do not rein in concupiscence, [[7:9|let them marry|nubant]], by contracting matrimony. [[7:9|For it is better to marry than to be burnt|Melius est enim nubere, quam uri]], that is, to burn with the fire of lust, to be tormented and overcome. And the comparison is an improper one [that is, "better" is not said of two goods, one greater than the other], as if one were to say: An angel is better than a devil. For to marry is good in itself and without fault; but to burn is simply evil.

paras.t: Deinde agit de inseparabilitate matrimonii. His autem qui matrimonio juncti sunt, id est legitime conjugatis, quando uterque fidelis est, præcipio non ego, quasi auctor præcepti, sed Dominus per se ipsum, uxorem a viro non discedere habitatione et toro, causa fornicationis excepta, quæ non exprimitur tanquam notissima. Quam solam Christus excepit: Quicumque, inquiens, uxorem dimiserit, et aliam duxerit, excepta causa fornicationis, mœchatur. Ceteras quippe universas molestias jubet Christus pro fide conjugii et castitate fortiter sustineri, secundum Augustinum. Ait enim Salvator: Quod Deus conjunxit, homo non separet.
paras.en: Next he treats of the indissolubility of matrimony. [[7:10|But to them that are married|His autem qui matrimonio juncti sunt]], that is, to the lawfully married, when both are believers, I command, [[7:10|not I|non ego]], as the author of the precept, [[7:10|but the Lord|sed Dominus]] by Himself, [[7:10|that the wife depart not from her husband|uxorem a viro non discedere]] in dwelling and bed, the cause of fornication excepted, which is not expressed as being very well known. This alone Christ excepted, saying: [[Matt 19:9|whosoever|Quicumque]], [[Matt 19:9|shall put away his wife|uxorem dimiserit]], [[Matt 19:9|and shall marry another|et aliam duxerit]], [[Matt 19:9|except it be for fornication|excepta causa fornicationis]], [[Matt 19:9|committeth adultery|mœchatur]]. All other troubles whatever Christ bids be borne bravely for the faith of marriage and for chastity, according to Augustine. For the Saviour says: [[Matt 19:6|What therefore God hath joined together, let no man put asunder|Quod Deus conjunxit, homo non separet]].

paras.t: Quod si discesserit mulier a viro, causa fornicationis ab ea inexcusabiliter commissæ, præcipit Dominus manere innuptam, id est alteri non posse matrimonialiter copulari, juxta illud: Qui dimissam duxerit, mœchatur; aut viro suo reconciliari: quod fieri potest. Nam sicut vir potest in adulterio deprehensam apud se sub spe correctionis tenere, sic potest repulsam, ad torum amicitiamque recipere. Quamvis autem matrimonium solvatur per fornicationem quantum ad torum, non tamen quantum ad vinculum. Matrimonium enim sic definitur: Matrimonium est personarum legitimarum conjunctio, indivisam vitæ consuetudinem retinens. Porro personæ plene legitimæ sunt, quas non impedit votum continentiæ, ordo, cognatio, dispar cultus, conditio, vel frigiditas. Personæ vero omnino illegitimæ sunt, quas impedit votum, ordo, cognatio, dispar cultus. Personæ vero nec plene legitimæ, nec plene illegitimæ sunt, per conditionem et frigiditatem. Si ergo personæ sunt plene legitimæ, separari non possunt post copulam carnalem, nisi de communi consensu, causa fornicationis excepta. Nam et lepra quamvis dividat conjugatos quantum ad cohabitationem, non tamen simpliciter quantum ad torum.
paras.en: [[7:11|And if she depart|Quod si discesserit]], the wife from the husband, on account of fornication committed inexcusably by her, the Lord commands [[7:11|that she remain unmarried|manere innuptam]], that is, that she cannot be joined in matrimony to another, according to that saying: [[Matt 19:9|he that shall marry her that is put away, committeth adultery|Qui dimissam duxerit, mœchatur]]; [[7:11|or be reconciled to her husband|aut viro suo reconciliari]]: which can be done. For as a husband can keep with him a wife caught in adultery, in hope of her amendment, so he can take back to bed and friendship one he has put away. Now although matrimony is loosed by fornication as to the bed, it is not so as to the bond. For matrimony is defined thus: Matrimony is the union of lawful persons, keeping an undivided partnership of life. Now those persons are fully lawful whom no vow of continence, order, kinship, disparity of worship, condition or frigidity impedes. Those persons are altogether unlawful whom a vow, order, kinship or disparity of worship impedes. And persons are neither fully lawful nor fully unlawful by reason of condition and frigidity [condition: servile condition, unknown to the other party; frigidity: impotence]. If then the persons are fully lawful, they cannot be separated after carnal union except by common consent, the cause of fornication excepted. For leprosy too, though it parts the spouses as to living together, does not simply part them as to the bed.

paras.t: Et vir uxorem non dimittat, nisi ob fornicationem. Nec semper ob fornicationem potest eam dimittere, ut si ipsemet eam prostituit, vel cum alia fornicatus fuerit, vel debitum reddere noluit, vel eam post adulterium manifeste deprehensam tenuerit, vel si mulier est violenter oppressa ab alio, sub specie proprii viri decepta, aut proprium virum probabiliter mortuum æstimans, alteri est conjuncta. Supplendum est hic de viro, quod de muliere prædictum est, scilicet, si discesserit, non ducat aliam, vel reconcilietur uxori.
paras.en: [[7:11|And let not the husband put away his wife|Et vir uxorem non dimittat]], except for fornication. Nor can he always put her away for fornication: as when he himself prostituted her, or has committed fornication with another woman, or would not render the debt, or kept her with him after she had been openly caught in adultery; or if the wife was violently forced by another, or deceived by his passing himself off as her own husband, or was joined to another believing her own husband probably dead. What was said before of the wife must be supplied here of the husband: namely, if he departs, let him not take another, or let him be reconciled to his wife.

paras.t: Consequenter agitur de matrimonio eorum quorum est dispar cultus, ubi videlicet unus est infidelis. Nam ceteris, quorum non est uterque fidelis, ego dico, non imperando, sed consulendo, non Dominus dicit hoc proprie seu immediate, aut imperative. Si quis frater, id est Christianus, uxorem habet infidelem, ita quod eo ad fidem converso, illa in infidelitate permansit: in exordio namque Ecclesiæ multoties alter conjugum convertebatur ad fidem, alio non credente; et hæc uxor infidelis consentit habitare cum illo, sine injuria seu blasphemia fidei, non dimittat illam. Hoc consulo.
paras.en: Next he treats of the matrimony of those of disparate worship, that is, where one is an unbeliever. [[7:12|For to the rest|Nam ceteris]], who are not both believers, [[7:12|I speak|ego dico]], not commanding but counselling; [[7:12|not the Lord|non Dominus]]: the Lord does not say this properly or immediately, or by way of command. [[7:12|If any brother|Si quis frater]], that is, a Christian, [[7:12|hath a wife that believeth not|uxorem habet infidelem]], so that when he was converted to the faith she remained in unbelief (for in the beginning of the Church it often happened that one of the spouses was converted to the faith while the other did not believe), [[7:12|and she consent to dwell with him|et hæc uxor infidelis consentit habitare cum illo]], without injury or blasphemy against the faith, [[7:12|let him not put her away|non dimittat illam]]. This I counsel.

paras.t: Et si qua mulier ad fidem conversa, habet virum infidelem, et hic consentit habitare cum illa pacifice, non dimittat virum. Hujus consilii ratio subditur. Intelligenda tamen sunt hæc, ut aliqui tenent, de his qui in infidelitate contraxerunt; non de his qui in dispari cultu contrahunt, quia tunc non est matrimonium, sed separandi sunt, quemadmodum et Esdras fecit.
paras.en: [[7:13|And if any woman|Et si qua mulier]], converted to the faith, [[7:13|hath a husband that believeth not and he consent to dwell with her|habet virum infidelem, et hic consentit habitare cum illa]] peaceably, [[7:13|let her not put away her husband|non dimittat virum]]. The reason for this counsel is added below. These things, however, are to be understood, as some hold, of those who contracted marriage in unbelief; not of those who contract it in disparity of worship, for then there is no marriage, but they are to be separated, as Esdras also did[[1 Esd 10:1||]].

paras.t: Sanctificatus est enim, id est ad fidem conversus, […] per admonitionem et instructionem, seu optima conversatione uxoris fidelis; et sanctificata est mulier infidelis, scilicet conversa, per virum fidelem. Hoc in primitiva Ecclesia sæpius accidit, ut unus conjugum converteretur ad fidem. Idque ob hanc utilitatem consulit Apostolus ut cohabitent, eo quod cohabitatio sit salutis occasio. Hinc etiam princeps Apostolorum in sua Canonica: Mulieres, inquit, subditæ sint viris suis, ut et si qui non credunt verbo, per mulierum conversationem sine verbo lucrifiant, considerantes in timore sanctam conversationem earum.
paras.en: [[7:14|For the unbelieving husband is sanctified|Sanctificatus est enim]], that is, converted to the faith, […] [some words are lost in the transcription here] through the admonition and instruction, or the excellent conduct, of the believing wife; [[7:14|and the unbelieving wife is sanctified|et sanctificata est mulier infidelis]], that is, converted, [[7:14|by the believing husband|per virum fidelem]]. This happened quite often in the early Church, that one of the spouses was converted to the faith. And for this benefit the Apostle counsels them to live together, because living together is an occasion of salvation. Hence too the prince of the Apostles says in his canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 3:1|let wives|Mulieres]], he says, [[1 Pet 3:1|be subject to their husbands: that, if any believe not the word, they may be won without the word, by the conversation of the wives|subditæ sint viris suis, ut et si qui non credunt verbo, per mulierum conversationem sine verbo lucrifiant]], [[1 Pet 3:2|Considering your chaste conversation with fear|considerantes in timore sanctam conversationem earum]].

paras.t: Alioqui, id est, nisi secundum consilium meum feceritis, pariter habitando, filii vestri, et etiam filiæ, quæ nomine filiorum dantur intelligi, immundi essent, id est, in infidelitate manerent. Si enim fidelis recedit, puer sequitur eum parentem qui manet in domo, et majorem populi partem. Et ita in primitiva Ecclesia, dum pauci erant fideles infidelibus dominis subditi, puer sequebatur ritum parentis infidelis manentis in domo. Imo si secutus fuisset fidelem parentem abeuntem, parens infidelis facile recuperasset eum auxilio infidelium principum. Nunc autem sancti sunt, id est, filii vestri convertuntur ad Christum, vobis simul manentibus. Poterat enim alter conjugum instruere filium.
paras.en: [[7:14|Otherwise|Alioqui]], that is, unless you do according to my counsel by living together, [[7:14|your children|filii vestri]], and daughters too, who are given to be understood under the name of sons [the Latin filii is literally "sons"; the Douay-Rheims has "children"], [[7:14|should be unclean|immundi essent]], that is, would remain in unbelief. For if the believing parent goes away, the child follows the parent who stays in the house, and the greater part of the people. And so in the early Church, while the believers were few and subject to unbelieving masters, the child followed the rite of the unbelieving parent who stayed in the house. Indeed, had he followed the believing parent who went away, the unbelieving parent would easily have got him back with the help of unbelieving princes. [[7:14|but now they are holy|Nunc autem sancti sunt]], that is, your children are converted to Christ while you remain together. For one of the spouses could instruct the child.

paras.t: Præterea advertendum, quod quia causa cohabitationis conjugum disparis cultus, erat spes conversionis errantis, idcirco in primitiva Ecclesia, quando passim convertebantur Judæi atque gentiles, licuit Christianis manere cum uxore seu viro infideli sive gentili, sive Judæa vel Judæo. Procedente autem tempore obduratis Judæis, non licuit fidelibus cohabitare conjugi infideli Judæo. Nunc vero gentilibus quoque obstinatis, non licet alicui infideli conjugi cohabitare. Et in hoc sensu loquuntur sacri canones, cohabitationem conjugum disparis cultus prohibentes. Apostolus vero loquitur pro tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: It is further to be noted that, because the reason for spouses of disparate worship living together was the hope that the one in error would be converted, in the early Church, when Jews and Gentiles were being converted on every side, it was lawful for Christians to remain with an unbelieving wife or husband, whether Gentile or Jewish. But as time went on and the Jews were hardened, it was not lawful for the faithful to live with an unbelieving Jewish spouse. And now, the Gentiles too being obstinate, it is not lawful for anyone to live with an unbelieving spouse. And it is in this sense that the sacred canons speak, which forbid spouses of disparate worship to live together. But the Apostle speaks for the time of the early Church.

paras.t: Quod si infidelis vir aut uxor discedit a fideli ex odio fidei, discedat. Nil enim mali contingit Christiano, sed liberatus est, potestque cum alio contrahere. Non enim est servituti subjectus frater aut soror in ejusmodi, id est, vir aut mulier fidelis non obligatur sequi infidelem discedentem, vel eum repetere, aut a matrimonio fidelis abstinere. In pace autem vocavit nos Deus, id est, ad hoc nos in domo sua, quæ est Ecclesia, posuit, ut pacifice convivamus. Ideo non oportet cum infideli discedente litigare.
paras.en: [[7:15|But if the unbeliever|Quod si infidelis]], husband or wife, [[7:15|depart|discedit]] from the believer out of hatred of the faith, [[7:15|let him depart|discedat]]. For no harm befalls the Christian, but he is set free, and can contract marriage with another. [[7:15|For a brother or sister is not under servitude in such cases|Non enim est servituti subjectus frater aut soror in ejusmodi]], that is, a believing husband or wife is not bound to follow the unbeliever who departs, or to seek him back, or to abstain from marriage. [[7:15|But God hath called us in peace|In pace autem vocavit nos Deus]], that is, He has set us in His house, which is the Church, for this, that we may live together in peace. So there is no need to quarrel with an unbeliever who departs.

paras.t: Deinceps persuadet Apostolus, vel quod non oporteat discedentem sequi, vel quod expediat habitare cum infideli pacifice se habenti. Unde enim scis, o mulier fidelis, si virum infidelem salvum facies, convertendo eum ad fidem? Aut unde scis, o vir fidelis, si mulierem infidelem salvam facies, perducendo eam ad Christum? nisi unicuique sicut Deus divisit, id est, hoc certo sciri non potest, nisi per gratiam specialis revelationis, quam Deus unicuique cui vult dividit, dans uni gratiam ampliorem, alteri vero minorem.
paras.en: Next the Apostle urges either that there is no need to follow the one who departs, or that it is expedient to live with an unbeliever who behaves peaceably. [[7:16|For how knowest thou, O wife|Unde enim scis, o mulier]] who believest, [[7:16|whether thou shalt save thy husband|si virum infidelem salvum facies]] who believes not, by converting him to the faith? [[7:16|Or how knowest thou, O man|Aut unde scis, o vir]] who believest, [[7:16|whether thou shalt save thy wife|si mulierem infidelem salvam facies]], by bringing her to Christ? [[7:17|But as the Lord hath distributed to every one|nisi unicuique sicut Deus divisit]] [Denis takes nisi, which the Douay-Rheims renders "But", as "unless": no one can know this unless God has given it him], that is, this cannot be known for certain except by the grace of a special revelation, which God divides to each one to whom He wills[[Rom 12:3||]][[Rom 12:6||]], giving to one a fuller grace, to another a lesser.

paras.t: Vel sic: Nisi unicuique sicut Deus divisit, id est, nisi cognoscas hoc ex futuro eventu, expectando gratiam, quam Deus singulis tradit, ubi, et quando, et quantum, et quomodo sibi placuerit.
paras.en: Or thus: [[7:17|But as the Lord hath distributed to every one|Nisi unicuique sicut Deus divisit]], that is, unless thou know it from what comes to pass afterwards, waiting for the grace which God gives to each one, where and when and how much and in what way it pleases Him.

paras.t: Ex præinductis autem infert Apostolus commune documentum. Et unumquemque sicut Dominus vocavit, ita ambulet, id est, quilibet fidelium in ea vocatione et statu perseveret et Christo deserviat, in quo a Deo ad fidem vocatus est, scilicet: ut qui in conjugio existens convertitur, maneat in conjugio; qui autem non ligatus convertitur seu vocatur, non contrahat. Hoc est consilium, non præceptum: estque intelligendum, quantum ad ea quæ non repugnant fidei bonisque moribus. Sunt autem conditiones et consuetudines pravæ, in quibus non est ambulandum. Nec idem est dicere, ambulare in statu in quo, et a quo, vocatus est homo. Nam in statu a quo quisquam vocatur, non est standum nec ambulandum, sed in statu in quo. Sicut enim conjux, ita et latro vocatur; sed conjux vocatur in conjugio, latro a latrocinio, quod fidei Christi repugnat, et ob id relinquendum est, non autem conjugium. Per hæc quoque non aufertur licentia tendendi ad status perfectiores. Hæc ergo doceo vos, et sicut in omnibus Ecclesiis doceo, id est, sicut et aliis omnibus prædico: ut sit distributio in genere.
paras.en: From what has gone before, the Apostle draws a general teaching. [[7:17|as God hath called every one: so let him walk|Et unumquemque sicut Dominus vocavit, ita ambulet]], that is, let each of the faithful persevere, and serve Christ, in that calling and state in which he was called by God to the faith: namely, that he who is converted while in marriage should remain in marriage, and he who is converted or called while not bound should not contract it. This is a counsel, not a precept; and it is to be understood of those things which are not contrary to the faith and good morals. For there are wicked conditions and customs in which one must not walk. Nor is it the same to say "to walk in the state in which a man is called" and "in the state from which he is called". For in the state from which anyone is called one must not stand or walk, but in the state in which he is called. For as a married man, so too a robber is called; but the married man is called in marriage, the robber from robbery, which is contrary to the faith of Christ and for that reason must be abandoned, but not marriage. Nor do these words take away leave to strive towards more perfect states. These things, then, I teach you, [[7:17|And so in all churches I teach|et sicut in omnibus Ecclesiis doceo]], that is, as I preach to all others too: so that "all" is distributed by kinds [distributio in genere, a term of logic: "all" is taken of every kind, not of every single one].

paras.t: Hæc insuper per exempla declarat. Circumcisus, id est in ritu Judaico seu statu Judaismi, aliquis vocatus est, id est, ad fidem Christi conversus est? non adducat præputium, id est, non compellatur ritum gentilem assumere seu gentiliter se habere, quantum ad ea quæ non sunt de necessitate salutis. In primitiva enim Ecclesia Judæi et gentiles conversi, in aliquibus observantiis differebant, magis quam postea. In præputio, id est in statu et ritu gentilium, aliquis vocatus est? non circumcidatur, imo nec ad ceteros ritus Judaicos se transferre cogatur. Unde et alibi dicitur: Si circumcidamini, Christus nihil vobis proderit. Servat ergo Apostolus quod congruere videt Ecclesiis tam gentilium quam Judæorum, nec aufert consuetudinem cujus observatio non obest saluti, ut asserit Augustinus.
paras.en: He further makes this plain by examples. [[7:18|being circumcised|Circumcisus]], that is, in the Jewish rite or the state of Judaism, [[7:18|Is any man called|aliquis vocatus est]], that is, converted to the faith of Christ? [[7:18|Let him not procure uncircumcision|non adducat præputium]], that is, let him not be compelled to take up the Gentile rite or to live as a Gentile, in those things which are not of necessity for salvation. For in the early Church converted Jews and Gentiles differed in some observances, more than afterwards. [[7:18|in uncircumcision|In præputio]], that is, in the state and rite of the Gentiles, [[7:18|Is any man called|aliquis vocatus est]]? [[7:18|Let him not be circumcised|non circumcidatur]]; nay, let him not be forced to go over to the other Jewish rites either. Hence it is also said elsewhere: [[Gal 5:2|if you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing|Si circumcidamini, Christus nihil vobis proderit]]. So the Apostle keeps what he sees to suit the Churches both of the Gentiles and of the Jews, and does not take away a custom whose observance does not hinder salvation, as Augustine asserts.

paras.t: Horum autem rationem subjungit: Circumcisio, id est ritus Judaicus, nihil est sub ratione finis, quia nihil proficit ad obtinendam salutem. Legalia enim quantum ad cæremonialia cessaverunt. Est tamen aliquid sub ratione formæ. Simili modo, et præputium, id est status seu ritus gentilis, nihil est, id est, non obest nec prodest saluti. Quod intelligendum est, quantum ad ea quæ indifferentia sunt, non quantum ad opera idololatriæ. Sed observatio mandatorum Dei aliquid est, quoniam promeretur vitam æternam, juxta illud: Si vis ad vitam ingredi, serva mandata; item et illud, Qui servat verbum Christi, vere in hoc caritas Dei perfecta est. Cui consonat illud Sapientiæ: Custoditio legum, consummatio incorruptionis.
paras.en: And he adds the reason for these things: [[7:19|Circumcision|Circumcisio]], that is, the Jewish rite, [[7:19|is nothing|nihil est]] considered as an end, since it profits nothing towards obtaining salvation. For the legal observances, as regards the ceremonial ones, have ceased. Yet it is something considered as a form [that is, as an outward rite it is still a thing, though it no longer leads to salvation]. In like manner [[7:19|and uncircumcision|et præputium]], that is, the Gentile state or rite, [[7:19|is nothing|nihil est]], that is, it neither hinders nor helps salvation. This is to be understood of things indifferent, not of works of idolatry. [[7:19|but the observance of the commandments of God|Sed observatio mandatorum Dei]] is something, since it merits eternal life, according to that saying: [[Matt 19:17|if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments|Si vis ad vitam ingredi, serva mandata]]; and that one too: [[1 John 2:5|he that keepeth|Qui servat]] the word of Christ, [[1 John 2:5|in him in very deed the charity of God is perfected|vere in hoc caritas Dei perfecta est]]. With which agrees that saying of Wisdom: [[Wis 6:19|the keeping of her laws is the firm foundation of incorruption|Custoditio legum, consummatio incorruptionis]].

paras.t: Hinc concludit Apostolus: Unusquisque in qua vocatione vocatus est, in ea permaneat. Cujus intellectus patet ex prædictis. Intellectus tamen verbi hujus diligenter pensandus est: quoniam multi male intelligunt, et per consequens nec intelligunt (quia falsum nescitur), et impertinenter allegant hoc verbum, quasi non debeat homo æmulari charismata meliora. Verba sancti Apostoli sicut in stilo simplicia sunt, ita in sensu profunda consistunt, quia ex corde doctissimo profluxerunt. His autem quæ nunc de circumcisione et præputio dicta sunt, consonat quod ad Galatas scribitur: In Christo Jesu nec circumcisio aliquid valet, nec præputium, sed nova creatura.
paras.en: Hence the Apostle concludes: [[7:20|Let every man abide in the same calling in which he was called|Unusquisque in qua vocatione vocatus est, in ea permaneat]]. Its meaning is plain from what has been said. Yet the meaning of this saying must be weighed with care: for many understand it wrongly, and so do not understand it at all (since what is false is not known), and bring up this saying beside the point, as though a man ought not to [[1 Cor 12:31|be zealous for the better gifts|æmulari charismata meliora]]. "The words of the holy Apostle, as they are simple in style, so they are deep in sense" [printed in italics, as a quotation; no source is named], for they flowed from a most learned heart. And with what has now been said of circumcision and uncircumcision agrees what is written to the Galatians: [[Gal 6:15|in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision: but a new creature|In Christo Jesu nec circumcisio aliquid valet, nec præputium, sed nova creatura]].

paras.t: Post introductionem exempli de ritu vivendi, ponitur exemplum de statu seu officio conditionis. Servus, id est in servitute hominum exsistens, vocatus es ad fidem vel opera bona? Non sit tibi cura, id est, non doleas de servitutis conditione, nec cupias eam effugere. Sed etsi potes liber fieri, id est a servitute hac liberari, magis utere servitute, id est, potius elige in servitute manere, quoniam est tibi occasio humilitatis, ad veram atque in Domino exsistentem libertatem pertinentis. Liberat nempe a servitute peccati, et libertate peccandi. Unde ait S. Ambrosius: Quanto quis propter Deum despectior est in hoc sæculo, tanto sublimius exaltabitur in futuro. Gregorius quoque ait: Tanto est homo pretiosior Deo, quanto propter eum vilior est mundo. Et Boetius: Quum omnis, inquit, fortuna timenda sit, magis tamen prospera quam adversa.
paras.en: After bringing in the example of the rite of living, an example is given of one's state or condition of life. [[7:21|being a bondman|Servus]], that is, living in servitude to men, [[7:21|Wast thou called|vocatus es]] to the faith or to good works? [[7:21|Care not for it|Non sit tibi cura]], that is, do not grieve over the condition of servitude, nor desire to escape it. [[7:21|but if thou mayest be made free|Sed etsi potes liber fieri]], that is, be freed from this servitude, [[7:21|use it rather|magis utere servitute]] [Denis reads "use servitude rather"], that is, choose rather to remain in servitude, since it is for thee an occasion of humility, which belongs to the true freedom, the freedom that is in the Lord. For humility frees from the servitude of sin and from the freedom of sinning. Hence St Ambrose says: The more anyone is despised in this world for God's sake, the more highly will he be exalted in the world to come. Gregory too says: A man is the more precious to God, the viler he is to the world for His sake. And Boethius: Though every fortune, he says, is to be feared, yet prosperous fortune more than adverse.

paras.t: Deinde ponitur ratio hujus exempli. Qui enim in Domino, id est in fide seu opere Dei, vocatus est exsistens servus, id est in conditione servili, loquendo de servitute humana et corporali, libertus est Domini, id est, de servitute peccati liberatus est a Domino, estque servus Domini, et per consequens vere et spiritualiter liber, quoniam Deo servire, regnare est: sicut et beatissima Agatha dixit, Summa ingenuitas est servitus Christi. Facit enim liberum ab obligatione peccati et servitute diaboli. Ideo quoque Salvator testatur: Si vos Filius liberaverit, vere liberi eritis. Similiter qui vocatus est liber, id est a prædicta servitute humana immunis, servus est Christi, dum ei obedit. Unde nec servitus, nec libertas repugnant obsequio Christi. Servitus tamen majoris boni occasio est: non ergo despiciatur a libero. Hinc quoque in Vitis Patrum narratur de quodam sancto Patre, qui nequaquam acquievit a servitute dominorum suorum liberari.
paras.en: Then the reason for this example is given. [[7:22|For he that is called in the Lord|Qui enim in Domino]], that is, in the faith or work of God, [[7:22|being a bondman|vocatus est exsistens servus]], that is, in a servile condition (speaking of human and bodily servitude), [[7:22|is the freeman of the Lord|libertus est Domini]], that is, he has been freed by the Lord from the servitude of sin, and is the servant of the Lord, and so truly and spiritually free, since to serve God is to reign: as the most blessed Agatha also said, The highest nobility is the servitude of Christ. For it makes one free from the bond of sin and from servitude to the devil. Therefore the Saviour too testifies: [[John 8:36|If therefore the son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed|Si vos Filius liberaverit, vere liberi eritis]]. [[7:22|Likewise he that is called, being free|Similiter qui vocatus est liber]], that is, exempt from the human servitude spoken of, [[7:22|is the bondman of Christ|servus est Christi]], while he obeys Him. So neither servitude nor freedom is contrary to the service of Christ. Yet servitude is the occasion of a greater good: so let it not be despised by the free man. Hence too it is told in the Lives of the Fathers of a certain holy Father who would by no means consent to be freed from the servitude of his masters.

paras.t: Pretio, id est pretioso sanguine Christi, empti estis ab obligatione mortis æternæ. Idcirco tam liber quam servus, servi sunt Christi. Emit etiam nos Salvator de manu Dei Patris, qui paratus erat projicere nos in infernum, ut essemus coheredes consortesque sui. Nolite ergo fieri servi hominum, id est, hominibus nolite vos finaliter aut principaliter subdere; sed vicem reddite Salvatori, et ei estote subjecti. Scriptum est enim: Dominum Deum tuum timebis, et illi soli servies. Quod licet de servitute latriæ accipi possit, tamen de omni servitute bona intelligi valet, eo quod quidquid servitutis impenditur homini, propter Deum, in Deo, et secundum Deum impendendum sit illi.
paras.en: [[7:23|with a price|Pretio]], that is, with the precious blood of Christ, [[7:23|You are bought|empti estis]] from the bond of eternal death. Therefore free man and slave alike are servants of Christ. The Saviour also bought us from the hand of God the Father[[Apoc 5:9||]], who was ready to cast us into hell, so that we might be joint heirs[[Rom 8:17||]] and partners with Him. [[7:23|be not made the bondslaves of men|Nolite ergo fieri servi hominum]], that is, do not subject yourselves to men as your last end or chief master; but repay the Saviour in turn, and be subject to Him. For it is written: [[Deut 6:13|Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and shalt serve him only|Dominum Deum tuum timebis, et illi soli servies]]. And though this may be taken of the servitude of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone], it can yet be understood of all good servitude, because whatever servitude is rendered to man must be rendered to him for God's sake, in God, and according to God.

paras.t: Ex his infert Apostolus, quod tamen prædictum est, quatenus repetitio sit confirmationis indicium. Unusquisque in quo vocatus est frater, id est, quilibet frater fidelis in quo statu ad Deum conversus est, in hoc maneat apud Deum, id est, in tali statu studeat Deo digne servire.
paras.en: From these things the Apostle infers what has, however, been said already, so that the repetition may be a mark of confirmation. [[7:24|let every man, wherein he was called|Unusquisque in quo vocatus est]], [[7:24|Brethren|frater]] [Denis reads frater, "brother", where the Vulgate has fratres, and takes it with "every man"], that is, every believing brother, in whatever state he was converted to God, [[7:24|therein abide with God|in hoc maneat apud Deum]], that is, in that state let him strive to serve God worthily.

paras.t: Expleto matrimonii documento, de virginitate agit Apostolus. De virginibus autem, id est de virginitatis atque perpetuæ continentiæ observatione, præceptum Domini non habeo : quoniam nec in veteri, neque in nova lege præcipitur. Imo in veteri lege maledicitur sterilis. In nova vero lege habetur : Qui potest capere, capiat. Consilium autem do de virginitate servanda, quasi de perfectione majori. Quod utique consilium Christus in Evangelio tradit : Si quis, inquiens, venit ad me, et non odit patrem et matrem et uxorem, non potest meus esse discipulus, id est imitator perfectus. Potest tamen esse servus. Itaque, Consilium do, tanquam misericordiam consecutus, id est gratiam apostolatus adeptus, a Domino, ut sim fidelis in officio mihi commisso.
paras.en: Having finished his teaching on marriage, the Apostle treats of virginity. [[7:25|Now, concerning virgins|De virginibus autem]], that is, concerning the keeping of virginity and of perpetual continence, [[7:25|I have no commandment of the Lord|præceptum Domini non habeo]]: since it is commanded neither in the old law nor in the new. Indeed, in the old law the barren woman is accursed[[Deut 7:14||]] [the margin gives “Ibid. vii, 14”, that is Deut. vii, 14, where it is promised that none shall be barren in Israel; Denis gives the sense, not the words]. But in the new law we have: [[Matt 19:12|He that can take, let him take it|Qui potest capere, capiat]]. But [[7:25|I give counsel|Consilium autem do]] concerning the keeping of virginity, as concerning a greater perfection. This counsel Christ indeed gives in the Gospel: [[Luke 14:26|If any man|Si quis]], he says, [[Luke 14:26|come to me, and hate not his father and mother and wife|venit ad me, et non odit patrem et matrem et uxorem]], [[Luke 14:26|he cannot be my disciple|non potest meus esse discipulus]], that is, a perfect imitator; yet he can be a servant. So then: [[7:25|I give counsel, as having obtained mercy|Consilium do, tanquam misericordiam consecutus]], that is, having received the grace of the apostleship, [[7:25|of the Lord, to be faithful|a Domino, ut sim fidelis]] in the office committed to me.

paras.t: Existimo ergo, id est, quum sim apostolus, cujus consilio est credendum, puto, et consulendo affirmo, hoc, videlicet in virginitate et jugi continentia permanere, bonum esse propter instantem necessitatem, id est ad vitandam occupationem conjugatis necessariam : quibus necesse est sollicitari circa temporalem provisionem domus, et prolis atque familiæ. Infirmis et imperfectis infirmam et imperfectam rationem proponit. Poterat enim digniorem causam inducere, videlicet quod status matrimonialis, ratione sollicitudinis sibi adjunctæ, plurimum retrahat a puritate atque fervore, ac stabilitate contemplationis et dilectionis divinæ. Et sicut Augustinus fatetur, virginitas supergreditur conditionem naturæ humanæ : per quam homines angelis assimilantur. Major tamen est victoria virginum, quam angelorum. Angeli enim sine carne vivunt, virgines vero in carne triumphant. Ideo subditur : quoniam bonum est homini sic esse, id est in virginitate manere. Est enim bonum atque honestum, propter vitæ puritatem ; delectabile, propter animi libertatem ; utile, propter copiosam mercedem. Virginibus quippe debetur aureola, et fructus centesimus, ut patet ibi : Sequuntur Agnum quocumque ierit.
paras.en: [[7:26|I think therefore|Existimo ergo]], that is: since I am an apostle, whose counsel is to be believed, I deem, and in counselling I affirm, [[7:26|that this|hoc]], namely to remain in virginity and unbroken continence, [[7:26|is good for the present necessity|bonum esse propter instantem necessitatem]], that is, for avoiding the business that married people cannot escape: for they must needs be anxious about providing temporal things for the house, the children and the household. To the weak and imperfect he puts forward a weak and imperfect reason. For he could have brought in a worthier cause: namely that the married state, by reason of the cares bound up with it, draws a man back very much from purity and fervour, and from steadiness in contemplation and in the love of God. And as Augustine declares, virginity rises above the condition of human nature: by it men are made like the angels. Yet the victory of virgins is greater than that of the angels; for the angels live without flesh, but virgins triumph in the flesh. Therefore he adds: [[7:26|that it is good for a man so to be|quoniam bonum est homini sic esse]], that is, to remain in virginity. For it is good: honourable [Latin honestum: Denis runs through the three kinds of good the schoolmen distinguish, the honourable (good in itself), the delightful and the useful], because of the purity of life; delightful, because of the freedom of the mind; useful, because of the abundant reward. For to virgins is due the aureole [that is, the special crown added in heaven to the essential reward, given to virgins, martyrs and doctors], and the hundredfold fruit[[Matt 13:8||]][[Matt 13:23||]], as is plain from the place where it is said: They [[Apoc 14:4|follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth|Sequuntur Agnum quocumque ierit]].

paras.t: Alligatus es uxori non solum vinculo matrimoniali, sed etiam copula carnali ? noli quærere solutionem, id est separationem a conjuge. Hoc dicit Apostolus, consulendo infirmis, ne incidant culpam majorem. Experti enim delectationem veneream, faciliter revertuntur ad eam. Nihilo minus licet et expedit quærere solutionem causa intrandi religionem, si insit animo firmum continendi propositum, nec aliunde occurrat rationabile impedimentum, videlicet negligentia prolis, vel periculum conjugis, aut simile aliquid. Solutus es ab uxore? id est, si uxorem non habes, noli quærere uxorem, si videris te posse continere.
paras.en: [[7:27|Art thou bound to a wife|Alligatus es uxori]], not only by the bond of marriage but also by carnal union? [[7:27|Seek not to be loosed|noli quærere solutionem]], that is, to be separated from thy spouse. The Apostle says this counselling the weak, lest they fall into a greater fault; for those who have known venereal pleasure easily return to it. Nevertheless it is lawful and expedient to seek to be loosed in order to enter religion [that is, a religious order], if there is in the mind a firm purpose of continence, and no reasonable impediment arises from elsewhere, such as neglect of the children, or danger to the spouse [that is, the danger that the spouse left in the world will fall into sin], or something of the kind. [[7:27|Art thou loosed from a wife?|Solutus es ab uxore?]] that is, if thou hast no wife, [[7:27|Seek not a wife|noli quærere uxorem]], if thou seest that thou art able to be continent.

paras.t: Si autem acceperis uxorem bono fine atque legitime, non peccasti, quum non sit illicitum : imo et bene fecisti. Et si nupserit virgo votum virginitatis non habens, non peccavit. Tribulationem tamen carnis, id est corporalem afflictionem in provisione temporalium rerum, et in variis curis sæculi hujus, habebunt hujusmodi, id est vir et mulier. Ego autem vobis parco, id est, fortiores rationes continendi vobis non profero, quum sitis incapaces et infirmi.
paras.en: [[7:28|But if thou take a wife|Si autem acceperis uxorem]] for a good end and lawfully, [[7:28|thou hast not sinned|non peccasti]], since it is not unlawful; indeed thou hast even done well. [[7:28|And if a virgin marry|Et si nupserit virgo]], not having a vow of virginity, [[7:28|she hath not sinned|non peccavit]]. Nevertheless [[7:28|such shall have|habebunt hujusmodi]], that is, husband and wife, [[7:28|tribulation of the flesh|Tribulationem tamen carnis]], that is, bodily affliction in providing temporal things and in the various cares of this world. [[7:28|But I spare you|Ego autem vobis parco]], that is, I do not set before you the stronger reasons for continence, since you are not able to receive them, and are weak.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Apostolus conjugatis formam vivendi, et ad virginalem perfectionem, quantum fieri potest appropinquandi. Hoc itaque dico, fratres : Tempus peregrinationis nostræ seu vitæ præsentis, breve est, prout Scriptura testatur : Dies nostri sicut umbra super terram, et nulla est mora. Et Jacobus : Quæ est vita vestra? Vapor est ad modicum parens, deinceps exterminabitur. Reliquum est, id est, hoc restat, ut et qui habent uxores, sint tanquam non habentes, id est, non nimis carnaliter afficiantur ad eas, nec actibus carnis totaliter immergantur, sed quantum fieri potest, studeant spiritualibus occupari, intentionemque finalem ad Deum referre.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows the married a form of living, and of drawing near, as far as may be, to virginal perfection. [[7:29|This therefore I say, brethren|Hoc itaque dico, fratres]]: [[7:29|The time|Tempus]] of our pilgrimage, or of the present life, [[7:29|is short|breve est]], as Scripture testifies: [[1 Par 29:15|Our days upon earth are as a shadow, and there is no stay|Dies nostri sicut umbra super terram, et nulla est mora]] [Job viii, 9 says the like, but Denis's words are those of 1 Par. xxix, 15]. And James: [[Jas 4:15|what is your life? It is a vapour which appeareth for a little while and afterwards shall vanish away|Quæ est vita vestra? Vapor est ad modicum parens, deinceps exterminabitur]]. [[7:29|It remaineth|Reliquum est]], that is, this is left: [[7:29|that they also who have wives be as if they had none|ut et qui habent uxores, sint tanquam non habentes]], that is, let them not be too carnally attached to them, nor wholly sunk in the acts of the flesh, but as far as may be let them strive to be occupied with spiritual things, and to refer their final intention to God.

paras.t: Et qui flent, id est tristantur, sint tanquam non flentes, id est, consideratione brevitatis vitæ præsentis, et spe consolationis æternæ respirent, et omnem inordinatam ac sæcularem tristitiam procul abjiciant. Et qui gaudent quocumque modo, sint tanquam non gaudentes, id est, in gaudio hujus vitæ non quiescant, nec illud perfectum reputent : sed potius horam mortis, diem judicii, pœnas inferni, propria mala, totumque mundi peccata pensantes, ingemiscant, et omnem inanem exsultationem contemnant. Unde per Sapientem dicitur : In die malorum, ne immemor sis bonorum; et in die bonorum, ne immemor sis malorum. Et qui emunt, sint tanquam non possidentes, id est, temporalia habeant non quasi semper mansura, sed cito auferenda, saltem in morte; nec inordinate afficiantur ad ea, pensantes quod ait Scriptura : Homo quum dormierit, non sumet omnia ; et, Divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere.
paras.en: [[7:30|And they that weep|Et qui flent]], that is, are sorrowful, let them be [[7:30|as though they wept not|tanquam non flentes]], that is, let them take breath again by considering the shortness of the present life and by the hope of eternal consolation, and cast far from them all inordinate and worldly sorrow. And [[7:30|they that rejoice|Et qui gaudent]] in whatever way, let them be [[7:30|as if they rejoiced not|tanquam non gaudentes]], that is, let them not rest in the joy of this life nor count it perfect, but rather, weighing the hour of death, the day of judgment, the pains of hell, their own evils and the sins of the whole world, let them groan, and despise all empty exultation. Hence it is said by the Wise Man: [[Ecclus 11:27|in the day of evils be not unmindful of good things|In die malorum, ne immemor sis bonorum]]; and [[Ecclus 11:27|in the day of good things be not unmindful of evils|in die bonorum, ne immemor sis malorum]] [Denis gives the two halves of the verse in the reverse order]. And [[7:30|they that buy|Et qui emunt]], let them be [[7:30|as if they possessed not|tanquam non possidentes]], that is, let them hold temporal things not as things that will always remain but as soon to be taken away, at death at least; and let them not be inordinately attached to them, weighing what Scripture says: Man, when he shall sleep, [[Ps 48:18|shall take nothing away|non sumet omnia]] [Denis joins Ps. xlviii, 18, “when he shall die he shall take nothing away”, with Job xxvii, 19, “The rich man when he shall sleep shall take away nothing with him”]; and: [[Ps 61:11|if riches abound, set not your heart upon them|Divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere]].

paras.t: Et qui utuntur hoc mundo, id est divitiis et ceteris rebus creatis, sint tanquam non utantur, id est, non finaliter inhæreant rebus creatis, nec per eas retardentur a Deo, sed pro nihilo reputent cuncta terrena, ut ad Dei fruitionem pertingant. Præterit enim, id est, indesinenter cadit, senescit et variatur, figura hujus mundi, id est dispositio, pulchritudo, et status terrenarum ac temporalium rerum, quæ sunt in transmutatione continua. Propter quod ait Joannes : Et mundus transit, et concupiscentia ejus. Et in Ecclesiaste habetur : Vidi cuncta quæ fiunt sub sole, et ecce universa vanitas et afflictio spiritus. Quidam exponunt de innovatione mundi circa judicium, quando qualitas et modus exsistentiæ rerum mundanarum peribit, non ipsa substantia.
paras.en: [[7:31|And they that use this world|Et qui utuntur hoc mundo]], that is, riches and other created things, let them be [[7:31|as if they used it not|tanquam non utantur]], that is, let them not cleave to created things as to their end, nor be held back from God by them, but count all earthly things as nothing, that they may attain to the enjoyment of God [Latin fruitio: the enjoyment of God as the last end, loved for his own sake, as against the use of creatures, which are loved for his sake]. For [[7:31|the fashion of this world|figura hujus mundi]], that is, the arrangement, beauty and state of earthly and temporal things, which are in continual change, [[7:31|passeth away|Præterit]], that is, unceasingly falls, grows old and changes. Wherefore John says: [[1 John 2:17|And the world passeth away and the concupiscence thereof|Et mundus transit, et concupiscentia ejus]]. And in Ecclesiastes we have: [[Eccles 1:14|I have seen all things that are done under the sun, and behold all is vanity, and vexation of spirit|Vidi cuncta quæ fiunt sub sole, et ecce universa vanitas et afflictio spiritus]]. Some expound this of the renewal of the world at the judgment, when the quality and manner of existence of the things of this world will perish, but not their substance itself.

paras.t: Volo autem vos sine sollicitudine, id est superflua cura circa sensibilia, esse. Hæc enim est sollicitudo mala, impediens libertatem mentis in Deo. De qua dicitur in Proverbiis : Expectatio sollicitorum peribit; et Philippensibus dicitur, Nihil solliciti sitis. Est quoque sollicitudo bona, quæ est vigilantia mentis circa divina. De qua legitur apud Michæam : Indicabo tibi, homo, quid sit bonum : utique sollicitum ambulare cum Deo tuo. Et ad Ephesios : Solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis. De hac sollicitudine subditur : Qui sine uxore est, sollicitus est quæ sunt Domini, id est, circa spiritualia cura ejus versatur, quomodo placeat Deo, id est quatenus corde mentis et animo diligenti obsequatur Domino eique placeat. […]
paras.en: [[7:32|But I would have you to be without solicitude|Volo autem vos sine sollicitudine]], that is, without superfluous care about the things of sense. For this is the evil solicitude, which hinders the freedom of the mind in God. Of it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 11:7|the expectation of the solicitous shall perish|Expectatio sollicitorum peribit]]; and to the Philippians it is said: [[Phil 4:6|Be nothing solicitous|Nihil solliciti sitis]]. There is also a good solicitude, which is the mind's watchfulness about divine things. Of it we read in Micheas: [[Mich 6:8|I will shew thee, O man, what is good|Indicabo tibi, homo, quid sit bonum]]: verily, [[Mich 6:8|to walk solicitous with thy God|sollicitum ambulare cum Deo tuo]]. And to the Ephesians: [[Eph 4:3|Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace|Solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis]] [Latin solliciti, “solicitous”, where the Douay-Rheims has “careful”]. Of this solicitude he goes on: [[7:32|He that is without a wife is solicitous for the things that belong to the Lord|Qui sine uxore est, sollicitus est quæ sunt Domini]], that is, his care is busied about spiritual things: [[7:32|how he may please God|quomodo placeat Deo]], that is, so that with the heart of his mind and a diligent spirit he may serve the Lord and please him. […]

paras.t: sollicitus est quæ sunt mundi, id est, circa temporalia sollicitatur, quomodo placeat uxori, et divisus est, id est animo vagus et affectu partitus : partim quærens placere Deo, partim uxori ; et partim temporalia, partim spiritualia quærens. Hæc idcirco dicit Apostolus, quoniam uxoratus minorem aptitudinem habet serviendi Deo, quam solutus. Sæpe tamen contingit ut conjugati devotiores sint, quam soluti vel etiam religiosi.
paras.en: [[7:33|is solicitous for the things of the world|sollicitus est quæ sunt mundi]], that is, is anxious about temporal things, [[7:33|how he may please his wife. And he is divided|quomodo placeat uxori, et divisus est]], that is, wandering in mind and parted in affection: seeking partly to please God, partly his wife; and seeking partly temporal things, partly spiritual. The Apostle says this because a married man has less aptness for serving God than one who is free. Yet it often happens that married people are more devout than the unmarried, or even than religious.

paras.t: Simili sensu de mulieribus subditur : Et mulier innupta, id est vidua, et virgo, cogitat quæ Domini sunt, id est, divina præcepta revolvit, in lege Domini meditatur, et divina recogitat, ut sit sancta, id est impolluta, munda, et virtutibus perornata, corpore et spiritu, id est anima, quatenus nec corporalia nec spiritualia habeat vitia, sed utrumque divinis obsequiis mancipet. Quæ autem nupta est, cogitat ea quæ sunt mundi, quomodo placeat viro. Unde et ipsa divisa est, sicut maritus, quoniam nullus eorum toto corde intentus est illi uni quod solum necessarium est. Si tamen nihil divinæ dilectioni præponant, vivunt in statu salutis, nec sunt simpliciter a Deo divisi, ut illi qui mortali vitio dividuntur a Deo, de quibus ait per Osee : Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt.
paras.en: In a like sense he adds about women: [[7:34|And the unmarried woman|Et mulier innupta]], that is, the widow, [[7:34|and the virgin thinketh on the things of the Lord|et virgo, cogitat quæ Domini sunt]], that is, turns over the divine precepts, meditates on the law of the Lord, and ponders divine things, [[7:34|that she may be holy|ut sit sancta]], that is, undefiled, clean, and adorned with virtues, [[7:34|both in body and in spirit|corpore et spiritu]], that is, in soul: so that she has vices neither of body nor of spirit, but gives both over to the service of God. [[7:34|But she that is married thinketh on the things of the world: how she may please her husband|Quæ autem nupta est, cogitat ea quæ sunt mundi, quomodo placeat viro]]. Hence she too is divided, like her husband, since neither of them is intent with the whole heart on that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]]. Yet if they put nothing before the love of God, they live in the state of salvation, and are not simply divided from God, like those who are divided from God by mortal sin, of whom he says by Osee: [[Osee 10:2|Their heart is divided: now they shall perish|Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt]].

paras.t: Porro hoc, puta non nubere, ad utilitatem vestram dico, id est, ad majorem profectum vestrum consulo ; non ut laqueum, id est fornicationis occasionem, vobis injiciam, id est proponam. Si enim Apostolus juberet non nubere, daret imperfectis ad vitia carnis proclivibus, occasionem fornicandi. Sed dico et consulo hoc ad id, id est propter id, quod honestum est, scilicet ad continentiam observandam, et quod facultatem præbeat, id est, hominem aptet, sine impedimento, id est sine distractione et molesta sollicitudine, Domino obsecrandi, id est Deum per sacra invocandi. Casta enim vita, efficit hominem aptum ad obsecrandum Dominum mente pura et stabili.
paras.en: [[7:35|And this|Porro hoc]], namely not to marry, [[7:35|I speak for your profit|ad utilitatem vestram dico]], that is, I counsel for your greater progress; [[7:35|not to cast a snare|non ut laqueum]], that is, an occasion of fornication, [[7:35|upon you|vobis injiciam]], that is, to set before you. For if the Apostle were to command not to marry, he would give the imperfect, who are prone to the vices of the flesh, an occasion of fornication. But I say and counsel this [[7:35|for that|ad id]], that is, on account of that, [[7:35|which is decent|quod honestum est]], namely for keeping continence, [[7:35|and which may give you power|et quod facultatem præbeat]], that is, may make a man fit, [[7:35|without impediment|sine impedimento]], that is, without distraction and troublesome solicitude, [[7:35|to attend upon the Lord|Domino obsecrandi]] [Latin obsecrandi, “of beseeching”, which the Douay-Rheims renders “to attend upon”], that is, to call upon God in holy things. For a chaste life makes a man fit to beseech the Lord with a pure and steady mind.

paras.t: Insuper, agit Apostolus de custodibus virginum, quia in primitiva Ecclesia erant patres carnales, et etiam spirituales, ut episcopi, quorum custodiæ virgines committebantur. Si quis autem custos virginum turpem se videri existimat, id est, hoc putat quod ipse aliis turpis videtur, seu male gratiosus, et inhoneste se habens ; vel, Turpem se videri existimat, id est, intra se turpem suspicionem habet ; super virgine sua, id est de virgine suæ custodiæ deputata, quod sit superadulta, id est, idcirco quod virgo jam attigerit annos pubertatis seu nubiles, appareantque in ea probabilia signa quod nubere cupiat, et ita oportet fieri, utpote ut virgo contrahat, eo quod continere non vult ; quod vult virgo, faciat custos ejus, tradens eam marito ; non peccat custos, si nubat virgo.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle treats of the guardians of virgins: for in the early Church there were fathers according to the flesh, and spiritual fathers too, such as bishops, to whose keeping virgins were committed. [[7:36|But if any man|Si quis autem]], a guardian of virgins, [[7:36|think that he seemeth dishonoured|turpem se videri existimat]], that is, thinks that he appears disgraceful to others, or in ill favour, and behaving unbecomingly; or, [[7:36|think that he seemeth dishonoured|Turpem se videri existimat]], that is, harbours within himself a shameful suspicion; [[7:36|with regard to his virgin|super virgine sua]], that is, concerning the virgin assigned to his keeping, [[7:36|for that she is above the age|quod sit superadulta]], that is, because the virgin has now reached the years of puberty, or of marriage, and there appear in her likely signs that she desires to marry, [[7:36|and it must so be|et ita oportet fieri]], namely that the virgin should marry, since she will not be continent: [[7:36|let him do what he will|quod vult virgo, faciat]], that is, let her guardian do what the virgin wills, giving her to a husband; [[7:36|He sinneth not|non peccat]], the guardian, [[7:36|if she marry|si nubat]], the virgin.

paras.t: Nam qui statuit in corde suo firmus, id est, custos virginis, qui stabili proposito mentis ordinavit virginem suam in virginitate servare, non habens necessitatem tradendi eam viro, eo quod velit continere, potestatem autem habens suæ voluntatis, id est de secura custodia virginis, ita quod potest voluntatem suam implere, per hoc quod virgo sibi consentit, et hoc judicavit in corde suo, id est, ex judicio rationis dictavit, servare virginem suam quam custodit, in virginitate, bene facit.
paras.en: [[7:37|For he that hath determined, being steadfast in his heart|Nam qui statuit in corde suo firmus]], that is, the guardian of a virgin who with a steady purpose of mind has resolved to keep his virgin in virginity, [[7:37|having no necessity|non habens necessitatem]] of giving her to a husband, because she wishes to be continent, [[7:37|but having power of his own will|potestatem autem habens suæ voluntatis]], that is, as to the secure keeping of the virgin, so that he can carry out his will, since the virgin consents to him, [[7:37|and hath judged this in his heart|et hoc judicavit in corde suo]], that is, has decided it by the judgment of reason, [[7:37|to keep his virgin|servare virginem suam]] whom he guards, in virginity, [[7:37|doth well|bene facit]].

paras.t: Igitur et qui matrimonio jungit, id est, marito legitimo tradit, virginem suam, bene facit. Facit enim rem licitam. Et qui non jungit virginem viro vinculo matrimoniali, melius facit. Magis enim meritorium est, virginem in virginitate servare, quam maritare, ceteris paribus : quia ad majus bonum cooperatur virgini, qui servat eam in virginitate, quam qui copulat eam viro.
paras.en: [[7:38|Therefore both he that giveth|Igitur et qui matrimonio jungit]], that is, hands over to a lawful husband, [[7:38|his virgin in marriage doth well|virginem suam, bene facit]]: for he does a lawful thing. And [[7:38|he that giveth her not|Et qui non jungit]], that is, does not join the virgin to a husband by the bond of marriage, [[7:38|doth better|melius facit]]. For, other things being equal, it is more meritorious to keep a virgin in virginity than to give her in marriage: since he who keeps her in virginity cooperates with the virgin toward a greater good than he who joins her to a husband.

paras.t: Mulier alligata est viro vinculo conjugali, quia nec potest discedere, nec alteri nubere, quanto tempore vir ejus vivit, id est toto tempore corporalis vitæ sui mariti. Quod si dormierit somno mortis, id est obierit, vir ejus, liberata est a vinculo conjugali. Unde infertur, quod si vir ejus resuscitaretur, non teneretur eum recipere. Qui vero nubat, id est, virum sibi placentem recipiat, si continere non velit, tantum in Domino, id est, secundum voluntatem Dei hoc fiat, videlicet secundum ordinationem Ecclesiæ. Per hoc Apostolus innuit, quod debent nuptiæ esse spontaneæ. Coactæ enim seu invitæ, malum exitum consueverunt sortiri. Propterea in Genesi de Rebecca inducitur : Vocemus puellam, et quæramus ejus voluntatem.
paras.en: [[7:39|A woman is bound|Mulier alligata est]] to her husband [Denis's text reads viro, “to her husband”, where the Vulgate has legi, “by the law”] by the bond of marriage, since she can neither depart nor marry another, [[7:39|as long as her husband liveth|quanto tempore vir ejus vivit]], that is, for the whole time of her husband's bodily life. But [[7:39|if her husband die|Quod si dormierit]] [Latin dormierit, “shall sleep”] the sleep of death, that is, pass away, [[7:39|she is at liberty|liberata est]] from the bond of marriage. Hence it is inferred that if her husband were raised from the dead, she would not be bound to take him back. [[7:39|Let her marry|nubat]] [the text reads Qui vero nubat; the gloss that follows supposes the Apostle's cui vult nubat, “to whom she will”], that is, let her take a husband who pleases her, if she will not be continent, [[7:39|only in the Lord|tantum in Domino]], that is, let this be done according to the will of God, namely according to the ordinance of the Church. By this the Apostle intimates that marriages ought to be free; for forced or unwilling ones commonly come to a bad end. Therefore in Genesis it is related of Rebecca: [[Gen 24:57|Let us call the maid, and ask her will|Vocemus puellam, et quæramus ejus voluntatem]] [the margin gives Gen. xxiv, v; the words are Gen 24:57].
