And Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 24:12|the charity of many|caritas multorum]] [[Matt 24:12|shall grow cold|Refrigescet]]. But it is to be understood as regards the inner perfection of charity: for charity is so perfect that neither the act nor the habit of charity is at odds with the state of the Blessed. Hence they do not come to an end with the present life, but are perfected in the life to come. Then […] the precept of charity will be perfectly fulfilled. It can, however, be understood of the charity of the perfect, who are so confirmed in love and grace that they can say with the Apostle: [[Rom 8:35|Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ|Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi]]?

paras.t: Sive sint prophetiæ, tamen evacuab[un]tur, id est, cessabunt cum vita præse[nti]. Prophetia enim est obscura cognitio, […] concernit futura ; cognitio autem Be[ato]rum est clara, et omnia sunt eis qu[…] præsentia. Sive linguæ, cessabunt esse […] patria. Non quod substantia linguæ […] usus ejus non erit ; nam Sancti in pa[tria] omnia corporis membra habebunt, et […]cali laude atque corporea voce utent[ur], prout probabilius dicitur. Intelligend[um] est ergo, quod donum linguarum ces[sa]bit, quia non habitur in patria alicui u[…] linguarum diversarum ad hoc, ut div[er]sis loquatur linguis, eo quod non om[nes] linguas intelligant : omnes enim om[nes] linguas cognoscent. Et sicut probabil[iter] æstimant aliqui, sicut in primo statu [ge]neris humani erat populus unus et [la]bium unum, ut patet in Genesi, sic[…] ultimo statu erit omnium electorum un[um] idioma. Ad quod applicari potest il[lud] Zachariæ : In die illa erit Dominus un[us] et nomen ejus unum. Sive scientia, [de]struetur : non quantum ad habitum, […] species intelligibiles ; sed quantum ad […]tum et modum agendi, id est quant[um] ad discursum et reflexionem ad phan[ta]smata ; quorum utrumque imperfectio[…] est. Ideo subdimitur :
paras.en: [[13:8|whether prophecies|Sive sint prophetiæ]], yet they [[13:8|shall be made void|evacuabuntur]], that is, they will cease with the present life. For prophecy is a dark knowledge, […] concerns things to come; but the knowledge of the Blessed is clear, and all things are […] present to them. [[13:8|or tongues shall cease|Sive linguæ, cessabunt]] to be […] heaven. Not that the substance of the tongue […] its use will not be; for the Saints in heaven will have all the members of the body, and will use […] praise and the bodily voice, as is more probably said. It is to be understood, then, that the gift of tongues will cease because in heaven no one will have […] [the lost word is probably *usus*, use] of diverse tongues for the purpose of speaking in diverse tongues, because not all understand all tongues: for all will know all tongues. And as some think probable, just as in the first state of the human race there was one people and one speech[[Gen 11:1||]][[Gen 11:6||]], as is clear in Genesis, so […] in the last state there will be one language of all the elect. To which can be applied that saying of Zacharias: [[Zach 14:9|in that day there shall be one Lord|In die illa erit Dominus unus]] [[Zach 14:9|and his name shall be one|et nomen ejus unum]]. [[13:8|or knowledge|Sive scientia]] [[13:8|shall be destroyed|destruetur]]: not as regards the habit, […] the intelligible species; but as regards […] and the manner of acting, that is, as regards discursive reasoning and the turning back to phantasms [*phantasmata*, the images of the imagination from which the mind draws its concepts in this life]; each of which […] imperfection. Therefore it is added:

paras.t: Ex parte enim, id est imperfecte, [co]gnoscimus, et ex parte prophetamus. I[…]que enim cognitio valde incompleta […]. Nam sicut se habet oculus noctuæ ad [lu]men solis, sic intellectus noster se ha[bet] ad manifestissima naturæ, id est ad [co]gnitionem substantiarum separatarum […] maxime Dei sublimis et benedicti ; q[uæ] tamen ex sua natura sunt maxime [co]gnoscibilia, quum sint maxime actu[ales] atque formales.
paras.en: [[13:9|For we know in part|Ex parte enim]], that is, imperfectly, [[13:9|and we prophesy in part|et ex parte prophetamus]]. […] knowledge is very incomplete […]. For as the eye of the owl is to the light of the sun, so is our intellect to the things most manifest in nature, that is, to the knowledge of the separate substances [that is, the angels and God, beings without matter] […] most of all of God, sublime and blessed; which nevertheless are of their own nature most knowable, since they are most fully actual and formal.

paras.t: Quum autem venerit quod […] enim perfectum est, id est, quum in patria fuerit nobis concessa visio Dei per speciem, quæ est perfecta et prorsus purissima ; evacuabitur, id est destruetur, quod ex parte est, id est imperfectio cognoscendi : non habitus cognoscitivus, nec actio ejus perfectionalis ; sed rationativus, quo proceditur a noto ad ignotum per inquisitionem : quod non erit in patria. — Sed circa hoc aliqui movent, quod etiam dilectio nostra est imperfecta, et imperfectio nostra tolletur in patria. Ad quod respondendum, quod licet imperfectio auferatur, directus tamen, immediatus ac proprius actus caritatis non tollitur, sed perficitur in Beatis.
paras.en: [[13:10|But when|Quum autem]] [[13:10|that which|quod]] […] [[13:10|is perfect|perfectum est]] [[13:10|is come|venerit]], that is, when in heaven there shall have been granted us the vision of God by species [*per speciem*: in his own form, not through images], which is perfect and altogether most pure, [[13:10|shall be done away|evacuabitur]], that is, destroyed, [[13:10|that which is in part|quod ex parte est]], that is, the imperfection of knowing: not the habit of knowing, nor its perfecting act, but the reasoning mode [*rationativus*, that is, ratiocinative], by which one proceeds from the known to the unknown by inquiry: this there will not be in heaven. But some raise a difficulty about this: that our love too is imperfect, and our imperfection will be taken away in heaven. To which it must be answered that, although the imperfection is taken away, the direct, immediate and proper act of charity is not taken away, but is perfected in the Blessed.

paras.t: Consequenter Apostolus ponit declarationem istorum per exemplum status puerilis, qui quum sit imperfectus, evacuatur adveniente matura ætate. Quum essem parvulus ætate, sensu et quantitate, loquebar ut parvulus, verba imperfecte pronuntiando ; sapiebam ut parvulus, circa veritatis notitiam sæpe errando ; cogitabam puerilia et jocosa, ut parvulus facere solet. Quando autem factus sum vir ætate et sensu, evacuavi quæ erant parvuli, id est, puerilia dereliqui, et ad perfectionem me transtuli.
paras.en: Next the Apostle makes these things plain by the example of the state of childhood, which, being imperfect, is done away when mature age comes. [[13:11|When I was a child|Quum essem parvulus]] in age, sense and size, [[13:11|I spoke as a child|loquebar ut parvulus]], pronouncing words imperfectly; [[13:11|I understood as a child|sapiebam ut parvulus]], often going astray about the knowledge of the truth; [[13:11|I thought|cogitabam]] childish and playful things, [[13:11|as a child|ut parvulus]] is wont to do. [[13:11|But, when I became a man|Quando autem factus sum vir]] in age and sense, [[13:11|I put away the things of a child|evacuavi quæ erant parvuli]], that is, I left childish things behind and moved on to perfection.

paras.t: Videmus oculo intellectuali, id est, Deum cognoscimus, nunc, id est in præsenti exsilio, per speculum, id est per obscuras imagines, scilicet creatas essentias, quæ Dei naturam imperfecte, imo obscurissime repræsentant. Non enim ostendunt quid Deus sit, sed quid non sit. Nec ostendunt de Deo quid est, sed quia est. Sic ergo videmus per speculum in ænigmate, id est in umbrosa similitudine, utpote in formis intelligibilibus, et Scripturarum signis ac tropis, in quibus modicum quid divinæ lucis resplendet. Omnis namque creata essentia omnisque species intelligibilis intellectum in hac vita perficiens, in infinitum occumbit et velut a perfectione divinæ naturæ latet, idcirco eum repræsentare non potest, nisi obscure et circumvelate. Propter quod divinissimus Dionysius asserit : Impossibile est aliter nobis lucere divinum radium, nisi circumvelatum variis velaminibus sensibilium rerum.
paras.en: [[13:12|We see|Videmus]] with the eye of the intellect, that is, we know God, [[13:12|now|nunc]], that is, in the present exile, [[13:12|through a glass|per speculum]], that is, through dark images, namely created essences, which represent the nature of God imperfectly, indeed most obscurely. For they do not show what God is, but what he is not; nor do they show of God what he is, but that he is. Thus, then, [[13:12|we see|videmus]] [[13:12|through a glass|per speculum]] [[13:12|in a dark manner|in ænigmate]] [*in ænigmate*, literally "in a riddle"], that is, in a shadowy likeness, namely in intelligible forms and in the signs and figures of the Scriptures, in which some small part of the divine light shines out. For every created essence and every intelligible species that perfects the intellect in this life falls infinitely short, and is, as it were, hidden from the perfection of the divine nature; therefore it cannot represent it except darkly and as through a veil. For this reason the most divine Dionysius asserts: It is impossible for the divine ray to shine upon us otherwise than veiled about with the various veils of sensible things.

paras.t: Tunc autem facie ad faciem. Nunc cognosco ex parte, id est imperfecte. Unde in Job dicitur : Ecce hæc ex parte dicta sunt viarum ejus ; et quum vix parvam stillam sermonum ejus audierimus, quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis ejus intueri ? Tunc autem, quum ad patriam venero, cognoscam Deum, sicut et cognitus sum ab eo, id est clare atque per speciem, sicut in prima Joannis Canonica legitur : Quum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est.
paras.en: [[13:12|but then face to face|Tunc autem facie ad faciem]]. [[13:12|Now I know in part|Nunc cognosco ex parte]], that is, imperfectly. Hence it is said in Job: [[Job 26:14|Lo, these things are said in part of his ways: and seeing we have heard scarce a little drop of his word, who shall be able to behold the thunder of his greatness?|Ecce hæc ex parte dicta sunt viarum ejus ; et quum vix parvam stillam sermonum ejus audierimus, quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis ejus intueri]] [[13:12|but then|Tunc autem]], when I come to the fatherland, [[13:12|I shall know|cognoscam]] God [[13:12|even as I am known|sicut et cognitus sum]] by him, that is, clearly and by species [that is, in his very essence, not through images], as we read in the first canonical Epistle of John: [[1 John 3:2|when he shall appear we shall be like to him: because we shall see him as he is|Quum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est]].

paras.t: Sciendum autem, quod Sicut, hoc loco non dicit æqualitatem, sed similitudinem quamdam, quæ consistit in hoc, quod sicut Deus gloriosus et sanctus videt se ipsum per propriam essentiam, ita quod in Deo idem sunt, quod videtur, et quo videtur, seu objectum et species ; sic nos videbimus eum per ipsius essentiam, tanquam per intelligibilem formam nostræ menti immediate, non tamen inhæsive, unitam ; sicque Deus erit nobis quod videbimus, et quo videbimus, seu objectum et species. Nulla namque forma creata tantæ perfectionis est, ut per eam videri possit Deus secundum quod in se ipso subsistit : imo ab hujusmodi divinæ essentiæ repræsentatione deficit infinite. Unde et summi philosophi, tam Platonici quam Peripatetici, dixerunt primam causam non cognosci ab aliqua substantia separata, nisi per negationem, et quia est, ita quod tanto verius perfectiusque cognosceretur Deus ab eis, quanto clarius cernerent Deum penitus invisibilem, inenarrabilem et incomprehensibilem esse. Hoc ergo Apostolus dicit videre Deum facie ad faciem, cognoscere eum sicut cognoscit nos. Videre autem per speciem, tantum est dicere, sicut videre per essentiam. Ad quam beatificam ac superdulcissimam visionem disponitur intellectus creatus in patria immediate per lumen gloriæ, quod est gratia consummata, ponens intellectum in esse deiformi ac deificato.
paras.en: Now it is to be known that [[13:12|even as|Sicut]] here does not express equality, but a certain likeness, which consists in this: that as the glorious and holy God sees himself through his own essence, so that in God that which is seen and that by which it is seen, that is, the object and the species [the *species* is the likeness or form through which the mind knows a thing], are the same; so we shall see him through his own essence, as through an intelligible form united to our mind immediately, yet not as inhering in it; and thus God will be to us that which we shall see and that by which we shall see, that is, object and species. For no created form is of such perfection that God could be seen through it as he subsists in himself: indeed it falls infinitely short of representing the divine essence in this way. Hence even the greatest philosophers, Platonists as well as Peripatetics, said that the first cause is not known by any separate substance [that is, an angel or pure intelligence] except by negation, and that it is; so that God would be known by them the more truly and perfectly, the more clearly they perceived that God is utterly invisible, unutterable and incomprehensible. This, then, is what the Apostle calls seeing God [[13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]] [the margin note beside this line is unreadable], and knowing him as he knows us. And to see by species is as much as to say to see by essence. To this beatific and most surpassingly sweet vision the created intellect is disposed in heaven immediately by the light of glory, which is grace consummated, setting the intellect in a deiform and deified being.

paras.t: Nunc autem, id est tempore viæ et peregrinationis istius, manent in corde fidelium fides, spes, caritas, tria hæc, id est hæ tres virtutes theologicæ, habentes Deum pro immediato objecto. Major autem horum, id est dignior fide et spe, est caritas. Tamen virtutes theologicæ digniores sunt ceteris omnibus donis atque virtutibus.
paras.en: [[13:13|And now|Nunc autem]], that is, in the time of the way and of this pilgrimage, [[13:13|there remain|manent]] in the heart of the faithful [[13:13|faith, hope, and charity, these three|fides, spes, caritas, tria hæc]], that is, these three theological virtues, which have God for their immediate object. [[13:13|but the greatest of these|Major autem horum]], that is, more worthy than faith and hope, [[13:13|is charity|est caritas]]. Yet the theological virtues are worthier than all other gifts and virtues.

14.title: Declaratio capituli quartidecimi: Sectamini caritatem
14.title_en: Explanation of the fourteenth chapter: Follow after charity

paras.t: FACTA determinatione quod caritas major sit ceteris donis, et gratiis gratis datis, nunc hortatur Apostolus ad caritatis imitationem, et gratiarum gratis datarum ponit comparationem, et ait : Sectamini toto cordis affectu caritatem Dei et proximi, quæ una est, quantum ad habitum, eo quod Deus sit finis et ratio diligendi proximum. Caritas ergo sectanda est, ut si non habeatur, studeamus eam acquirere ; si vero habetur, enitamur in ea proficere, et omnia nostra exercitia ad ejus incrementum referre. Ait enim Salvator : In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem. Æmulamini, id est concupiscite, spiritualia dona, videlicet gratias gratis datas, ut aliis proficiatis. Magis autem optate, ut prophetetis, quam ut linguis loquamini, quoniam donum prophetiæ majus est dono linguarum.
paras.en: Having established that charity is greater than the other gifts and than the graces freely given [that is, *gratiæ gratis datæ*: gifts such as prophecy and tongues, given for the good of others rather than for the holiness of the one who receives them], the Apostle now exhorts them to the imitation of charity, and sets out a comparison of the graces freely given, and says: [[14:1|Follow after|Sectamini]] with the whole affection of the heart [[14:1|charity|caritatem]] towards God and neighbour, which is one as regards the habit, because God is the end and the reason of loving our neighbour. Charity, then, is to be followed after: so that, if it is not had, we may strive to acquire it; and if it is had, we may endeavour to advance in it, and refer all our exercises to its increase. For the Saviour says: [[John 13:35|By this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another.|In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem]] [[14:1|Be zealous for|Æmulamini]], that is, desire, [[14:1|spiritual gifts|spiritualia]], namely the graces freely given, that you may profit others. [[14:1|But rather|Magis autem]] desire [[14:1|that you may prophesy|ut prophetetis]] than that you may speak with tongues, because the gift of prophecy is greater than the gift of tongues.

paras.t: Qui enim loquitur lingua, id est, diversis loquelis utitur, sicut per donum linguarum accepit, loquens videlicet lingua ignota et peregrina; vel, Qui loquitur lingua, id est idiomate proprio ac voce sine intellectu eorum quæ dicit, proferens signa quorum signata ignorat; non hominibus loquitur, id est non ad instructionem eorum, sed Deo, id est ad laudem ipsius, vel quia a Deo intelligitur, cujus laudibus instat. Nemo enim audit: idcirco non hominibus loquitur. Nemo enim audit auditu cordis, id est, nullus intelligit quid ille loquatur, quantum est ex virtute locutionis illius. Donum enim linguarum per se non instruit intellectum. Sumitur nempe hoc loco, Loqui linguis, pro locutione non perfecte intellecta, nec satis explanata: sicut purus grammaticus physicam legere potest in Latino, sed non potest eam exponere; et aliquis simplex legit Horas canonicas, quarum sensum non capit. Spiritus autem prophetiæ, id est Spiritus Sanctus per Prophetas, loquitur mysteria, id est divina secreta. Dat enim Prophetis intellectum eorum, ut possint Scripturarum sententias evidenter cognoscere et aliis prædicare: quod est Ecclesiam ædificare. Propterea subditur: Nam qui prophetat, id est, Scripturas exponit, et sensus latentes declarat, hominibus, id est ad profectum hominum, loquitur, scilicet ad ædificationem incipientium, et exhortationem proficientium, et consolationem mæstorum.
paras.en: [[14:2|For he that speaketh in a tongue|Qui enim loquitur lingua]], that is, uses divers speeches, as he has received them through the gift of tongues, speaking namely in an unknown and foreign tongue; or, he that [[14:2|speaketh|loquitur]] [[14:2|in a tongue|lingua]], that is, in his own idiom and with his voice, without understanding what he says, uttering signs whose meaning he does not know: [[14:2|speaketh not unto men|non hominibus loquitur]], that is, not for their instruction, [[14:2|but unto God|sed Deo]], that is, to His praise, or because he is understood by God, on whose praises he is intent. [[14:2|For no man heareth|Nemo enim audit]]: therefore he does not speak to men. For no man hears with the hearing of the heart, that is, no one understands what he is saying, so far as the power of his speech goes; for the gift of tongues does not of itself instruct the understanding. For *to speak with tongues* is taken in this place for speech that is not perfectly understood nor sufficiently explained: as a mere grammarian can read physics in Latin but cannot expound it, and some simple man reads the canonical Hours without grasping their sense. [[14:2|Yet by the Spirit|Spiritus autem]] of prophecy, that is, the Holy Ghost through the Prophets, [[14:2|he speaketh mysteries|loquitur mysteria]], that is, divine secrets [Denis reads *Spiritus*, "the Spirit speaketh mysteries", where the Vulgate has *Spiritu*, "by the Spirit"]. For He gives the Prophets the understanding of them, so that they can know the meanings of the Scriptures clearly and preach them to others: which is to edify the Church. Therefore it is added: [[14:3|But he that prophesieth|Nam qui prophetat]], that is, expounds the Scriptures and declares their hidden senses, [[14:3|to men|hominibus]], that is, for the profit of men, [[14:3|speaketh|loquitur]], namely [[14:3|unto edification|ad ædificationem]] of beginners, [[14:3|and exhortation|et exhortationem]] of those who are advancing, [[14:3|and comfort|et consolationem]] of the sorrowful.

paras.t: Qui loquitur lingua, secundum sensum expositum, semetipsum ædificat, id est, sibimet solum proficit, seque in bono actu exercet, proferendo verba divina, et Deum orando, quamvis sensum non capiat. Qui autem prophetat, Ecclesiam Dei ædificat, sicut nunc dictum est. Prophetare autem, ut patuit, et ut ait Ambrosius, sumitur jam pro eo quod est, visiones divinas sibi vel aliis factas, seu sacras Scripturas divinitus revelatas, per intellectuale lumen menti communicatum exponere.
paras.en: [[14:4|He that speaketh in a tongue|Qui loquitur lingua]], in the sense expounded, [[14:4|edifieth himself|semetipsum ædificat]], that is, profits himself alone, and exercises himself in a good act, by uttering divine words and praying to God, although he does not grasp the sense. [[14:4|But he that prophesieth, edifieth the church|Qui autem prophetat, Ecclesiam Dei ædificat]] [Denis, with the Vulgate, reads "the Church of God"], as has just been said. Now *to prophesy*, as has appeared, and as Ambrose says, is taken here for this: to expound, by an intellectual light imparted to the mind, divine visions made to oneself or to others, or the sacred Scriptures divinely revealed.

paras.t: Denique S. Thomas in secunda secundæ ponit tres rationes, cur donum prophetiæ dignius est dono linguarum. Prima est, quoniam donum prophetiæ consistit in interiori illuminatione mentis; donum vero linguarum refertur ad diversas voces proferendas, quæ sunt signa intelligibilis veritatis. Secunda, quoniam donum prophetiæ ordinatur ad notitiam rerum; donum vero linguarum, ad notitiam vocum. Tertia, quia prophetiæ donum utilius est, eo quod valeat ad ædificationem Ecclesiæ, sicut declaravit Apostolus.
paras.en: Lastly, St Thomas, in the Secunda Secundæ [the second part of the second part of his *Summa*; the place is q. 176, a. 2], gives three reasons why the gift of prophecy is worthier than the gift of tongues. The first is that the gift of prophecy consists in an inward enlightening of the mind, whereas the gift of tongues has to do with uttering divers words, which are signs of intelligible truth. The second, that the gift of prophecy is ordered to the knowledge of things, but the gift of tongues to the knowledge of words. The third, that the gift of prophecy is more useful, since it serves for the edification of the Church, as the Apostle has shown.

paras.t: Ne autem Apostolus videatur donum linguarum omnino contemnere, addit: Volo autem, quantum in me est, vos omnes loqui linguis diversis ex dono Spiritus, scilicet quum sit quoddam donum; magis autem volo vos prophetare. Nam major spiritualiter, id est perfectior, est, ceteris paribus, qui prophetat, reserando abdita Scripturarum, quam qui loquitur linguis: nisi forte interpretetur, id est, ea quæ loquitur clare exponere possit. Sic enim major esset, quia sic haberet utrumque donum, videlicet prophetiam et linguas. Nam interpretatio sermonum ad donum prophetiæ reducitur. — Unde per sui ipsius exemplum ostendit, quod donum linguarum non prosit aliis per se, nisi adjuncta interpretatione sermonum. Ait enim: Nunc autem, o fratres, si venero ad vos linguis loquens, id est diversa idiomata proferens; quid vobis prodero, ita loquendo? nisi vobis loquar, aut in revelatione, id est exponendo revelationem divinitus factam (quæ est, quum quædam mysteria per figuras ostenduntur, sicut in Apocalypsi), aut in scientia, id est exponendo ea quæ ad scientiam spectant et eadem illuminant, aut in prophetia, id est exponendo dicta prophetica, aut in doctrina, id est exponendo ea quæ ad morum informationem concernunt.
paras.en: Lest the Apostle should seem to despise the gift of tongues altogether, he adds: [[14:5|And I would|Volo autem]], as far as lies in me, [[14:5|have you all to speak with tongues|vos omnes loqui linguis]], divers tongues by the gift of the Spirit, that is, since it is a gift; [[14:5|but rather to prophesy|magis autem volo vos prophetare]]. [[14:5|For greater|Nam major]] spiritually, that is, more perfect, [[14:5|is|est]], other things being equal, [[14:5|he that prophesieth|qui prophetat]], by unlocking the hidden things of the Scriptures, [[14:5|than he that speaketh with tongues|quam qui loquitur linguis]]: [[14:5|unless perhaps he interpret|nisi forte interpretetur]], that is, unless he can clearly expound what he speaks. For so he would be greater, because he would then have both gifts, namely prophecy and tongues; for the interpretation of speeches is reduced to the gift of prophecy. — Hence he shows by his own example that the gift of tongues does not of itself profit others, unless the interpretation of speeches is joined to it. For he says: [[14:6|But now, brethren, if I come to you speaking with tongues|Nunc autem, o fratres, si venero ad vos linguis loquens]], that is, uttering divers idioms, [[14:6|what shall I profit you|quid vobis prodero]] by speaking so, [[14:6|unless I speak to you either in revelation|nisi vobis loquar, aut in revelatione]], that is, by expounding a revelation divinely made (which is when certain mysteries are shown by figures, as in the Apocalypse), [[14:6|or in knowledge|aut in scientia]], that is, by expounding the things that belong to knowledge and throw light on them, [[14:6|or in prophecy|aut in prophetia]], that is, by expounding prophetic sayings, [[14:6|or in doctrine|aut in doctrina]], that is, by expounding the things that concern the forming of morals?

paras.t: Præterea introducit exemplum Apostolus de rebus inanimatis, ad ostendendum quod linguæ sine interpretatione inutiles sint. Tamen quæ sine anima sunt, id est inanimata, vocem dantia, id est sonantia (sumit enim sonum pro voce, nam vox proprie est animatorum), sive id inanimatum, sit tibia, sive cithara : nisi distinctionem sonorum dederint, id est, distinctos sonos reddiderint ; quomodo scietur, id est discernetur, quod canitur, aut quod citharizatur ? quasi dicat : Quis poterit aliter judicare modos et consonantias carminis ? Etenim si incertam vocem, id est indeterminatum sonum, dederit tuba qua clangitur tempore prælii, quis parabit se ad bellum ? Nullus utique. Institutus est enim certus modus clangendi tempore præparationis ad pugnam.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle brings in an example from inanimate things, to show that tongues without interpretation are useless. [[14:7|Even things without life|Tamen quæ sine anima sunt]], that is, inanimate things, [[14:7|that give sound|vocem dantia]], that is, that sound (for he takes *voice* for sound, since voice properly belongs to living things) [the Latin has *vocem*, "voice", where the Douay-Rheims has "sound"], [[14:7|whether|sive]] the inanimate thing be [[14:7|pipe or harp|tibia, sive cithara]]: [[14:7|except they give a distinction of sounds|nisi distinctionem sonorum dederint]], that is, render distinct sounds, [[14:7|how shall it be known|quomodo scietur]], that is, discerned, [[14:7|what is piped or harped|quod canitur, aut quod citharizatur]]? As if to say: Who could otherwise judge the measures and harmonies of the song? [[14:8|For if|Etenim si]] [[14:8|the trumpet give|dederit tuba]] that is blown in time of battle [[14:8|an uncertain sound|incertam vocem]], that is, an undetermined sound, [[14:8|who shall prepare himself to the battle|quis parabit se ad bellum]]? No one at all. For a fixed manner of sounding was laid down for the time of preparing for the fight.

paras.t: Consequenter Apostolus applicat similitudinem istam ad propositum. Ita et vos per linguam, id est, linguis loquendo, nisi manifestum sermonem dederitis, id est, verba vestra plane atque faciliter exposueritis ; quomodo scietur, id est, ab auditoribus intelligetur, id quod dicitur, id est, prædicatur a vobis ? Non utique intelligetur. Eritis enim in aera loquentes, id est inanem sonum verborum in aere formantes, et corporum aures, non animorum intelligentias percutientes. Tam multa idiomata, utputa genera linguarum sunt in hoc mundo, videlicet septuaginta duo ; et nihil sine voce est, id est, unaquæque plebs utitur propria voce ; vel, quælibet res habet vocem qua significatur. Si ergo nesciero virtutem, id est significationem, vocis quam loquor vel audio, ero ei cui loquor, id est, quem docere præsumo, barbarus, id est non intelligibilis. Barbarum enim vocamus quod non intelligimus. Et qui loquitur mihi lingua extranea vel obscura, erit mihi barbarus, id est non intellectus.
paras.en: Next the Apostle applies this likeness to the matter in hand. [[14:9|So likewise you|Ita et vos]] [[14:9|by the tongue|per linguam]], that is, by speaking with tongues, [[14:9|except|nisi]] [[14:9|you utter|dederitis]] [[14:9|plain speech|manifestum sermonem]], that is, set out your words plainly and easily, [[14:9|how shall it be known|quomodo scietur]], that is, understood by the hearers, [[14:9|what is said|id quod dicitur]], that is, preached by you? It will not be understood at all. [[14:9|For you shall be speaking into the air|Eritis enim in aera loquentes]], that is, forming an empty sound of words in the air, and striking the ears of bodies, not the understandings of minds. [[14:10|There are, for example, so many kinds of tongues in this world|Tam multa idiomata, utputa genera linguarum sunt in hoc mundo]] (so many idioms, that is), namely seventy-two; [[14:10|and none is without voice|et nihil sine voce est]], that is, each people uses its own speech; or, every thing has a word by which it is signified. [[14:11|If then I know not the power|Si ergo nesciero virtutem]], that is, the meaning, [[14:11|of the voice|vocis]] which I speak or hear, [[14:11|I shall be to him to whom I speak|ero ei cui loquor]], that is, whom I presume to teach, [[14:11|a barbarian|barbarus]], that is, not intelligible; for we call barbarous what we do not understand. [[14:11|and he that speaketh|Et qui loquitur]] to me in a foreign or obscure tongue will be to me [[14:11|a barbarian|barbarus]], that is, not understood.

paras.t: Sic et vos, quoniam æmulatores estis spirituum, id est appetitores spiritualium munerum Spiritus Sancti, ad ædificationem Ecclesiæ quærite ut abundetis, id est, ad hoc laborate spiritualibus donis impleri, ut aliorum saluti cooperemini : quod est ædificare Ecclesiam. Et ideo qui loquitur lingua, id est, loquendo utitur dono linguarum, oret Deum ut interpretetur, id est, ut Deus conferat sibi gratiam interpretationis sermonum, ut quæ loquitur, plane intelligat et aliis evidenter proponat. Nam si orem lingua, id est, verba orationis sine intellectu pronuntiem, spiritus meus, id est voluntas, orat, id est, ad Deum afficitur, quia ei per caritatem unitur, et cupit adipisci quod verba orationis significant, licet sensum in speciali anima non cognoscat. Significatur vero voluntas per spiritum, quoniam spiritus vim impulsivam seu motivam importat. Impulsio autem seu motio respicit voluntatem, cujus est ferre atque impellere amantem in amatum. Mens autem mea, id est intellectus, sine fructu est, id est sine contemplatione et delectatione, quæ consistunt in distincta et propria cognitione eorum quæ per orationem designantur. Quid ergo est mihi agendum? Orabo spiritu, id est affectu, orabo et mente, id est in intellectu, orando Deum toto corde, ita ut diligenter attendam, atque ardenter optem quod oro. Simili modo psallam, id est, Deum laudabo, spiritu, psallam et mente. Ex his patet donum prophetiæ dignius esse dono linguarum, quia per donum prophetiæ orat quis mente et spiritu : intelligit enim quæ dicit ; sed per donum linguarum non orat homo, nisi in spiritu.
paras.en: [[14:12|So you also, forasmuch as you are zealous of spirits|Sic et vos, quoniam æmulatores estis spirituum]], that is, desirous of the spiritual gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[14:12|seek to abound unto the edifying of the church|ad ædificationem Ecclesiæ quærite ut abundetis]], that is, labour to be filled with spiritual gifts for this end, that you may cooperate in the salvation of others: which is to edify the Church. [[14:13|And therefore he that speaketh by a tongue|Et ideo qui loquitur lingua]], that is, who in speaking uses the gift of tongues, [[14:13|let him pray|oret]] God [[14:13|that he may interpret|ut interpretetur]], that is, that God may bestow on him the grace of the interpretation of speeches, so that he may understand plainly what he speaks and set it clearly before others. [[14:14|For if I pray in a tongue|Nam si orem lingua]], that is, pronounce the words of a prayer without understanding, [[14:14|my spirit|spiritus meus]], that is, the will, [[14:14|prayeth|orat]], that is, is moved towards God, because it is united to Him by charity, and desires to obtain what the words of the prayer signify, although the soul does not know their sense in particular. Now the will is signified by *spirit*, because spirit implies an impelling or moving force; and impulse or motion has to do with the will, whose part it is to carry and impel the lover towards the beloved. [[14:14|but my understanding|Mens autem mea]], that is, the intellect, [[14:14|is without fruit|sine fructu est]], that is, without contemplation and delight, which consist in a distinct and proper knowledge of the things that are signified by the prayer. [[14:15|What is it then|Quid ergo est]] that I must do? [[14:15|I will pray with the spirit|Orabo spiritu]], that is, with the affection, [[14:15|I will pray also with the understanding|orabo et mente]], that is, in the intellect: praying to God with the whole heart, so that I attend diligently to what I pray for, and ardently desire it. In like manner [[14:15|I will sing|psallam]], that is, I will praise God, [[14:15|with the spirit|spiritu]], [[14:15|I will sing also with the understanding|psallam et mente]]. From this it is plain that the gift of prophecy is worthier than the gift of tongues, because by the gift of prophecy one prays with the mind and with the spirit, for he understands what he says; but by the gift of tongues a man prays only in the spirit.

paras.t: Ceterum si benedixeris, id est, alii bona dixeris, seu benedictionem contuleris, sicut facit episcopus et sacerdos, spiritu, id est, non verbis quæ ab aliis intelligantur, sed solum lingua ; qui supplet locum idiotæ, id est dato quod nemo tunc adsit nisi illitteratus et rudis, quomodo dicet, Amen, super benedictionem tuam ? id est, quomodo tibi respondebit, et consensus ac desiderii verbum tuæ benedictioni adjiciet? Non potest hoc facere cum attentione, quoniam quid dicas nescit, id est, sensum tuæ benedictionis non percipit. Nam tu quidem bene gratias agis Deo, ipsum laudando in spiritu, id est cum affectu; sed alter non ædificatur, id est, non proficit, non accenditur, nec instruitur in verbis tuis quæ non intelligit, eo quod non loqueris interpretando seu exponendo sermonem.
paras.en: [[14:16|Else, if thou shalt bless|Ceterum si benedixeris]], that is, speak good things to another, or confer a blessing, as the bishop and the priest do, [[14:16|with the spirit|spiritu]], that is, not in words that others understand, but with the tongue only, [[14:16|he that holdeth the place of the unlearned|qui supplet locum idiotæ]], that is, granted that no one is then present but an unlettered and simple man: [[14:16|how shall|quomodo]] he [[14:16|say, Amen, to thy blessing|dicet, Amen, super benedictionem tuam]]? that is, how will he answer thee, and add a word of assent and desire to thy blessing? He cannot do this with attention, [[14:16|because he knoweth not what thou sayest|quoniam quid dicas nescit]], that is, he does not perceive the sense of thy blessing. [[14:17|For thou indeed givest thanks well|Nam tu quidem bene gratias agis]] to God, praising Him in the spirit, that is, with affection; [[14:17|but the other is not edified|sed alter non ædificatur]], that is, he does not profit, he is not kindled nor instructed by thy words, which he does not understand, because thou dost not speak so as to interpret or expound what thou sayest.

paras.t: Gratias ago Deo meo quod omnium vestrum lingua loquor. Data est enim Apostolis per donum linguarum, universarum linguarum scientia, quatenus universis gentibus prædicarent. Sed in ecclesia materiali, et inter fideles, volo potius quinque, id est pauca, verba loqui sensu meo, id est cum intellectu perfecto, ut me ipsum intelligam, et ab aliis intelligar, ut et alios instruam, sicut pertinet ad prædicatorem ; quam decem millia verborum loqui, id est quantamcumque verborum multitudinem : ponit enim determinatum pro indeterminato, quemadmodum in Daniele legitur, Millia millium ministrabant ei, etc. ; in lingua dumtaxat, id est sine intellectu et aliorum instructione.
paras.en: [[14:18|I thank my God I speak with all your tongues|Gratias ago Deo meo quod omnium vestrum lingua loquor]]. For through the gift of tongues the knowledge of all tongues was given to the Apostles, that they might preach to all nations. [[14:19|But in the church|Sed in ecclesia]] (the material church [that is, the building where the faithful gather]), and among the faithful, [[14:19|I had rather|volo potius]] speak [[14:19|five|quinque]], that is, a few, [[14:19|words|verba]] [[14:19|with my understanding|sensu meo]], that is, with perfect understanding, so that I understand myself and am understood by others, [[14:19|that I may instruct others also|ut et alios instruam]], as belongs to a preacher, [[14:19|than ten thousand words|quam decem millia verborum]] spoken, that is, any multitude of words whatever (for he puts a definite number for an indefinite one, as we read in Daniel: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him|Millia millium ministrabant ei]], etc.) [[14:19|in a tongue|in lingua]] only, that is, without understanding and without the instruction of others.

paras.t: Fratres mei, nolite pueri effici sensibus, id est, pueris nolite conformari quantum ad imperfectam eorum cognitionem, ne more puerorum erretis discernendo inter bonum et malum, verum et falsum. Scriptum est enim : Puer centum annorum maledicetur. Sed malitia parvuli estote, id est, puerorum innocentiam sectemini : sicut et Christus monet, Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum ; et Psalmista, Testimonium (inquit) Domini fidele, sapientiam præstans parvulis. Sensibus autem, id est interioribus actibus intellectus, perfecti sitis, ut habeatis sensus exercitatos ad discretionem boni et mali. Quis autem sit sensus perfectus, innuitur per Sapientem, qui dicit : Cogitare de sapientia, sensus est consummatus.
paras.en: [[14:20|Brethren|Fratres]] of mine, [[14:20|do not become children in sense|nolite pueri effici sensibus]], that is, do not be like children as regards their imperfect knowledge, lest after the manner of children you go astray in discerning between good and evil, true and false. For it is written: A child of a hundred years shall be accursed[[Is 65:20||]] [Denis joins two clauses of the verse, which reads "the child shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed"]. [[14:20|But in malice be children|Sed malitia parvuli estote]], that is, follow the innocence of children: as Christ also warns, [[Matt 18:3|unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 18:8|the testimony|Testimonium]], he says, [[Ps 18:8|of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones|Domini fidele, sapientiam præstans parvulis]]. [[14:20|and in sense|Sensibus autem]], that is, in the inward acts of the understanding, [[14:20|be perfect|perfecti sitis]], so that you may have your senses exercised to the discerning of good and evil. And what perfect sense is, the Wise Man indicates when he says: [[Wis 6:16|To think, therefore, upon her, is perfect understanding|Cogitare de sapientia, sensus est consummatus]] [Denis has "to think of wisdom", where the verse has "upon her", meaning wisdom; "perfect understanding" is *sensus consummatus*, "perfect sense", the word of the Apostle's "in sense"].

paras.t: In lege enim (prout lex omnes Scripturas veteris Testamenti includit) scriptum est in Isaia : Quoniam in aliis linguis, et labiis aliis, id est non solum in Hebræo, sed in diversis linguarum generibus, et insolito modo loquendi, loquar per Apostolos populo huic Judæorum ; et nec sic, id est non propter tam evidens signum, exaudient me, id est sermonibus meis acquiescent, dicit Dominus. Hoc contigisse patet in Actibus, ubi inducitur quemadmodum Apostoli Spiritu Sancto recepto, loquebantur Judæis variis linguis. Judæi tamen pro majori parte permanserunt increduli. Hoc allegat Apostolus, ut ostendat Corinthiis cur non debent tam inhianter quærere donum linguarum, quod ipsi ex quadam curiositate magis quærebant quam gratiam prophetiæ : ob hoc quod linguæ in signum sunt infidelibus, ipsi vero jam erant fideles. Unde concludit : Itaque linguæ in signum sunt non fidelibus, sed infidelibus, id est non propter necessitatem vel conversionem credentium, qui sciunt Deum omnia posse, nec indigent tali miraculo. Infidelibus vero necessaria fuit novitas hujus miraculi, ut vel sic admonerentur converti ad Dominum. Prophetiæ autem in signum sunt, non infidelibus, sed fidelibus, quia non proponuntur infidelibus, ne margaritæ projiciantur ante porcos, vel sanctum canibus detur.
paras.en: [[14:21|In the law|In lege]] (inasmuch as *the law* includes all the Scriptures of the Old Testament) [[14:21|it is written|scriptum est]], in Isaias[[Is 28:11||]]: [[14:21|In other tongues and other lips|Quoniam in aliis linguis, et labiis aliis]], that is, not only in Hebrew, but in divers kinds of tongues and in an unwonted manner of speaking, [[14:21|I will speak|loquar]] through the Apostles [[14:21|to this people|populo huic]] of the Jews; [[14:21|and neither so|et nec sic]], that is, not even for so evident a sign, [[14:21|will they hear me|exaudient me]], that is, assent to my words, [[14:21|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]. That this came to pass is plain from the Acts, where it is told how the Apostles, having received the Holy Ghost, spoke to the Jews in divers tongues[[Acts 2:4||]]. Yet the Jews for the most part remained unbelieving. The Apostle alleges this to show the Corinthians why they ought not to seek the gift of tongues so greedily (which out of a certain curiosity they sought more than the grace of prophecy): because tongues are a sign to unbelievers, whereas they were already believers. Hence he concludes: [[14:22|Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to believers but to unbelievers|Itaque linguæ in signum sunt non fidelibus, sed infidelibus]], that is, not for the need or the conversion of believers, who know that God can do all things and have no need of such a miracle; but for unbelievers the novelty of this miracle was necessary, that by it at least they might be admonished to turn to the Lord. [[14:22|but prophecies|Prophetiæ autem]] are for a sign, [[14:22|not to unbelievers but to believers|non infidelibus, sed fidelibus]], because they are not set before unbelievers, lest pearls be cast before swine, or what is holy be given to dogs[[Matt 7:6||]].

paras.t: Adhuc autem probat Apostolus, quod donum linguarum non sit adeo appetendum, ut donum prophetiæ. Si ergo universa ecclesia, id est societas fidelium, conveniat in unum mente et corpore, et omnes fideles linguis loquantur diversis et inlucidatis, intrent autem idiotæ aut infideles, et audiant vos sic loquentes ; nonne dicent quod insanitis, tanquam obsessi vel arrepticii ? Quum enim fuerit inter vos tantus tumultus et confusio linguarum, nec unus intellexerit alium, videbimini similes phreneticis, illusis atque amentibus. Si autem omnes fideles prophetent, id est, abdita Scripturarum exponant, et intellectualiter de secretis conferant, vel divinitus revelata Dei aliis publice dicant, intret autem quis infidelis aut idiota, convincitur ab omnibus, et dijudicatur ab omnibus. […]phetantibus, quod sit in aliquo errore, dijudicatur, id est, damnabilis demonstratur, ab omnibus. Occulta enim cordis ejus, videlicet peccata latentia, seu cogitationes injustæ, manifesta fiunt per prophetias illorum. Et ita cadens in faciem, id est, se peccatorem agnoscens, pœnitens, et in terra prosternens se, adorabit Deum pro indulgentia et misericordia, pronuntians quod vere Deus in vobis sit per gratiam specialem.
paras.en: The Apostle proves further that the gift of tongues is not so much to be desired as the gift of prophecy. [[14:23|If therefore the whole church|Si ergo universa ecclesia]], that is, the society of the faithful, [[14:23|come together into one place|conveniat in unum]] in mind and body, [[14:23|and all speak with tongues|et omnes fideles linguis loquantur]], all the faithful, in divers tongues not made clear, [[14:23|and there come in unlearned persons or infidels|intrent autem idiotæ aut infideles]], and hear you speaking so, [[14:23|will they not say that you are mad|nonne dicent quod insanitis]], as if possessed or seized by a spirit? For when there is among you so great a tumult and confusion of tongues, and no one understands another, you will seem like men in a frenzy, deluded and out of their minds. [[14:24|But if all prophesy|Si autem omnes fideles prophetent]], all the faithful, that is, expound the hidden things of the Scriptures, and confer together with understanding about secret things, or tell others publicly the things divinely revealed by God, [[14:24|and there come in one that believeth not or an unlearned person|intret autem quis infidelis aut idiota]], [[14:24|he is convinced of all|convincitur ab omnibus]], and [[14:24|he is judged of all|dijudicatur ab omnibus]]. […] [a line or more is lost here at a column break; only the end of the next word survives, *…phetantibus*, probably *prophetantibus*, "by those prophesying"], that he is in some error, [[14:24|he is judged|dijudicatur]], that is, shown to be worthy of condemnation, [[14:24|of all|ab omnibus]]. [[14:25|The secrets of his heart|Occulta enim cordis ejus]], namely hidden sins or unjust thoughts, [[14:25|are made manifest|manifesta fiunt]] through their prophecies. [[14:25|And so, falling down on his face|Et ita cadens in faciem]], that is, acknowledging himself a sinner, repenting and prostrating himself on the ground, [[14:25|he will adore God|adorabit Deum]] for pardon and mercy, [[14:25|affirming that God is among you indeed|pronuntians quod vere Deus in vobis sit]] by a special grace.

paras.t: Consequenter pandit Apostolus quomodo utendum sit donis linguarum ac prophetiæ. Quid ergo est, fratres? id est, quum prædicta ita se habeant, quid est agendum? Quum convenitis in ecclesiam, unusquisque vestrum, id est aliquis de omni genere congregationis vestræ; vel, Unusquisque vestrum in se, vel in alio sibi per caritatem conjuncto; psalmum habet, id est laudem Dei cum cantico, doctrinam habet moralem ad alios imbuendos, apocalypsim, id est revelationem, habet, linguam habet, id est donum linguarum, interpretationem habet, id est facultatem exponendi Scripturas aut linguas. Omnia autem hæc ad ædificationem fiant ecclesiæ, id est ordinate et caritative, secundum quod congruit congregationi fidelium.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows how the gifts of tongues and of prophecy are to be used. [[14:26|How is it then, brethren|Quid ergo est, fratres]]? that is, since the foregoing is so, what is to be done? [[14:26|When you come together|Quum convenitis]] in the church, [[14:26|every one of you|unusquisque vestrum]], that is, someone of every kind in your congregation; or, every one of you in himself, or in another joined to him by charity, [[14:26|hath a psalm|psalmum habet]], that is, the praise of God with song, [[14:26|hath a doctrine|doctrinam habet]] of morals for instructing others, [[14:26|hath a revelation|apocalypsim, id est revelationem, habet]] [Denis glosses the Greek word *apocalypsim* with the Latin *revelationem*, "revelation"], [[14:26|hath a tongue|linguam habet]], that is, the gift of tongues, [[14:26|hath an interpretation|interpretationem habet]], that is, the faculty of expounding the Scriptures or tongues. [[14:26|let all things be done to edification|Omnia autem hæc ad ædificationem fiant]] of the church, that is, in order and in charity, as befits a congregation of the faithful.

paras.t: Sive lingua quis loquitur, id est, si aliquis loquendo utitur dono linguarum, secundum duos fiat talis locutio, aut ut multum sit, fiat secundum tres, id est, non nisi duo, vel ad majus tres, ita loquantur, ne tempus expendatur in tali occupatione minus fructuosa in se. Fiat quoque locutio ista et per partes, id est successive, quantum ad tempus, ut unus loquatur post alium, vel divisim, quantum ad partes populi: vel intercise, ut post unam partem locutionis, sequatur ejus expositio, et post aliam partem similiter: sicut fit quando prædicator prædicat hominibus ignotæ linguæ per interpretem. Ideo subditur: et unus interpretetur, id est, aliquis sit qui exponat populo quæ dicuntur. Si autem non fuerit præsens aliquis interpres, id est expositor, taceat in ecclesia qui loquitur lingua, quia nullum ædificat, nisi ipsemet interpretetur; sibi autem, id est ad suam propriam utilitatem, loquatur orando, et Deo, id est ad gloriam Dei in secreto, ut nullum impediat.
paras.en: [[14:27|If any speak with a tongue|Sive lingua quis loquitur]], that is, if anyone in speaking uses the gift of tongues, [[14:27|let it be by two|secundum duos]], let such speaking be, [[14:27|or at the most|aut ut multum]], let it be [[14:27|by three|tres]]: that is, let no more than two, or at most three, speak so, lest time be spent on an occupation that is in itself less fruitful. Let this speaking also be [[14:27|and in course|et per partes]] [literally "by parts", which Denis takes in three ways], that is, successively as to time, so that one speaks after another; or separately, as to the parts of the people; or in turns, so that after one part of the speech its exposition follows, and likewise after another part: as is done when a preacher preaches through an interpreter to men of an unknown tongue. Therefore it is added: [[14:27|and let one interpret|et unus interpretetur]], that is, let there be someone to expound to the people what is said. [[14:28|But if there be no interpreter|Si autem non fuerit præsens aliquis interpres]] present, that is, an expounder, [[14:28|let him hold his peace in the church|taceat in ecclesia]], he that speaks with a tongue, because he edifies no one, unless he himself interprets; [[14:28|to himself|sibi autem]], that is, for his own profit, let him [[14:28|speak|loquatur]] in prayer, [[14:28|and to God|et Deo]], that is, to the glory of God in secret, so as to hinder no one.

paras.t: Prophetæ, id est Scripturarum expositores sive doctores, duo vel tres dicant, id est, in ecclesia prædicent ordinate et sigillatim: tot enim sufficiunt; et ceteri dijudicent, id est, diligenter discernant, ne forte aliquid falsitatis commisceatur. Quod si aliquid melius et ignotum ac necessarium revelatum fuerit per Spiritum Sanctum, sedenti, id est alicui auditori, prior prophetans taceat, dans locum loquendi huic illuminato. Potestis enim omnes per singulos, id est sigillatim, scilicet unus post alium, prophetare, id est Scripturam sacram disserere, ejusque mysteria declarare, ut omnes discant, etiam superiores ab inferioribus, quia non omnia omnibus revelantur, sed aliqua uni, aliqua alteri, et omnes exhortentur, id est, verbum exhortationis proponant, quilibet suo loco ac tempore, ne fiat turbatio.
paras.en: [[14:29|And let the prophets|Prophetæ]], that is, the expounders or teachers of the Scriptures, [[14:29|speak, two or three|duo vel tres dicant]], that is, preach in the church in order and one at a time, for so many are enough; [[14:29|and let the rest judge|et ceteri dijudicent]], that is, discern carefully, lest perhaps some falsehood be mingled in. [[14:30|But if any thing|Quod si aliquid]] better, unknown and needful, [[14:30|be revealed|revelatum fuerit]] by the Holy Ghost [[14:30|to another sitting|sedenti]], that is, to some hearer, [[14:30|let the first|prior]] who is prophesying [[14:30|hold his peace|taceat]], giving room to speak to this one who has been enlightened. [[14:31|For you may all|Potestis enim omnes]] [[14:31|one by one|per singulos]], that is, singly, namely one after another, [[14:31|prophesy|prophetare]], that is, discourse on Holy Scripture and declare its mysteries, [[14:31|that all may learn|ut omnes discant]], even superiors from inferiors, since not all things are revealed to all, but some to one and some to another, [[14:31|and all may be exhorted|et omnes exhortentur]], that is, may set forth a word of exhortation [Denis takes *exhortentur* actively, "may exhort"], each in his own place and time, lest there be disorder.

paras.t: Et spiritus Prophetarum Prophetis subjecti sunt. Hoc multi exponunt de Spiritu Sancto: qui pluraliter dicitur Spiritus, propter diversitatem donorum suorum, vel propter pluralitatem Prophetarum quos implet. Dicitur autem Prophetis subjectus, quia non cogit eos tacere vel loqui. Ideo unus potest alteri cedere. Aptius vero videtur posse intelligi de spiritu rationali, creato videlicet: ut spiritus, id est animæ, seu ratio et voluntas Prophetarum dicantur eis subjecta, quia Prophetæ non sunt locuti sicut amentes et insensati, ut voluerunt hæretici; sed sponte et libere loquebantur, ita quod sibi ipsis poterant imperare et obedire. Non enim est dissensionis, id est discordiæ, Deus, auctor vel approbator, sed pacis: ideo vult ut unus alteri cedat; sicut in omnibus ecclesiis sanctorum doceo per me ipsum et discipulos meos, et per epistolas meas.
paras.en: [[14:32|And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets|Et spiritus Prophetarum Prophetis subjecti sunt]]. Many expound this of the Holy Ghost, who is called *spirits* in the plural on account of the diversity of His gifts, or on account of the plurality of the Prophets whom He fills; and He is said to be subject to the Prophets because He does not compel them to be silent or to speak, and so one can give way to another. But it seems that it can more fittingly be understood of the rational spirit, that is, the created one: so that the spirits, that is, the souls, or the reason and will, of the Prophets are said to be subject to them, because the Prophets did not speak like madmen and senseless persons, as the heretics would have it, but spoke freely and of their own accord, so that they could command themselves and obey themselves. [[14:33|For God is not the God of dissension|Non enim est dissensionis]], that is, of discord, the author or approver, [[14:33|but of peace|sed pacis]]: therefore He wills that one give way to another; [[14:33|as also I teach in all the churches of the saints|sicut in omnibus ecclesiis sanctorum doceo]], by myself and by my disciples, and by my letters.

paras.t: Et quia jam dixit Apostolus, Potestis omnes prophetare, ne hoc de utroque sexu intelligatur, subjecit : Mulieres in ecclesiis taceant, id est, nec prophetare, id est docere, nec loqui linguis præsumant. Non enim permittitur eis aliqua auctoritate loqui in ecclesia, nisi secrete orando : sed præcipitur eis subditas esse viris, sicut et lex dicit in Genesi : Sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui. Si quid autem volunt discere, domi viros suos interrogent ut instruantur, non in ecclesia. Turpe est enim, id est inhonestum ac indecens, mulierem loqui in ecclesia : Primo, quoniam mulieribus convenit esse verecundas ac subditas; docere autem pertinet ad eminentiorem. Secundo, quoniam ratio naturaliter debilior est in femina quam in viro. Tertio, ne ex sermocinatione mulieris concitetur libido virorum. Colloquium enim illius quasi ignis exardescit.
paras.en: And since the Apostle has just said, [[14:31|you may all prophesy|Potestis omnes prophetare]], lest this be understood of both sexes, he adds: [[14:34|Let women keep silence in the churches|Mulieres in ecclesiis taceant]], that is, let them not presume either to prophesy, that is, to teach, or to speak with tongues. [[14:34|For it is not permitted them|Non enim permittitur eis]] by any authority [[14:34|to speak|loqui]] in the church, except in praying secretly; [[14:34|but|sed]] they are commanded [[14:34|to be subject|subditas esse]] to the men, [[14:34|as also the law saith|sicut et lex dicit]] in Genesis: [[Gen 3:16|thou shalt be under thy husband's power, and he shall have dominion over thee|Sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui]]. [[14:35|But if they would learn anything|Si quid autem volunt discere]], [[14:35|let them ask their husbands at home|domi viros suos interrogent]], that they may be instructed, not in the church. [[14:35|For it is a shame|Turpe est enim]], that is, dishonourable and unbecoming, [[14:35|for a woman to speak in the church|mulierem loqui in ecclesia]]: first, because it befits women to be modest and subject, while teaching belongs to one of higher standing; second, because reason is naturally weaker in woman than in man; third, lest the lust of men be stirred up by a woman's talk, for [[Ecclus 9:11|her conversation burneth as fire|Colloquium enim illius quasi ignis exardescit]].

paras.t: Insuper increpantur Corinthiorum rebelles, qui in aliquibus præsumpserunt mutare ordinationes Apostoli. Ne ergo et huic ordinationi de silentio mulierum resistere audeant, dicitur eis : An a vobis verbum Dei processit? id est, non utique a vobis ortum sumpsit prædicatio evangelica, sed a nobis. Idcirco tenemini acquiescere nostris statutis. An in vos solos pervenit? id est, non vobis tantum, sed aliis multis annuntiata et infusa est Christi doctrina. Ideo conformetis vos aliis, et implete quod dico. Si quis videtur propheta esse, aut spiritualis, id est, qui vere prophetat, exponendo Scripturarum mysteria, vel prædicendo futura, cognoscat, id est, spiritualiter penset, quæ scribo vobis, quoniam Domini sunt mandata, id est ex divina inspiratione a me prolata, non ex proprio corde conficta. Si quis autem ignorat ista quæ scire tenetur, ignorabitur, id est, a Deo non cognoscetur notitia approbationis : sicut nec illi quibus dicitur, Nescio vos unde sitis.
paras.en: Moreover, the rebellious among the Corinthians are rebuked, who in some things had presumed to change the Apostle's ordinances. So, lest they dare to resist this ordinance too, about the silence of women, it is said to them: [[14:36|Or did the word of God come out from you|An a vobis verbum Dei processit]]? that is, the preaching of the Gospel certainly did not take its rise from you, but from us; therefore you are bound to acquiesce in our statutes. [[14:36|Or came it only unto you|An in vos solos pervenit?]]? that is, the doctrine of Christ has been announced and poured in not to you only, but to many others; therefore conform yourselves to the others, and fulfil what I say. [[14:37|If any seem to be a prophet or spiritual|Si quis videtur propheta esse, aut spiritualis]], that is, one who truly prophesies, by expounding the mysteries of the Scriptures or by foretelling the future, [[14:37|let him know|cognoscat]], that is, let him weigh spiritually, [[14:37|the things that I write to you, that they are the commandments of the Lord|quæ scribo vobis, quoniam Domini sunt mandata]], that is, uttered by me from divine inspiration, not invented out of my own heart. [[14:38|But if any man know not|Si quis autem ignorat]] these things which he is bound to know, [[14:38|he shall not be known|ignorabitur]], that is, he will not be known by God with the knowledge of approval: as neither are those to whom it is said, [[Luke 13:25|I know you not, whence you are|Nescio vos unde sitis]].

paras.t: Itaque, fratres, æmulamini, id est desiderate, prophetare (secundum sensum jam sæpe præhabitum); et loqui linguis, id est uti dono linguarum, nolite prohibere eos qui possunt sic loqui, quamvis melius sit prophetare. Omnia autem quæ fiunt inter vos, honeste, id est virtuose, et secundum ordinem, id est ordinate, fiant in vobis, ut nihil reprehensibile in actibus vestris appareat, et cum debitis circumstantiis cuncta agantur. Optimum enim in rebus est ordo; et peccatum non est nisi recessus ab ordine.
paras.en: [[14:39|Wherefore, brethren, be zealous|Itaque, fratres, æmulamini]], that is, desire, [[14:39|to prophesy|prophetare]] (in the sense already often given before); and [[14:39|to speak with tongues|et loqui linguis]], that is, to use the gift of tongues, [[14:39|forbid not|nolite prohibere]] to those who can speak so, although it is better to prophesy. [[14:40|But let all things|Omnia autem]] that are done among you, [[14:40|decently|honeste]], that is, virtuously, [[14:40|and according to order|et secundum ordinem]], that is, in an orderly way, [[14:40|be done|fiant]] among you, so that nothing blameworthy may appear in your acts, and all things may be done with their due circumstances. For order is the best thing in things; and sin is nothing but a departure from order.

15.title: Expositio capituli quintidecimi: Notum autem vobis facio, fratres, Evangelium
15.title_en: Explanation of the fifteenth chapter: Now I make known unto you, brethren, the gospel

paras.t: COMPLETO tractatu de sacramentis et gratiis, nunc agit de resurrectione mortuorum: de qua primo recte instructi fuerunt Corinthii ab ipso Apostolo: postmodum vero quum recessisset Apostolus, a perversis infecta est fides illorum de resurrectione futura. Itaque ait: Notum autem vobis facio, fratres, id est, ad memoriam revoco, clarumque expono, Evangelium quod prædicavi vobis, id est bonam annuntiationem de Christo, quod Evangelium et accepistis, adhibendo fidem evangelicæ prædicationi, in quo et statis, habendo intellectum erectum ad Deum in veritate evangelicæ legis, voluntatem quoque a ruina peccati elevatam, per quod et salvamini, credendo testimoniis Evangelii, ejusque obediendo præceptis. Et hoc utique sic est, qua ratione prædicaverim vobis, si retinetis, id est, si diligenter recolitis qua ratione, id est quo fine, qua spe, seu quo argumento prædicaverim vobis Evangelium Christi. Prædicavi enim vobis ad hunc finem, id est propter hanc spem, ut consequamini vitam æternam. Argumentum quoque quo probavi resurrectionem futuram, fuit resurrectio Christi. Hæc autem retinetis, et per Evangelium istud salvamini, nisi, id est si non, frustra et inaniter credidistis.
paras.en: Having completed his treatment of the sacraments and graces [that is, the gifts of grace treated in the preceding chapters], he now treats of the resurrection of the dead. On this the Corinthians were first rightly instructed by the Apostle himself; but afterwards, when the Apostle had gone away, their faith in the resurrection to come was infected by perverse men. So he says: [[15:1|Now I make known unto you, brethren|Notum autem vobis facio, fratres]], that is, I call back to your memory and set out clearly, [[15:1|the gospel which I preached to you|Evangelium quod prædicavi vobis]], that is, the good tidings about Christ, [[15:1|which also you have received|quod Evangelium et accepistis]] by giving faith to the gospel preaching, [[15:1|and wherein you stand|in quo et statis]], having your understanding raised up to God in the truth of the gospel law, and your will lifted up from the fall of sin; [[15:2|By which also you are saved|per quod et salvamini]], by believing the testimonies of the Gospel and obeying its precepts. And this is indeed so, [[15:2|after what manner I preached unto you|qua ratione prædicaverim vobis]], [[15:2|if you hold fast|si retinetis]], that is, if you diligently call to mind after what manner, that is, to what end, with what hope, or by what argument I preached to you the Gospel of Christ. For I preached to you to this end, that is, for the sake of this hope, that you may obtain eternal life; and the argument by which I proved the resurrection to come was the resurrection of Christ. These things you hold fast, and through this Gospel you are saved, [[15:2|unless|nisi]], that is, if not, [[15:2|you have believed in vain|frustra et inaniter credidistis]].

paras.t: Tradidi enim, id est prædicavi, vobis in primis, id est inter præcipua puncta quæ docui: prædicavi, inquam, testimonium fidei, quod et accepi, id est, per divinam revelationem cognovi, non excogitavi: quoniam Christus mortuus, id est occisus, est pro peccatis nostris tollendis, secundum Scripturas. Scriptum est enim in Threnis: Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris; et in Isaia, Ipse autem vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra.
paras.en: [[15:3|For I delivered|Tradidi enim]], that is, I preached, [[15:3|unto you first of all|vobis in primis]], that is, among the chief points that I taught: I preached, I say, the testimony of faith, [[15:3|which I also received|quod et accepi]], that is, which I came to know by divine revelation and did not think up myself: [[15:3|how that Christ died|quoniam Christus mortuus]], that is, was slain, [[15:3|for our sins|est pro peccatis nostris]], to take them away, [[15:3|according to the scriptures|secundum Scripturas]]. For it is written in Lamentations: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins|Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris]]; and in Isaias: [[Is 53:5|But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins|Ipse autem vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra]].

paras.t: Et quia sepultus est, et quia resurrexit tertia die secundum Scripturas. De sepultura quippe Isaias prædixit: Et erit sepulcrum ejus gloriosum; item, Dabit impios pro sepultura, et divites pro morte sua. De resurrectione quoque ait Osee: Vivificabit nos post duos dies, in die tertia suscitabit nos; et Sophonias, Exspecta me, dicit Dominus, in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum.
paras.en: [[15:4|And that he was buried: and that he rose again on the third day according to the scriptures|Et quia sepultus est, et quia resurrexit tertia die secundum Scripturas]]. For of the burial Isaias foretold: [[Is 11:10|and his sepulchre shall be glorious|Et erit sepulcrum ejus gloriosum]]; and again: [[Is 53:9|he shall give the ungodly for his burial, and the rich for his death|Dabit impios pro sepultura, et divites pro morte sua]]. Of the resurrection, too, Osee says: [[Osee 6:3|He will revive us after two days: on the third day he will raise us up|Vivificabit nos post duos dies, in die tertia suscitabit nos]]; and Sophonias: [[Soph 3:8|expect me, saith the Lord, in the day of my resurrection that is to come|Exspecta me, dicit Dominus, in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum]].

paras.t: Et quia visus est Cephæ, id est Petro. Quamvis locus hujus apparitionis ignoretur, creditur tamen facta quando Petrus a monumento recessit in die resurrectionis, quando videlicet Maria Magdalene dixit se Christum vidisse. Et post hæc visus est undecim Apostolis in conclavi, Thoma præsente. Deinde visus est plus quam quingentis fratribus, id est discipulis, simul; ex quibus multi manent, id est, in corpore vivunt, usque adhuc, quidam autem dormierunt somno beatæ mortis in Domino. De hac visione nullus Evangelistarum scribit.
paras.en: [[15:5|And that he was seen by Cephas|Et quia visus est Cephæ]], that is, by Peter. Although the place of this appearance is not known, it is believed to have happened when Peter went back from the tomb on the day of the resurrection, that is, when Mary Magdalen said that she had seen Christ[[John 20:18||]]. [[15:5|and after that by the eleven|Et post hæc visus est undecim]] Apostles in the closed room, Thomas being present[[John 20:26||]] [the margin gives Ibid. 20, that is, John 20:20; the appearance with Thomas present is John 20:26]. [[15:6|Then was he seen by more than five hundred brethren|Deinde visus est plus quam quingentis fratribus]], that is, disciples, [[15:6|at once: of whom many remain|simul; ex quibus multi manent]], that is, are living in the body, [[15:6|until this present, and some are fallen asleep|usque adhuc, quidam autem dormierunt]] in the sleep of a blessed death in the Lord[[Apoc 14:13||]]. Of this appearance none of the Evangelists writes.

paras.t: Deinde visus est seorsum Jacobo Minori fratri Domini, primo Hierosolymorum episcopo. De hac apparitione non loquitur Evangelium. Deinde visus est Apostolis omnibus in die ascensionis.
paras.en: [[15:7|After that, he was seen|Deinde visus est]] apart [[15:7|by James|Jacobo]] the Less, the brother of the Lord, the first bishop of Jerusalem. Of this appearance the Gospel does not speak. [[15:7|then by all the apostles|Deinde visus est Apostolis omnibus]] on the day of the Ascension[[Mark 16:14||]] [the margin gives Mark xvi, 14–16].

paras.t: Novissime autem omnium prædictorum, videlicet post ascensionem et Spiritus Sancti missionem, tanquam abortivo, visus est et mihi proficiscenti Damascum. Abortivum autem vocatur proles quæ extra debitum et congruum tempus nascitur, vel cum violentia de ventre educitur, vel ad debitam quantitatem non pervenit. Ideo propter tria comparat se Apostolus abortivo: primo, quoniam alii Apostoli ante missionem Paracleti sunt renati, ipse postea ab Anania; secundo, quia cum quadam coactione conversus est, scilicet per terrorem et minas; tertio, quia aliis Apostolis minor fuit, consideratione vitæ præteritæ, quando persecutus est Christianos. Ideo subdit: Ego enim sum minimus Apostolorum: non simpliciter, sed quantum ad aliquid, utpote quia ultimo ad apostolatum vocatus est. Hoc modo Jacobus Alphæi, frater Domini, dictus est Minor, respectu Jacobi filii Zebedæi, non sanctitate aut dignitate, sed quia vocatione posterior. Iterum, Minimus sum Apostolorum, ratione præteritorum malorum. Qui non sum dignus vocari apostolus, per respectum ad merita mea præcedentia, quoniam persecutus sum Ecclesiam Dei, viros ac mulieres ad judicium pertrahens: quod alii Apostoli nunquam fecerunt.
paras.en: [[15:8|And last of all|Novissime autem omnium]] those mentioned, namely after the Ascension and the sending of the Holy Ghost, [[15:8|as by one born out of due tine|tanquam abortivo]], [[15:8|he was seen also by me|visus est et mihi]] as I was journeying to Damascus[[Acts 9:3||]] [the margin gives Acts ix, 2–7]. Now that offspring is called *abortive* [Latin *abortivum*, a child born untimely; the Douay-Rheims renders it "one born out of due time"] which is born outside the due and fitting time, or is drawn out of the womb by violence, or does not reach its due size. So the Apostle compares himself to one born out of due time on three counts: first, because the other Apostles were reborn before the sending of the Paraclete, and he afterwards, by Ananias[[Acts 9:17||]]; secondly, because he was converted with a certain compulsion, namely through terror and threats; thirdly, because he was less than the other Apostles, in consideration of his past life, when he persecuted the Christians. So he adds: [[15:9|For I am the least of the apostles|Ego enim sum minimus Apostolorum]]: not simply, but in a certain respect, inasmuch as he was the last to be called to the apostolate. In this way James of Alpheus, the brother of the Lord, was called the Less[[Mark 15:40||]] with respect to James the son of Zebedee: not in holiness or dignity, but because he was later in being called. Again, I am the least of the Apostles by reason of past evils. [[15:9|who am not worthy to be called an apostle|Qui non sum dignus vocari apostolus]], in respect of my former merits, [[15:9|because I persecuted the church of God|quoniam persecutus sum Ecclesiam Dei]], dragging men and women to judgment[[Acts 8:3||]][[Acts 9:1||]]: which the other Apostles never did.

paras.t: Gratia autem Dei gratum faciente, et gratis data, non propriis viribus aut meritis, sum id quod sum in esse supernaturali et spirituali: per gratiam enim gratum facientem, habeo esse deiforme et Deo acceptum, quoad ultimum finem; per gratiam vero gratis datam, sum apostolus, propheta, doctor, interpres, signorum patrator. Et gratia ejus in me vacua, id est infructuosa, non fuit; sed abundantius illis omnibus laboravi, id est cunctis Apostolis, scilicet, quolibet eorum seorsum, non plus omnibus simul acceptis. Nullus enim Apostolorum tanta spatia percurrisse, tot populis prædicasse, tot persecutiones legitur pertulisse, ut Paulus; nec aliquis eorum sic propriis manibus victum quæsivit, ut ipse. Sed ne ista videatur jactanter dixisse, subjecit: Non autem ego sic laboravi propria potestate, vel tanquam principalis causa operum bonorum, sed gratia Dei mecum, scilicet, cooperata et auxiliata est mihi, fuitque principalior causa bonorum, quam ego seu mea natura. Gratia enim se habet ad liberum arbitrium, ut sessor ad equum.
paras.en: [[15:10|But by the grace of God|Gratia autem Dei]], both the grace that makes pleasing and the grace freely given [*gratia gratum faciens*, sanctifying grace, which makes a man pleasing to God, and *gratia gratis data*, a gift such as prophecy, given for the good of others], not by my own strength or merits, [[15:10|I am what I am|sum id quod sum]] in supernatural and spiritual being. For by the grace that makes pleasing I have a godlike being, acceptable to God, as regards the last end; and by the grace freely given I am an apostle, a prophet, a teacher, an interpreter, a worker of signs. [[15:10|And his grace in me hath not been void|Et gratia ejus in me vacua]], that is, fruitless, [[15:10|but I have laboured more abundantly than all they|sed abundantius illis omnibus laboravi]], that is, than all the Apostles: than any one of them taken singly, that is, not more than all of them taken together. For none of the Apostles is read to have travelled such distances, preached to so many peoples, endured so many persecutions as Paul; nor did any of them seek his living with his own hands as he did[[1 Cor 4:12||]]. But lest he seem to have said this boastfully, he added: [[15:10|Yet not I|Non autem ego]] laboured thus by my own power, or as the principal cause of the good works, [[15:10|but the grace of God with me|sed gratia Dei mecum]], that is, worked with me and helped me, and was a more principal cause of the good done than I or my nature. For grace stands to free will as the rider to the horse.

paras.t: Sive enim ego, sive illi, id est tam ego quam ceteri Apostoli, sic prædicavimus, videlicet Christum resurrexisse, vel nos per ejus gratiam operari, et sic credidistis sicut evangelizavimus vobis.
paras.en: [[15:11|For whether I or they|Sive enim ego, sive illi]], that is, both I and the other Apostles, [[15:11|so we preach|sic prædicavimus]], namely that Christ has risen, or that we work through his grace, [[15:11|and so you have believed|et sic credidistis]], as we preached the gospel to you.

paras.t: Præterea, ex resurrectione Christi capitis nostri, ostendit Apostolus generalem resurrectionem futuram. Si autem, id est Quia, Christus prædicatur a veris Apostolis quod resurrexit a mortuis: quomodo quidam hæretici dicunt in vobis, id est inter vos, quoniam resurrectio mortuorum corporalis et universalis non est credenda, neque futura? Si autem resurrectio mortuorum non est futura, sequitur quod neque Christus resurrexit. Eadem quippe ratio est de capite et de membris.
paras.en: Next, from the resurrection of Christ our head, the Apostle shows the general resurrection to come. [[15:12|Now if|Si autem]], that is, Since, [[15:12|Christ be preached|Christus prædicatur]] by the true Apostles, [[15:12|that he arose again from the dead|quod resurrexit a mortuis]], [[15:12|how do some|quomodo quidam]] heretics [[15:12|among you say|dicunt in vobis]], that is, in your midst, [[15:12|that there is no resurrection of the dead|quoniam resurrectio mortuorum corporalis et universalis non est]], bodily and universal, to be believed, and none to come? [[15:13|But if there be no resurrection of the dead|Si autem resurrectio mortuorum non est]] to come, it follows [[15:13|then Christ is not risen again|quod neque Christus resurrexit]]. For the reasoning is the same for the head and for the members.

paras.t: Si autem Christus non resurrexit veraciter, sed phantastice: sicut dixerunt hæretici, scilicet Marciani et Marcionitæ, qui Christi incarnationem dixerunt fuisse phantasticam, quos secutus est immundissimus Manichæus; inanis est ergo, id est, infructuosa, vana et falsa est, prædicatio nostra quæ asserit Christum resurrexisse. Simili ratione inanis est et fides vestra catholica. Inveniuntur autem, id est, si ita est ut dicunt hæretici, nos Apostoli esse probamur et summi testes fidei Dei, id est mendaciter testantes de Deo; quoniam testimonium dicimus adversus Deum, id est contra veritatem et voluntatem Dei, videlicet quod suscitaverit Christum a morte; quem non suscitavit, id est, quem sequitur non esse suscitatum a Deo, si mortui non resurgunt.
paras.en: [[15:14|And if Christ be not risen again|Si autem Christus non resurrexit]] truly, but only in appearance, as the heretics said, namely the Marcians and the Marcionites, who said that Christ's incarnation was a phantom, and whom the most unclean Manichæus followed: [[15:14|then is our preaching vain|inanis est ergo]], that is, fruitless, empty and false is [[15:14|our preaching|prædicatio nostra]], which asserts that Christ has risen. By the same reasoning [[15:14|your faith is also vain|inanis est et fides vestra]], your Catholic faith. [[15:15|Yea, and we are found|Inveniuntur autem]], that is, if it is as the heretics say, we Apostles are proved to be, and the chief ones, [[15:15|false witnesses of God|testes fidei Dei]] [the transcription reads *testes fidei Dei*, "witnesses of the faith of God"; the gloss that follows shows that the sense is *false witnesses*], that is, bearing lying witness about God; [[15:15|because we have given testimony against God|quoniam testimonium dicimus adversus Deum]], that is, against the truth and the will of God, namely [[15:15|that he hath raised up Christ|quod suscitaverit Christum]] from death, [[15:15|whom he hath not raised up|quem non suscitavit]], that is, who, it follows, was not raised up by God, [[15:15|if the dead rise not again|si mortui non resurgunt]].

paras.t: Nam si mortui non resurgunt, neque Christus resurrexit, qui ad hoc incarnatus et passus est, ideoque surrexit, ut nos ad immortalem vitam reduceret. Quod si Christus non resurrexit, vana est fides vestra, quia non potest vos ad ultimum finem seu veram felicitatem perducere; adhuc enim, scilicet post Baptismi ac fidei receptionem, estis in peccatis vestris præteritis, sicut et ante, secundum eos qui Christi resurrectionem non profitentur. Fides etenim vana, et Baptismus falsum repræsentans, non tollunt peccata. Baptismus autem, Christi sepulturam ac resurrectionem repræsentat, ut dictum est ad Romanos. Si ergo Christus non resurrexit, fides vestra inanis est, et Baptismus falsa significat. Non ergo tolluntur vestra peccata per fidem atque Baptismum. Ergo et qui dormierunt in Christo, id est, in fide Christi defuncti sunt, perierunt, id est, damnati sunt, eo quod in fide inani et pristinis vitiis sint defuncti.
