Let him put it, then, laying it up with himself as a gift, [[16:2|what it shall well please him|quod ei bene placuerit]], that is, as much as he gives willingly, so as not to be burdened; [[16:2|that when I come|ut non quum venero]], that is, when I am with you, [[16:2|the collections be not then to be made|tunc collectæ fiant]], that is, the alms be gathered: for then we shall have other things to see to; and it would also weigh on you if you gave it all at once.

paras.t: Quum autem præsens fuero apud vos : quos probaveritis, id est, approbaveritis, seu aptos judicaveritis, per epistolas hos mittam, id est, istos destinabo cum litteris commendatoriis meis ac vestris, perferre gratiam vestram, id est gratiosam eleemosynam, in Jerusalem ad primitivam Ecclesiam sub Jacobo militantem. Quod si dignum fuerit, id est, rationabilis causa occurrerit, ut et ego eam in Jerusalem cum eleemosynis istis, mecum ibunt quos probaveritis.
paras.en: [[16:3|And when I shall be with you|Quum autem præsens fuero apud vos]]: [[16:3|whomsoever you shall approve|quos probaveritis]], that is, approve of, or judge to be fit, [[16:3|by letters, them will I send|per epistolas hos mittam]], that is, I will dispatch them with letters of commendation, mine and yours, [[16:3|to carry your grace|perferre gratiam vestram]], that is, your gracious alms, [[16:3|to Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]], to the primitive Church militant under James. [[16:4|And if it be meet|Quod si dignum fuerit]], that is, if a reasonable cause arise, [[16:4|that I also go|ut et ego eam]] to Jerusalem with these alms, [[16:4|they shall go with me|mecum ibunt]], those whom you shall have approved.

paras.t: Veniam autem ad vos, quum Macedoniam (quæ est pars Græciæ) pertransiero, visitando illic et in locis vicinis discipulos. Nam Macedoniam provinciam illam pertransibo, non diu ibi morando, quum non sit necesse. Apud vos autem forsitan, scilicet si Deus præstiterit, permanebo multis diebus, vel etiam hiemabo : quia multa sunt corrigenda in vobis, ideo diuturna medici spiritualis præsentia vobis necessaria est ; ut vos me ducatis quocumque iero, quum a vobis recessero. Illa tamen non fuit principalis causa hujus mansionis ; sed hoc dicit Apostolus ad inflammandum caritatem eorum ad se, vel ad familiaritatem ostendendam.
paras.en: [[16:5|Now I will come to you|Veniam autem ad vos]], [[16:5|when I shall have passed through Macedonia|quum Macedoniam (quæ est pars Græciæ) pertransiero]] (which is a part of Greece), visiting the disciples there and in the places round about. [[16:5|For I shall pass through Macedonia|Nam Macedoniam provinciam illam pertransibo]], that province, not staying there long, since there is no need. [[16:6|And with you perhaps|Apud vos autem forsitan]], namely if God grant it, [[16:6|I shall abide|permanebo]] many days, [[16:6|or even spend the winter|vel etiam hiemabo]]: because there is much to be corrected in you, and so the lasting presence of the spiritual physician is necessary for you; [[16:6|that you may bring me on my way whithersoever I shall go|ut vos me ducatis quocumque iero]] [Denis's text reads *ducatis*, "lead"; a footnote in the edition gives *deducatis*, "bring on the way", as in the Vulgate], when I leave you. Yet that was not the chief reason for this stay; but the Apostle says this to kindle their love towards him, or to show his familiarity with them.

paras.t: Volo enim vos modo in transitu videre, id est tempore modico. [Spero enim me aliquantulum temporis manere apud vos, si Dominus permiserit.] Permanebo autem Ephesi, unde et istam epistolam vobis transmisi, usque ad Pentecosten. Ostium enim mihi apertum est magnum et evidens, id est, vehemens ratio mihi occurrit illic manendi, eo quod corda multorum parata sint recipere verbum Dei; et adversarii multi sunt ibi qui Evangelio contradicunt, contra quos oportet me armare fideles, vel illis quoque aperte resistere.
paras.en: For I wish to [[16:7|see you now by the way|vos modo in transitu videre]] [Denis's text reads *Volo*, "I will", where the Vulgate has *Nolo*, "I will not"], that is, for a short time; [[16:7|for I trust that I shall abide with you some time, if the Lord permit|Spero enim me aliquantulum temporis manere apud vos, si Dominus permiserit]] [these words are printed in square brackets: the editor has supplied the rest of the verse, which Denis passes over]. [[16:8|But I will tarry at Ephesus|Permanebo autem Ephesi]], whence also I have sent you this letter, [[16:8|until Pentecost|usque ad Pentecosten]]. [[16:9|For a great door and evident is opened unto me|Ostium enim mihi apertum est magnum et evidens]], that is, a strong reason for staying there presents itself to me, because the hearts of many are ready to receive the word of God; [[16:9|and many adversaries|et adversarii multi]] are there, who speak against the Gospel, against whom I must arm the faithful, or else openly resist them myself.

paras.t: Si autem venerit Timotheus ad vos, videte, id est, studete ad hoc, ut sine timore sit apud vos, id est secure, ita ut nullus ei molestus sit. Opus enim Domini operatur, prædicando Evangelium Christi, sicut et ego. Ne quis ergo illum spernat, eo quod juvenis sit. Unde alibi dicit : Nemo adolescentiam tuam contemnat. Deducite autem illum in pace, egrediendo et ambulando cum eo pacifice per aliquod spatium, ut veniat ad me Ephesum. Exspecto enim illum cum fratribus cum eo venturis. De Apollo autem fratre : qui erat vir potens in Scripturis et eloquens; quem Apostolus ordinavit Corinthiis in episcopum, sicut et ipsi rogaverunt; notum vobis facio, quoniam multum rogavi eum, non præcepi, ut veniret ad vos cum fratribus secum agentibus. Recesserat quippe a Corinthiis propter dissensionem eorum, quam sedare non potuit : propter quod redivit Ephesum ad Apostolum. Et utique non fuit voluntas ejus ut nunc veniret ad vos, quamdiu estis in ista discordia. Veniet autem quum ei vacuum, id est opportunum, fuerit, quando videlicet perceperit vos emendatos.
paras.en: [[16:10|Now if Timothy come|Si autem venerit Timotheus ad vos]], [[16:10|see|videte]], that is, take care of this, [[16:10|that he be with you without fear|ut sine timore sit apud vos]], that is, in safety, so that no one trouble him; [[16:10|for he worketh the work of the Lord|Opus enim Domini operatur]], by preaching the Gospel of Christ, [[16:10|as I also do|sicut et ego]]. [[16:11|Let no man therefore despise him|Ne quis ergo illum spernat]], because he is young. Hence he says elsewhere: [[1 Tim 4:12|Let no man despise thy youth|Nemo adolescentiam tuam contemnat]]. And [[16:11|conduct ye him on his way in peace|Deducite autem illum in pace]], going out and walking with him peaceably for some distance, [[16:11|that he may come to me|ut veniat ad me]] at Ephesus. [[16:11|For I look for him with the brethren|Exspecto enim illum cum fratribus]] who will come with him. [[16:12|And touching our brother Apollo|De Apollo autem fratre]], who was a man mighty in the Scriptures and eloquent, whom the Apostle ordained bishop for the Corinthians, as they themselves had asked: [[16:12|I give you to understand|notum vobis facio]], [[16:12|that I much entreated him|quoniam multum rogavi eum]], not commanded him, [[16:12|to come unto you with the brethren|ut veniret ad vos cum fratribus]] who are with him. For he had left the Corinthians because of their dissension, which he could not settle; for which reason he went back to Ephesus to the Apostle. [[16:12|and indeed it was not his will at all to come at this time|Et utique non fuit voluntas ejus ut nunc veniret ad vos]], as long as you are in this discord. [[16:12|But he will come when he shall have leisure|Veniet autem quum ei vacuum, id est opportunum, fuerit]], that is, when it is opportune for him: namely when he perceives that you have amended.

paras.t: Vigilate, id est, diligentes et solliciti estote, ne torpor pigritiæ irruat super vos; state, id est, firmiter perseverate, in fide; viriliter agite : maledictus enim qui facit opus Dei negligenter; confortamini, proficiendo semper in gratia Dei; omnia vestra opera in caritate fiant, id est caritative atque concorditer : aliter enim non essent meritoria.
paras.en: [[16:13|Watch ye|Vigilate]], that is, be diligent and careful, lest the torpor of sloth fall upon you; [[16:13|stand fast|state]], that is, persevere firmly, [[16:13|in the faith|in fide]]; [[16:13|do manfully|viriliter agite]]: for [[Jer 48:10|Cursed be he that doth the work of the Lord|maledictus enim qui facit opus Dei]] negligently [Denis quotes this in the form common in his day: the Vulgate has *opus Domini fraudulenter*, "the work of the Lord deceitfully"]; [[16:13|be strengthened|confortamini]], by ever advancing in the grace of God; [[16:14|Let all your things be done in charity|omnia vestra opera in caritate fiant]] [Denis reads *omnia vestra opera*, "all your works"], that is, charitably and in concord: for otherwise they would not be meritorious.

paras.t: Obsecro autem vos, fratres, nostis domum Stephanæ, id est familiam illius matronæ. Unde supra dixi : Baptizavi autem et Stephanæ domum. Nostis etiam et domum Fortunati et Achaici, id est horum virorum qui mecum fuerunt, quum vobis prædicavi; quoniam sunt primitiæ Achaiæ, id est, primi in Achaia crediderunt, et in ministerium sanctorum ordinaverunt se ipsos, id est, sponte se obtulerunt ad ministrandum fidelibus. Hoc itaque obsecro, ut et vos subditi sitis per humilem obedientiam, ejusmodi, id est istis et talibus personis, et omni cooperanti mihi et laboranti mecum in vobis, id est ad vestram salutem. Gaudeo autem in præsentia Stephanæ et Fortunati et Achaici, id est, de hoc lætor quod tales personæ vobiscum sunt; quoniam id quod vobis deerat, quantum ad salutarem doctrinam, ipsi suppleverunt, docendo vos plenius. Refecerunt enim, id est, spiritualiter nutrierunt seu impleverunt, et meum spiritum, id est animam meam jucunditate, eo quod instruant vos, et vestrum spiritum refecerunt veritatis notitia.
paras.en: [[16:15|And I beseech you, brethren|Obsecro autem vos, fratres]], [[16:15|you know the house of Stephanus|nostis domum Stephanæ]], that is, the family of that matron [Denis takes Stephanas for a woman]. Hence I said above: [[1 Cor 1:16|And I baptized also the household of Stephanus|Baptizavi autem et Stephanæ domum]]. You know also [[16:15|and of Fortunatus, and of Achaicus|et domum Fortunati et Achaici]], that is, of these men who were with me when I preached to you; [[16:15|that they are the firstfruits of Achaia|quoniam sunt primitiæ Achaiæ]], that is, they were the first in Achaia to believe, [[16:15|and have dedicated themselves to the ministry of the saints|et in ministerium sanctorum ordinaverunt se ipsos]], that is, they offered themselves of their own accord to serve the faithful. This, then, I beseech: [[16:16|That you also be subject|ut et vos subditi sitis]] by humble obedience [[16:16|to such|ejusmodi]], that is, to these and such persons, [[16:16|and to every one that worketh with us and laboureth|et omni cooperanti mihi et laboranti]] with me among you, that is, for your salvation. [[16:17|And I rejoice in the presence of Stephanus and Fortunatus and Achaicus|Gaudeo autem in præsentia Stephanæ et Fortunati et Achaici]], that is, I am glad of this, that such persons are with you; [[16:17|because that which was wanting on your part|quoniam id quod vobis deerat]], as regards saving doctrine, [[16:17|they have supplied|ipsi suppleverunt]], by teaching you more fully. [[16:18|For they have refreshed|Refecerunt enim]], that is, have spiritually nourished or filled, [[16:18|both my spirit|et meum spiritum]], that is, my soul, with gladness, because they instruct you, [[16:18|and yours|et vestrum]]: your spirit they have refreshed with the knowledge of the truth.

paras.t: Vel sic : Gaudeo autem in præsentia Stephanæ, etc., id est de hoc quod venerunt ad me : quoniam illud quod vobis deerat, id est quod vos minus debito mihi fecistis, ipsi suppleverunt. Refecerunt enim, id est, consolati sunt, vel paverunt, et meum spiritum et vestrum : quia mihi benefaciendo, benefecerunt et vobis, quibus Apostolum servaverunt. Cognoscite ergo, id est diligenter attendite et honorate, qui ejusmodi sunt, id est tales personas.
paras.en: Or thus: [[16:17|And I rejoice in the presence of Stephanus|Gaudeo autem in præsentia Stephanæ]], etc., that is, at this, that they have come to me: [[16:17|because that which was wanting on your part|quoniam illud quod vobis deerat]], that is, what you did for me less than you owed, [[16:17|they have supplied|ipsi suppleverunt]]. [[16:18|For they have refreshed|Refecerunt enim]], that is, have comforted or fed, [[16:18|both my spirit and yours|et meum spiritum et vestrum]]: for in doing good to me they did good to you also, for whom they preserved the Apostle. [[16:18|Know them, therefore|Cognoscite ergo]], that is, attend to them carefully and honour them, [[16:18|that are such|qui ejusmodi sunt]], that is, such persons.

paras.t: Salutant vos, id est, salutem vobis cupiunt atque annuntiant […] Asiæ minoris, cujus metropolis est Ephesus, ubi conscripta est præsens epistola. […] Salutant vos in Domino multum, id est cum ingenti affectu. […] Aquila […] ejus, […]clesia, id est cum societate fidelium commorante in domo eorum, apud quos et hospitor. Horum duorum frequenter Apostolus meminit, quia in primitiva Ecclesia notabiles erant, et bene instructi in fide.
paras.en: They [[16:19|salute you|Salutant vos]], that is, they wish you well and send you greeting […] of Asia Minor, whose chief city is Ephesus, where the present letter was written. […] [[16:19|salute you much in the Lord|Salutant vos in Domino multum]], that is, with great affection. […] [[16:19|Aquila|Aquila]] […] his, […] church, that is, with the company of the faithful dwelling in their house, [[16:19|with whom I also lodge|apud quos et hospitor]]. The Apostle often mentions these two, because they were notable in the primitive Church and well instructed in the faith.

paras.t: Salutant vos fratres omnes in Epheso exsistentes. Salutate invicem in osculo sancto, id est spirituali et puro, etiam corporali : sicut in primitiva Ecclesia fuerat consuetudo. Salutatio mea manu Pauli, id est propria manu subscripta. Scripsit enim Apostolus propria manu in fine epistolarum suarum salutationem, ne deciperentur fideles, recipiendo epistolas pseudoapostolorum pro epistolis Pauli.
paras.en: [[16:20|All the brethren salute you|Salutant vos fratres omnes]] who are at Ephesus. [[16:20|Salute one another with a holy kiss|Salutate invicem in osculo sancto]], that is, a spiritual and pure one, and a bodily one too, as the custom had been in the primitive Church. [[16:21|The salutation of me Paul, with my own hand|Salutatio mea manu Pauli]], that is, subscribed with my own hand. For the Apostle wrote the greeting with his own hand at the end of his letters, so that the faithful should not be deceived into receiving letters of false apostles as letters of Paul.

paras.t: Si quis non amat Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, sit anathema, id est separatus a consortio fidelium, et condemnatus a Deo, Maranatha, id est in adventu Domini, vel donec veniat Dominus. Maranatha quippe interpretatur, Dominus venit. Dicitque Lyra, quod sint duæ dictiones. Augustinus vero, cui potius creditur, ait quod sit unum nomen compositum ex Græco et Syro : et potius est Syrum quam Hebræum. Hæc autem imprecatio mali, non est intelligenda dicta de zelo ultionis seu invidiæ, sed affectu justitiæ, vel modo prænuntiationis propheticæ.
paras.en: [[16:22|If any man love not our Lord Jesus Christ, let him be anathema|Si quis non amat Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, sit anathema]], that is, separated from the fellowship of the faithful and condemned by God, [[16:22|maranatha|Maranatha]], that is, at the coming of the Lord, or until the Lord come. For *Maranatha* is interpreted "The Lord cometh" [*venit* can mean either "cometh" or "has come"]. And Lyra says that it is two words. But Augustine, who is rather to be believed, says that it is one word compounded of Greek and Syriac; and it is Syriac rather than Hebrew. Now this imprecation of evil is not to be understood as said out of zeal for vengeance or out of envy, but from a love of justice, or by way of prophetic foretelling.

paras.t: Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi vobiscum, quæ est formale ac habituale principium totius vitæ meritoriæ; sed et caritas mea, id est talis dilectio qualem ego habeo, sit cum omnibus vobis in Christo Jesu, id est finaliter propter Christum. Amen. Christus enim est finis noster, sicut in Apocalypsi testatur : Ego sum Alpha et Omega, principium et finis. Cui semper sit omnis honor, virtus, beatitudo et gloria, quoniam ipse cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[16:23|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi vobiscum]]: grace, which is the formal and habitual principle of the whole meritorious life [that is, what gives a life its merit, abiding in the soul as a habit]. And also: [[16:24|My charity|caritas mea]], that is, such love as I have, [[16:24|be with you all in Christ Jesus|sit cum omnibus vobis in Christo Jesu]], that is, for the sake of Christ as its end. [[16:24|Amen|Amen]]. For Christ is our end, as he testifies in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:8|I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end|Ego sum Alpha et Omega, principium et finis]] [the same words stand at Apoc 22:13]. To him be ever all honour, power, blessedness and glory, since he, with the Father and the Holy Ghost, is God most high and blessed above all. Amen.
